## Direct impacts

### Iran

Main article: [Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran](/wiki/Impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war_on_Iran "Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran")

#### Leadership

See also: [2026 Iranian supreme leader election](/wiki/2026_Iranian_supreme_leader_election "2026 Iranian supreme leader election")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_%28cropped%29.jpg/120px-Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_\(cropped\).jpg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_%28Cropped%29.jpg/120px-Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_%28Cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_\(Cropped\).jpg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg/120px-Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg)](/wiki/File:Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg)

The three members of the [Interim Leadership Council](/wiki/Interim_Leadership_Council "Interim Leadership Council") – President [Masoud Pezeshkian](/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian "Masoud Pezeshkian"), Chief Justice [Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i](/wiki/Gholam-Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i "Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i") and Ayatollah [Alireza Arafi](/wiki/Alireza_Arafi "Alireza Arafi")

The death of Ali Khamenei triggered an election for a new supreme leader. Under the terms of Iran's constitution, an [Interim Leadership Council](/wiki/Interim_Leadership_Council "Interim Leadership Council") was established on 1 March to exercise the functions of Iran's [head of state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") until a new supreme leader is elected.[\[236\]](#cite_note-Reuters-2026-267)

[Mojtaba Khamenei](/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei "Mojtaba Khamenei") was elected on 8 March 2026 to replace his father as supreme leader,[\[722\]](#cite_note-757) and the IRGC, as well as Iran's top leaders, including [Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf](/wiki/Mohammad_Bagher_Ghalibaf "Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf"), [Ali Larijani](/wiki/Ali_Larijani "Ali Larijani"), and [Masoud Pezeshkian](/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian "Masoud Pezeshkian"),[\[723\]](#cite_note-Sabah-2026-758) pledged their allegiance to him.[\[724\]](#cite_note-759)

In late March, the NYT described Iran's leadership as paralyzed with severely disrupted decision-making process. It also reported that the damage to communications infrastructure caused paranoia and internal power struggles.[\[725\]](#cite_note-760)

#### Civilian life

See also: [2025–2026 Iranian protests § After the strikes](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests#After_the_strikes "2025–2026 Iranian protests")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp/250px-Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp)

Residents in Tehran on the third day of US-Israeli airstrikes, 3 March 2026

According to UN Human Rights Chief [Volker Türk](/wiki/Volker_T%C3%BCrk "Volker Türk"), the "reckless" war is disproportionately impacting civilians in the Middle East and beyond.[\[726\]](#cite_note-761)

138,000 civilian sites in Iran were damaged during the conflict, with estimated time of reconstruction being 2 to 5 years.[\[727\]](#cite_note-762)

As the US and Israel executed joint strikes targeting Iranian military and institutional targets, Iran's capital reportedly became a [ghost town](/wiki/Ghost_town "Ghost town"), as civilians feared going outside or to their daily jobs.[\[728\]](#cite_note-763) Reports have emerged that prisoners in [Evin Prison](/wiki/Evin_Prison "Evin Prison") have been receiving limited bread and water since the onset of the war.[\[729\]](#cite_note-764) After the strikes, schools were ordered closed while banks and government offices remained in operation at reduced capacity. Local media reported that subway and bus services would remain operational.[\[730\]](#cite_note-765)

Amid the renewed "near total" [internet blackout in Iran](/wiki/2026_Internet_blackout_in_Iran "2026 Internet blackout in Iran"), [NetBlocks](/wiki/NetBlocks "NetBlocks") reported that internet connectivity in Iran dropped to 4% of ordinary levels.[\[625\]](#cite_note-BBC_News-2026b-659)[\[731\]](#cite_note-766)[\[732\]](#cite_note-767) While the internet blackout has exceeded 240 hours, making it the second longest ever, the government started handing out "white sim cards", which bypass filters, to government supporters, in order to allow them to promote its messaging.[\[733\]](#cite_note-768)[\[213\]](#cite_note-bm-241) As news of Khamenei's death broke, security forces were deployed to prevent an uprising, with footage showing them opening fire on celebrants in the streets[\[734\]](#cite_note-769)[\[735\]](#cite_note-770)[\[736\]](#cite_note-771) and shooting at people chanting behind the windows of their homes.[\[737\]](#cite_note-772)

During the first two weeks of March 2026, over 70,000 [Afghan refugees](/wiki/Afghans_in_Iran "Afghans in Iran") returned to Afghanistan, frequently under forced circumstances, exacerbating the country's [severe humanitarian crisis](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_hunger_crisis_in_Afghanistan "2025–2026 hunger crisis in Afghanistan").[\[738\]](#cite_note-773) Arafat Jamal, the UNHCR Representative in Afghanistan, noted that they faced limited options amid the [military confrontations between Afghanistan and Pakistan](/wiki/2026_Afghanistan%E2%80%93Pakistan_War "2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan War").[\[739\]](#cite_note-774)

According to *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*, the war has overshadowed the executions of political prisoners in Iran, including those involved in the mass protests of January 2026, allowing Iran to continue carrying out death sentences and other severe punishments with little international scrutiny.[\[740\]](#cite_note-775)

#### Military

On 26 March, it was reported that children as young as 12 years of age may join Iran's war support, leading to concerns of the use of [child soldiers](/wiki/Child_soldiers "Child soldiers").[\[741\]](#cite_note-776)[\[742\]](#cite_note-777)[\[743\]](#cite_note-778) Days later, rights groups stated an 11-year-old was killed while on duty at a Tehran checkpoint.[\[744\]](#cite_note-779)

On 29 March, footage showed Iraq's [Popular Mobilization Forces](/wiki/Popular_Mobilization_Forces "Popular Mobilization Forces") deployed in Iran.[\[745\]](#cite_note-780)[\[746\]](#cite_note-781)[\[490\]](#cite_note-iranintl28march-523)

#### Kurdish–Iranian crisis

Further information: [2026 Kurdish–Iranian crisis](/wiki/2026_Kurdish%E2%80%93Iranian_crisis "2026 Kurdish–Iranian crisis")

According to *[The Wall Street Journal](/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")*, Trump had been open to supporting armed militias, particularly [Kurds in Iran](/wiki/Kurds_in_Iran "Kurds in Iran") that have been [in armed conflict with Tehran for decades](/wiki/Kurdish_separatism_in_Iran "Kurdish separatism in Iran")[\[298\]](#cite_note-wsj3march-329) and have historically been a regional ally of the United States.[\[747\]](#cite_note-782) However, Trump later said he had ruled out sending the Kurds to Iran.[\[748\]](#cite_note-783)

#### Cultural heritage sites

Main article: [Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran War](/wiki/Destruction_of_cultural_heritage_sites_during_the_2026_Iran_War "Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran War")

Multiple historic and cultural sites, including [UNESCO World Heritage Sites](/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Sites "UNESCO World Heritage Sites"), were damaged during the war. The most affected was [Chehel Sotoun](/wiki/Chehel_Sotoun "Chehel Sotoun") and its rich *[ayeneh-kari](/wiki/Ayeneh-kari "Ayeneh-kari")*.[\[749\]](#cite_note-784) On 2 March, a strike on [Arg Square](/wiki/Arg_Square "Arg Square") damaged nearby [Golestan Palace](/wiki/Golestan_Palace "Golestan Palace"), prompting [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") to issue a statement of concern.[\[750\]](#cite_note-785)[\[751\]](#cite_note-786) On 5 March, the [Azadi Sport Complex](/wiki/Azadi_Sport_Complex "Azadi Sport Complex") was bombed.[\[752\]](#cite_note-787) An 8 March strike on [Falak-ol-Aflak](/wiki/Falak-ol-Aflak "Falak-ol-Aflak"), which was marked with a [blue shield emblem](/wiki/Hague_Convention_for_the_Protection_of_Cultural_Property_in_the_Event_of_Armed_Conflict "Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict"), damaged several sections of the site.[\[753\]](#cite_note-ArtNewspaper310-788) Strikes on [Isfahan](/wiki/Isfahan "Isfahan") on 9 March damaged [Naqsh-e Jahan Square](/wiki/Naqsh-e_Jahan_Square "Naqsh-e Jahan Square"), Chehel Sotoun, [Ali Qapu](/wiki/Ali_Qapu "Ali Qapu"), the [Shah Mosque](/wiki/Shah_Mosque_\(Isfahan\) "Shah Mosque (Isfahan)"), [Jameh Mosque](/wiki/Jameh_Mosque_of_Isfahan "Jameh Mosque of Isfahan"), and [Teymouri Hall](/wiki/Natural_History_Museum_of_Isfahan "Natural History Museum of Isfahan").[\[754\]](#cite_note-789)[\[753\]](#cite_note-ArtNewspaper310-788) On 11 March, UNESCO urged protection for Iran's [heritage sites](/wiki/Heritage_sites "Heritage sites") and World Heritage Sites that have been damaged or are under high risk due to the war, alongside other [historic sites](/wiki/Historic_site "Historic site") in Israel, Lebanon, and across the Middle East.[\[755\]](#cite_note-790)

### Israel

Israel declared a nationwide [state of emergency](/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency"), saying that the strikes on Iran were the largest that it had ever launched.[\[216\]](#cite_note-Liebermann-2026-244)[\[756\]](#cite_note-791) Israeli schools and workspaces were closed and public gatherings were canceled.[\[757\]](#cite_note-792)

In the 40 days from the start of the war through the [8 April ceasefire](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire"), there were a total of 650 missile attacks from Iran to Israel, the majority of which carried cluster munitions. About 16 of the missiles that made it past Israeli missile defenses carried conventional warheads, while 50 had cluster munitions. The attacks killed a total of 24 people, all of them civilians, and resulted in more than 7,000 injuries. Of the 24 civilians killed, 14 were struck by warheads with conventional explosive warheads and 10 were victims of cluster submunitions; two of the deaths were inside a sheltered space, with the other fatalities being people in unprotected areas.[\[758\]](#cite_note-793)

### Palestine

See also: [Gaza war](/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war")

The Israeli [Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories](/wiki/Coordinator_of_Government_Activities_in_the_Territories "Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories") closed multiple aid crossings in the [Gaza Strip](/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip"), specifically interrupting free circulation on the [Egypt–Gaza border](/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Gaza_border "Egypt–Gaza border").[\[759\]](#cite_note-794) Israeli forces suspended [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") humanitarian movements and postponed planned rotations of international humanitarian staff, including medical evacuations and the return of people into Gaza, which the [United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs](/wiki/United_Nations_Office_for_the_Coordination_of_Humanitarian_Affairs "United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs") condemned.[\[760\]](#cite_note-795)

[Israeli settler violence](/wiki/Israeli_settler_violence "Israeli settler violence") against [Palestinians](/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") in [occupied West Bank](/wiki/Occupied_West_Bank "Occupied West Bank") has increased; settlers have taken advantage of curbs on movement imposed during the renewed [Israeli state of emergency](/wiki/Israeli_state_of_emergency "Israeli state of emergency"). The renewed blocking of West Bank roads in the context of the [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war") has delayed medics from assisting injured Palestinians.[\[761\]](#cite_note-796) The EU stated on 10 March that the Israeli actions were unacceptable and urged the Israeli authorities to make immediate efforts to prevent the violence against Palestinian civilians under [international law](/wiki/International_law "International law"), warning that "impunity for such acts risks provoking further violence".[\[762\]](#cite_note-797)

This section is an excerpt from [2026 Lebanon war § Casualties](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war#Casualties "2026 Lebanon war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Lebanon_war&action=edit)\]

As of 1 May, at least 2,618 people have been killed and 8,094 wounded by Israeli strikes in Lebanon during the 2026 Lebanon war.[\[763\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_Lebanon1-798) Internal [Hezbollah](/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah") sources said that over 1,000 Hezbollah fighters had been killed in the war[\[764\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_Hezbollah1-799) while the [Israel Defense Forces](/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces "Israel Defense Forces") (IDF) said that it had killed 1,700 fighters.[\[765\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_Hezbollah2-800)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Tyre_Funeral_21_April.jpg/250px-Tyre_Funeral_21_April.jpg)](/wiki/File:Tyre_Funeral_21_April.jpg)

Funerary procession in Tyre for a deceased Hezbollah fighter, 21 April 2026

This section is an excerpt from [2026 Lebanon war § Displacement](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war#Displacement "2026 Lebanon war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Lebanon_war&action=edit)\]

According to Lebanon, over 1.2 million Lebanese nationals,[\[766\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_displaced-801) corresponding to more than one-sixth of the country's population,[\[767\]](#cite_note-802) were displaced.[\[768\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_Kelliher-803)[\[769\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_AP_News-804) Over 40,000 homes in southern Lebanon have been destroyed.[\[770\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_NPR-14042026-805) Israel's evacuation orders in Lebanon covered an area of over 1,470 square kilometres (570 sq mi), encompassing 14% of the country's territory. The displacement in Lebanon has been called one of the most severe and fastest-growing refugee crises worldwide.[\[766\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_displaced-801) The war exacerbated the economic and humanitarian problems that have been ongoing in Lebanon since the [2019 financial crisis](/wiki/Lebanese_liquidity_crisis "Lebanese liquidity crisis") and [2020 Beirut explosion](/wiki/2020_Beirut_explosion "2020 Beirut explosion").[\[771\]](#cite_note-2026_Lebanon_war_ForeignPolicy-03042026-806)

### Gulf Arab states

The [Arab states of the Persian Gulf](/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf") started a campaign of prosecution against civilians and foreign citizens that shared or reposted rumours from unverified sources about the Iranian attacks, with the stated main goal to curb misinformation that could harm public order.[\[772\]](#cite_note-807) Bahrain's Cyber Crime Directorate also started a campaign of arresting civilians in the country, which has a large [Shiite minority](/wiki/Shia_in_Bahrain "Shia in Bahrain"), who allegedly expressed "their support for the Iranian shelling targeting the Kingdom of Bahrain", describing such activities as treason and as promotion of hostile acts against the state.[\[773\]](#cite_note-808) Trump said "Even if we knew Gulf countries would be hit, big deal we did what we have to do".[\[774\]](#cite_note-UrasEtAl-809)

## Economic impacts

Main articles: [Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war"), [2026 Iran war regional mobilizations](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_regional_mobilizations "2026 Iran war regional mobilizations"), and [Evacuations during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Evacuations_during_the_2026_Iran_war "Evacuations during the 2026 Iran war")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/20260309_DM_MiddleEast_Repatriations%281%29.pdf/page1-250px-20260309_DM_MiddleEast_Repatriations%281%29.pdf.jpg)](/wiki/File:20260309_DM_MiddleEast_Repatriations\(1\).pdf)

A map of emergency evacuation of persons to Europe

The war had global economic consequences: [oil](/wiki/Price_of_oil "Price of oil") and [gas prices](/wiki/Natural_gas_prices "Natural gas prices") surged, aviation and tourism were disrupted, and financial markets shuddered.[\[775\]](#cite_note-810)[\[776\]](#cite_note-811) [International Energy Agency](/wiki/International_Energy_Agency "International Energy Agency") (IEA) head [Fatih Birol](/wiki/Fatih_Birol "Fatih Birol") described the situation as the "greatest global energy security challenge in history".[\[777\]](#cite_note-812)

### Energy

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/2021-_Retail_price_of_gasoline_%28US%29.svg/250px-2021-_Retail_price_of_gasoline_%28US%29.svg.png)](/wiki/File:2021-_Retail_price_of_gasoline_\(US\).svg)

The retail price of gasoline in the US increased at the outbreak of war in Ukraine and Iran.[\[778\]](#cite_note-NYTimes_20260420-813)

Oil and natural gas prices rose in direct response to Iranian threats to attack tankers and other ships and to Iranian strikes on oil facilities in Gulf producing countries.[\[779\]](#cite_note-814) 20% of global oil and gas production normally transit the Strait of Hormuz.[\[780\]](#cite_note-Buchanan-2026-815) As the war continued, oil and gas prices ebbed and flowed as markets attempted to assess the likelihood of an end to the conflict. Prices ranged from below $70 before the war[\[781\]](#cite_note-816) to as high as $139 on 7 March.[\[782\]](#cite_note-817) Gas prices also rose.[\[259\]](#cite_note-bloomberg4march-290)

Toward the end of March significant shortages of domestic [petroleum products](/wiki/Petroleum_product "Petroleum product") emerged in [southeast Asia](/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") as reserves ran out.[\[783\]](#cite_note-bbc-20260324-818)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/USS_Bainbridge_%28DDG_96%29_transits_the_Suez_Canal_during_Operation_Epic_Fury_%289552415%29.jpg/250px-USS_Bainbridge_%28DDG_96%29_transits_the_Suez_Canal_during_Operation_Epic_Fury_%289552415%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:USS_Bainbridge_\(DDG_96\)_transits_the_Suez_Canal_during_Operation_Epic_Fury_\(9552415\).jpg)

The guided-missile destroyer [USS *Bainbridge*](/wiki/USS_Bainbridge_\(DDG-96\) "USS Bainbridge (DDG-96)") passes through the [Suez Canal](/wiki/Suez_Canal "Suez Canal") during Operation Epic Fury, March 2026

Stock markets initially fell, with the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average "Dow Jones Industrial Average") falling over 400 points (one percent) on 2 March alone,[\[784\]](#cite_note-819) although by mid-April had recovered and reached record highs.[\[785\]](#cite_note-820)

The UN [World Food Programme](/wiki/World_Food_Programme "World Food Programme") and various economic analysts warned that the war is driving significant, long-term increases in global [food prices](/wiki/Food_prices "Food prices").[\[786\]](#cite_note-821)[\[787\]](#cite_note-822)

### Commodities

Disruption in the supply of essential [fertilizers](/wiki/Fertilizer "Fertilizer") due to the closure of the Strait threatened food production in many countries.[\[788\]](#cite_note-823) The Fertilizer Institute stated that nearly 50% of global [urea](/wiki/Urea "Urea") and [sulfur](/wiki/Sulfur "Sulfur") exports annually transited through the Strait of Hormuz, made worse by the natural gas shortage, which is a key feedstock for [nitrogen fertilizers](/wiki/Nitrogen_fertilizer "Nitrogen fertilizer").[\[780\]](#cite_note-Buchanan-2026-815)

### Air travel

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Grounded_airliners_at_Manchester_Airport_Feb_2026.jpg/250px-Grounded_airliners_at_Manchester_Airport_Feb_2026.jpg)](/wiki/File:Grounded_airliners_at_Manchester_Airport_Feb_2026.jpg)

Airliners of [Qatar Airways](/wiki/Qatar_Airways "Qatar Airways"), [Kuwait Airways](/wiki/Kuwait_Airways "Kuwait Airways") and [Emirates](/wiki/Emirates_\(airline\) "Emirates (airline)") grounded at [Manchester Airport](/wiki/Manchester_Airport "Manchester Airport"), 28 February 2026.

Iran's airspace emptied of civilian aircraft during the conflict,[\[789\]](#cite_note-824) as Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, Syria and the UAE closed their respective airspaces.[\[790\]](#cite_note-825)[\[791\]](#cite_note-826)[\[792\]](#cite_note-827) Some carriers suspended service to the Middle East.[\[793\]](#cite_note-828)

[Spirit Airlines](/wiki/Spirit_Airlines "Spirit Airlines"), an American [low-cost airline](/wiki/Low-cost_airline "Low-cost airline"), ceased operations on 2 May 2026, after increased fuel costs from the war exacerbated its existing financial difficulties.[\[794\]](#cite_note-829)

### Strait of Hormuz

This section is an excerpt from [2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis&action=edit)\]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Hormuz_map.png/250px-Hormuz_map.png)](/wiki/File:Hormuz_map.png)

The [Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz "Strait of Hormuz") highlighted by a red box, at the entrance to the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf")

[Shipping traffic](/wiki/Maritime_transport "Maritime transport") through the [Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz "Strait of Hormuz"), a major maritime [choke point](/wiki/Choke_point "Choke point") for world [energy trade](/wiki/Commodity_market#Energy "Commodity market"), has been largely blocked by [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") since 28 February 2026, when the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Israel](/wiki/Israel "Israel") launched an air war against Iran and [assassinated its supreme leader](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei"), [Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Ali_Khamenei "Ali Khamenei"). In retaliation, Iran launched missile and drone attacks on Israel, US military bases, and US-allied [Gulf states](/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf"). The [Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps](/wiki/Iranian_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps "Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps") (IRGC) issued warnings forbidding passage through the strait, boarded and attacked merchant ships, and laid [sea mines](/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine") in the strait. Since 13 April, the US has simultaneously [blockaded Iranian ports](/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran"). Until the US–Israeli war against Iran, the Strait of Hormuz was open and about 25% of the world's seaborne [oil trade](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_oil_exports "List of countries by oil exports") and 20% of the world's [liquefied natural gas](/wiki/Liquefied_natural_gas "Liquefied natural gas") passed through it.

The Iranian warnings and subsequent attacks on vessels prompted shipping firms to suspend operations in the strait.[\[795\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_How_US-830)[\[796\]](#cite_note-831) This caused a sharp decline in maritime transit, with [tanker](/wiki/Tanker_\(ship\) "Tanker (ship)") traffic dropping first by about 70% and over 150 ships anchoring outside the strait to avoid risks.[\[797\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_NYT2.28.26-832)[\[798\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_TheGuardian3.2.26-833)\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] Soon afterwards traffic dropped to about zero. On 27 March, the IRGC announced that the strait was closed to any vessel going "to and from" the ports of the US, Israel, and their allies.[\[799\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_AFP-03272026-834) The [International Maritime Organization](/wiki/International_Maritime_Organization "International Maritime Organization") reported on 21 April that about 20,000 mariners and 2,000 ships were stranded in the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf") due to the closure.[\[800\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_AJ-21042026-835) According to Majid Rafizadeh, Iran is violating the [United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea](/wiki/United_Nations_Convention_on_the_Law_of_the_Sea "United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea"), which it has not ratified.[\[801\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_UNCLOS1-836)[\[802\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_UNCLOS2-837)

Amid fears of prolonged supply shortages, oil prices rose faster than during any other conflict in recent history;[\[803\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_AC-03182026-838) [Brent crude oil](/wiki/Brent_Crude "Brent Crude") prices surpassed US$100 per [barrel](/wiki/Barrel_\(unit\) "Barrel (unit)") on 8 March for the first time in four years, rising to US$126 per barrel at their peak.[\[798\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_TheGuardian3.2.26-833)[\[804\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_Reuters3.1.26-839)[\[805\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_surges-840)[\[806\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_CNBC-03082026-841) The largest-ever monthly increase in oil prices occurred in March 2026.[\[807\]](#cite_note-842)\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] The closure of the strait has been the largest disruption to world energy supply since the [1970s energy crisis](/wiki/1970s_energy_crisis "1970s energy crisis")[\[808\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_Guardian-03112026-843) as well as the largest in the history of the world oil market.[\[809\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_Atlantic-13032026-844) Other commodity markets to suffer supply disruption and price increases due to the crisis include aluminum,[\[810\]](#cite_note-845) fertilizer,[\[811\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_AC-27032026-846) and helium.[\[812\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_Axios-07042026-847)[\[813\]](#cite_note-848)

On 9 March, [US president Donald Trump falsely claimed that Iran's](/wiki/False_or_misleading_statements_by_Donald_Trump_\(second_term\)#Claims_about_Iran "False or misleading statements by Donald Trump (second term)")\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] military had been destroyed and that the strait was open, saying that the US might seize control of it from Iran.[\[814\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_CBSNews3.16.26-849) On 15 March, he called on [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") members and China to help to reopen the strait.[\[815\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_TheGuardian3.16.26-850) In late March and early April, Trump repeatedly threatened to destroy Iran's infrastructure if it did not reopen the strait.[\[816\]](#cite_note-851) On 8 April, [a temporary ceasefire](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire") between Iran and the US was agreed and was to involve the reopening of the strait. However, Iran began controlling traffic through the strait and charging tolls of over $1 million per ship.[\[817\]](#cite_note-852)\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] Following the failure of the [Islamabad Talks](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks"), the [US Navy](/wiki/US_Navy "US Navy") itself began to blockade Iranian ports from 13 April.[\[818\]](#cite_note-853)[\[819\]](#cite_note-854) The situation was described by *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* as a "dual blockade", with the US Navy blockading Iran and Iran blockading the Gulf.[\[820\]](#cite_note-2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis_Guardian_24_Apr_26-855)\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

On 17 April, due to [an Israel–Lebanon ceasefire agreement](/wiki/2026_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire "2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire"), Iran announced that the Strait of Hormuz would be open to commercial shipping during the truce. Despite this, the US continued its blockade of Iran,[\[821\]](#cite_note-856) and Iran reimposed restrictions as a result.[\[822\]](#cite_note-857)[\[823\]](#cite_note-858)[\[824\]](#cite_note-859) On 4 May, Trump launched [Operation Project Freedom](/wiki/Operation_Project_Freedom "Operation Project Freedom"), a US Navy mission to escort merchant ships out of the Gulf. The Iranian military warned that this would be a ceasefire violation.[\[825\]](#cite_note-860)\[*[not verified in body](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] On 6 May, President Trump announced a temporary pause in the US military's "Project Freedom" operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, indicating "great progress" toward a possible agreement with Iran. The operation will be delayed briefly to assess the potential for a "complete and final agreement" with Iran.[\[826\]](#cite_note-861)

### Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb

See also: [Red Sea crisis](/wiki/Red_Sea_crisis "Red Sea crisis")

[Houthi-controlled Yemen](/wiki/Houthi-controlled_Yemen "Houthi-controlled Yemen") threatened shipping in the [Gulf of Aden](/wiki/Gulf_of_Aden "Gulf of Aden") and [Red Sea](/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea"). Its threats had been suspended since 10 October 2025.[\[827\]](#cite_note-862) March threats by [Houthi](/wiki/Houthis "Houthis") leader [Abdul-Malik al-Houthi](/wiki/Abdul-Malik_al-Houthi "Abdul-Malik al-Houthi") had not stopped Red Sea traffic as of mid-April, although traffic remained under historic levels after crashing in 2024 as a result of Houthi attacks.[\[828\]](#cite_note-863) On 15 March, the *[Associated Press](/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press")* reported that the weapons stockpile of the Houthis was running low from repeated attacks on Israel, while Iran had not been able to resupply them, because of the war.[\[829\]](#cite_note-864)[\[830\]](#cite_note-865)

### Internet infrastructure

Further information: [Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Cyberwarfare_during_the_2026_Iran_war "Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war")

Three [Amazon Web Services](/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services") data centers in the United Arab Emirates were struck and damaged as a result of [drone strikes](/wiki/Drone_strikes "Drone strikes"), leading to outages of web infrastructure within the Middle East,[\[831\]](#cite_note-866) causing "sparks and fire" as well as "major structural damage" for 2 of the centers, with internal water levels reaching up to 4 cm, worsened by the failure of cooling and air systems. Fundamental web infrastructure including [S3 storage](/wiki/Amazon_S3 "Amazon S3"), [EC2 compute](/wiki/Amazon_Elastic_Compute_Cloud "Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud") and [DynamoDB databases](/wiki/Amazon_DynamoDB "Amazon DynamoDB") suffered complete outages in early March.[\[832\]](#cite_note-867) Iran shut down Internet access for its people throughout the war.[\[833\]](#cite_note-868) Users who took the potentially fatal risk of smuggling [Starlink](/wiki/Starlink "Starlink") terminals into the country [retained some access](/wiki/2026_Internet_blackout_in_Iran "2026 Internet blackout in Iran").

### Military costs

US military costs were estimated at $25-35 billion as of early April.[\[834\]](#cite_note-869) Israeli costs were estimated at $11 billion.[\[835\]](#cite_note-870) Costs to the Iranian economy were estimated at $40-50 billion, around 10% of [GDP](/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product").[\[836\]](#cite_note-871) The monetary costs of Iranian attacks were much lower than the costs of neutralizing them: PATRIOT and THAAD interceptors are $4 million and $12 million, respectively, as opposed to $50,000 for a Shahed drone.[\[372\]](#cite_note-ndtv10march-404)

## Reactions

Further information: [Reactions to the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war "Reactions to the 2026 Iran war") and [Protests against the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Protests_against_the_2026_Iran_war "Protests against the 2026 Iran war")

### Iran

This section is an excerpt from [Reactions to the 2026 Iran war § Government](/wiki/Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war#Government "Reactions to the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

Iran's Foreign Ministry vowed a response as Iranian forces struck US bases across the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf").[\[837\]](#cite_note-872)[\[838\]](#cite_note-873) The [Supreme National Security Council](/wiki/Supreme_National_Security_Council "Supreme National Security Council") said Iran was targeted by a "brutal air operation" carried out by the US and Israel, saying: "This occurred once again during negotiations, and the enemy imagines that the resilient Iranian nation will surrender to their petty demands through these cowardly actions."[\[839\]](#cite_note-874) Iranian foreign minister [Abbas Araghchi](/wiki/Abbas_Araghchi "Abbas Araghchi") called the attacks "wholly unprovoked, illegal, and illegitimate" and said attacks by Iran will continue until as long as they are defending.[\[840\]](#cite_note-875)[\[841\]](#cite_note-876) Vice President Aref stated that the path to social justice will not be resisted or stopped by any missile attack.[\[842\]](#cite_note-877) Iranian president [Masoud Pezeshkian](/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian "Masoud Pezeshkian") said that if the US and Israel are not held accountable for their actions "global order will be shaken".[\[843\]](#cite_note-878) Pezeshkian said that US should take their unconditional surrender demand "to their grave".[\[844\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_The_Indian_Express-2026-879) He initially apologized for the attacks on neighboring nations, blaming "miscommunication in the ranks".[\[844\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_The_Indian_Express-2026-879)[\[845\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera-2-880) Later he said that Iran had to target countries whose territory was used to attack Iran.[\[846\]](#cite_note-881) Iranian officials rejected Trump's attempt to insert himself into the [government's succession plans](/wiki/2026_Iranian_supreme_leader_election "2026 Iranian supreme leader election").[\[847\]](#cite_note-882)

On 19 March, Iranian [Foreign Ministry spokesperson](/wiki/Spokesperson_for_the_Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_of_Iran "Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran") [Esmail Baghaei](/wiki/Esmail_Baghaei "Esmail Baghaei") accused the US and Israel of "terrorist acts" over the deaths of top figures, calling the attacks an "illegal war". He said that Australia's military assets were legitimate targets, over the deployment of a [surveillance aircraft](/wiki/Surveillance_aircraft "Surveillance aircraft") along with personnel to the UAE.[\[848\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_abcint-883)[\[849\]](#cite_note-884) On 20 March, [Abolfazl Shekarchi](/wiki/Abolfazl_Shekarchi "Abolfazl Shekarchi") warned US and Israeli personnel that Iran was tracking the movements of "officials, commanders, and pilots" beyond active conflict zones and warned that public and recreational locations would no longer be safe for them.[\[850\]](#cite_note-885) Iran denied targeting Azerbaijan, Turkey and Oman, blaming "Israeli [false flag](/wiki/False_flag "False flag")" attacks.[\[851\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Khalilova-2026-886)[\[852\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Khamenei-887)

Vice president [Mohammad Reza Aref](/wiki/Mohammad_Reza_Aref "Mohammad Reza Aref") described the alleged use of a [bunker-buster bomb](/wiki/Bunker-buster_bomb "Bunker-buster bomb") in an attack on the university as a "symbol of Trump’s madness and ignorance".[\[853\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_aljazeera6april-888) Deputy foreign minister [Kazem Gharibabadi](/wiki/Kazem_Gharibabadi "Kazem Gharibabadi") condemned what he called the repeated [targeting of historical and cultural sites in Iran](#Cultural_heritage_sites) as "an assault on part of Iran's civilizational identity".[\[854\]](#cite_note-889) Araghchi labeled the [strike on a Tehran fuel depot](/wiki/Black_rain#Notable_incidences "Black rain") as "ecocide".[\[855\]](#cite_note-890) The Iranian government declared it had lifted import/export rules and restrictions,[\[856\]](#cite_note-891) and announced that fuel and medicine were readily available.[\[857\]](#cite_note-892) The [national post](/wiki/National_Post_Company_of_the_Islamic_Republic_of_Iran "National Post Company of the Islamic Republic of Iran") temporarily paused parcel delivery.[\[858\]](#cite_note-893) All sporting events were canceled. Iranian [hajj](/wiki/Hajj "Hajj") pilgrims returned by land.[\[859\]](#cite_note-894)

#### Media coverage

##### Background

Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and [domestic unrest in Iran](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests "2025–2026 Iranian protests"). Iranian state media, such as the [IRNA](/wiki/IRNA "IRNA"), portrayed these developments as provocations.[\[860\]](#cite_note-Brookings_Institute-03032026-895)

##### Disinformation and propaganda

[](/wiki/File:Explosive_Media_L_O_S_E_R.webm "Play video")Duration: 2 minutes and 41 seconds.2:41[](/wiki/File:Explosive_Media_L_O_S_E_R.webm)

[Lego](/wiki/Lego "Lego")\-style [propaganda](/wiki/Propaganda "Propaganda") animation produced by Iranian media company [Explosive Media](/wiki/Explosive_Media "Explosive Media") using [text-to-video modeling](/wiki/Text-to-video_model "Text-to-video model").

Iranian state-controlled outlets have been described as employing propaganda techniques, including the use of [AI-generated videos](/wiki/AI-generated_video "AI-generated video") (such as those produced by [Explosive Media](/wiki/Explosive_Media "Explosive Media")) and inflated casualty figures.[\[861\]](#cite_note-896) Trump has accused Iran of using artificial intelligence as a "disinformation weapon."[\[862\]](#cite_note-897) Iranian media broadcast manipulated images of alleged victories, prompting fact-checking from organizations like [NewsGuard](/wiki/NewsGuard "NewsGuard").[\[863\]](#cite_note-CNN-05032026-898) The Iranian government responded to the [Trump administration](/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump")'s use of video game clips, cartoon characters, and blockbuster movie scenes for Iran messaging with an AI-generated [propaganda video](/wiki/Propaganda_video "Propaganda video") mimicking [Lego animation](/wiki/Brickfilm "Brickfilm"), produced by the Revayat-e-Fath Institute and redistributed on various government-run outlets, including redistribution by the [Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs](/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_\(Iran\) "Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)"). The video declares itself in remembrance of the [Minab school attack](/wiki/Minab_school_attack "Minab school attack") and showcases Iran attacking various of its neighbours and American-Israeli outposts.[\[864\]](#cite_note-899)[\[865\]](#cite_note-900)

Rumors that Israeli Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") had been killed in Iranian attacks were circulating widely on social media and were amplified by Iranian state-controlled outlets.[\[866\]](#cite_note-i24NEWS-16032026-901)[\[867\]](#cite_note-CTV_News-15032026-902) Users claimed that footage of Netanyahu speaking at a press conference on 13 March 2026 was AI-generated, citing alleged anomalies such as a “sixth finger.”[\[868\]](#cite_note-903)

##### Impact

Coverage of the war strained journalistic resources, with reports of targeted attacks on media infrastructure.[\[869\]](#cite_note-904)

### Israel

This section is an excerpt from [Reactions to the 2026 Iran war § Israel](/wiki/Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war#Israel "Reactions to the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Tel_Aviv_120326_Dizengoff_02.jpg/250px-Tel_Aviv_120326_Dizengoff_02.jpg)](/wiki/File:Tel_Aviv_120326_Dizengoff_02.jpg)

Israelis pay tribute to US troops at a memorial in [Dizengoff Square](/wiki/Dizengoff_Square "Dizengoff Square"), Tel Aviv, following the 1 March 2026 drone strike in Kuwait

Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") said the goal of the strikes was to "remove the existential threat posed by the terrorist regime in Iran", stating that "our joint action will create the conditions for the brave Iranian people to take their destiny into their own hands."[\[870\]](#cite_note-905) Foreign minister [Gideon Sa'ar](/wiki/Gideon_Sa%27ar "Gideon Sa'ar") said that military action against Iran was urgently needed "despite the significant risks involved", adding that "delay would have allowed the Iranian regime to reach a level of immunity for its nuclear programme, as well as to engage in the mass production of long-range ballistic missiles".[\[871\]](#cite_note-906) Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") was the first to report and celebrate the assassination, stating "for 47 years, the Ayatollah regime has chanted '[Death to Israel](/wiki/Death_to_Israel "Death to Israel")' and '[Death to America](/wiki/Death_to_America "Death to America").' It has spilled our blood, murdered many Americans, and slaughtered its own people."[\[872\]](#cite_note-907) Defense Minister [Israel Katz](/wiki/Israel_Katz "Israel Katz") celebrated the killing, stating "he who acted to destroy Israel – has been destroyed ... Justice has been served, and the [axis of evil](/wiki/Axis_of_evil "Axis of evil") has suffered a mortal blow."[\[873\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Jazeera2-908) On 29 March, [Yuli Edelstein](/wiki/Yuli_Edelstein "Yuli Edelstein") said that the strikes had set Iran back by years, but they had not yet succeeded in removing the Iranian threat.[\[874\]](#cite_note-909) Opposition leaders also supported the strikes.[\[875\]](#cite_note-910)

A March 2026 survey by the [Israel Democracy Institute](/wiki/Israel_Democracy_Institute "Israel Democracy Institute") (IDI) found that 82% of the Israeli public supported ongoing military operations, including 93% of [Jewish Israelis](/wiki/Israeli_Jews "Israeli Jews") and 26% of [Arab Israelis](/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel "Arab citizens of Israel").[\[876\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_timesofisrael-poll-911)

#### Media coverage

##### Background

Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and reports of Iranian domestic unrest. Outlets such as [CNN](/wiki/CNN "CNN") and *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* detailed US military buildups in the region, speculating about possible attacks.[\[877\]](#cite_note-CNN-02032026-912) Israeli broadcasters focused on the threats posed by Iranian proxies such as [Hezbollah](/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah").[\[860\]](#cite_note-Brookings_Institute-03032026-895)

##### Disinformation and propaganda

Rumors that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had been killed in Iranian attacks were circulating widely on social media and were amplified by Iranian state-controlled outlets.[\[866\]](#cite_note-i24NEWS-16032026-901)[\[867\]](#cite_note-CTV_News-15032026-902) Netanyahu responded by posting several videos, including one filmed in a Jerusalem cafe in which he sarcastically declared that he was "dying for coffee" while holding up a cappuccino and holding up his hands to show that he had five fingers.[\[878\]](#cite_note-913) The cafe video itself quickly became the subject of fresh rumors, with some social media users and commentators claiming that it too was AI-generated or a [deepfake](/wiki/Deepfake "Deepfake"). The cafe later released images as evidence that Netanyahu had visited.[\[879\]](#cite_note-914)[\[880\]](#cite_note-915)

### United States

This section is an excerpt from [Reactions to the 2026 Iran war § United States](/wiki/Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war#United_States "Reactions to the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Donald_Trump_OEF.jpg/250px-Donald_Trump_OEF.jpg)](/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_OEF.jpg)

US president Trump overseeing the start of "Operation Epic Fury"

President [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") said the US attack on Iran was "to prevent this very wicked, radical dictatorship from threatening America"[\[881\]](#cite_note-916) and to eliminate "imminent threats" from Iran, adding: "For 47 years, the Iranian regime has chanted '[Death to America](/wiki/Death_to_America "Death to America")' and waged an unending campaign of bloodshed and mass murder, targeting the United States, our troops and the innocent people in many, many countries".[\[882\]](#cite_note-917) He suggested that [regime change was an aim](/wiki/Regime_change_efforts_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war"), and called for Iranians to overthrow their government.[\[883\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_:0-918) Trump also said that talks with Iran will be easier following the [assassination of Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei").[\[884\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_octopus-919) When Iran responded by [closing the Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis") and launching [strikes against Arab Gulf allies](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Arab_countries "2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries"), Trump said nobody had warned him and "Nobody expected that. We were shocked". It was later revealed that the president had been told of this likely Iranian retaliation.[\[885\]](#cite_note-920)

Trump wrote on 6 March: "There will be no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER!"[\[886\]](#cite_note-921) On 9 March, Trump said that "the war is very complete, pretty much", and falsely claimed the Iranian military had been destroyed and the Strait of Hormuz had re-opened.[\[887\]](#cite_note-922) Five days later, he called for US allies and China to send warships to help re-open the strait.[\[888\]](#cite_note-923) Trump went on to claim that the US and Israel had "won" the war several times, while continuing to say that the US had not yet completed its objectives.[\[889\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_shifting_timeline-924)[\[890\]](#cite_note-925) He denied that he had ever called for regime change.[\[891\]](#cite_note-926) The president also repeatedly claimed that Iran's military had been destroyed, despite it continuing to launch attacks.[\[892\]](#cite_note-927)[\[893\]](#cite_note-928)

In late March and early April, Trump repeatedly gave ultimatums to Iran, threatening to destroy Iran's civilian infrastructure and bombing it "back to the Stone Ages" if it did not make a deal with the US and re-open the Hormuz strait.[\[894\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_flip-flopping-929) On 7 April, the president threatened that "a whole civilization will die tonight".[\[895\]](#cite_note-930)[\[896\]](#cite_note-931) Following the failed [Islamabad Talks](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks"), Trump said that he "doesn't care" about negotiations,[\[897\]](#cite_note-932) and announced that the US itself would impose a [naval blockade of Iran](/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran") from 13 April.[\[898\]](#cite_note-933) Trump said on 17 April that the Hormuz strait is "COMPLETELY OPEN",[\[889\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_shifting_timeline-924) but on 23 April Trump claimed that he is the one keeping it closed, because opening it would allow Iran to make "$500 million a day".[\[899\]](#cite_note-934)

Reactions inside the US were overall negative but split along party lines, with the majority of Republicans supporting the war and the majority of Democratic and independent voters opposing it.[\[900\]](#cite_note-935)[\[901\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_abc-polls-iran-936) Pundits split similarly, although some notable right-wing pundits such as [Matt Walsh](/wiki/Matt_Walsh_\(political_commentator\) "Matt Walsh (political commentator)") opposed it.[\[902\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Griffing_2026-937)

#### Media coverage

##### Background

Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and reports of Iranian domestic unrest. Outlets such as [CNN](/wiki/CNN "CNN") and *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* detailed US military buildups in the region, speculating about possible attacks.[\[877\]](#cite_note-CNN-02032026-912)

As the airstrikes began, initial reporting relied heavily on satellite imagery and official briefings. The Pentagon's announcements of the destruction of Iranian assets were widely echoed, but independent verification proved difficult due to Tehran's communications restrictions.[\[903\]](#cite_note-938)

##### Disinformation and propaganda

The White House faced backlash over a video that mixed real war footage with video game clips.[\[863\]](#cite_note-CNN-05032026-898) Critics said such efforts distorted public understanding.[\[904\]](#cite_note-Mondoweiss-04032026-939) [The Trump administration's use](/wiki/Use_of_copyrighted_works_by_the_second_Trump_administration "Use of copyrighted works by the second Trump administration") of [copyrighted](/wiki/Copyrighted "Copyrighted") video game clips, cartoon characters, and blockbuster movie scenes for Iran messaging risked turning war into entertainment and a spectacle.[\[905\]](#cite_note-940)

The White House circulates videos fusing real airstrike footages with visuals from video games and action movies, "transforming acts of destruction into a spectacle of national triumph", keeping the audience detached from the human suffering it produces.[\[906\]](#cite_note-941) A video from the White House drew widespread criticism and bewilderment. Another clip used [Kesha](/wiki/Kesha "Kesha")'s song "[Blow](/wiki/Blow_\(Kesha_song\) "Blow (Kesha song)")" under the footage of an airstrike, which prompted the singer to protest against the "perverts".[\[907\]](#cite_note-942) [Blase Cupich](/wiki/Blase_Cupich "Blase Cupich"), an American [Catholic Cardinal](/wiki/Cardinal_\(Catholic_Church\) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") who is close with [Pope Leo XIV](/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV"), referred to a video released by the White House of attacks on Iran mixed with Hollywood film clips as "horrifying" and "sickening".[\[908\]](#cite_note-943)

##### United States media and government

On 14 March 2026, [Federal Communications Commission](/wiki/Federal_Communications_Commission "Federal Communications Commission") Chairman [Brendan Carr](/wiki/Brendan_Carr "Brendan Carr"), a Trump appointee, warned broadcasters that those who "perpetrate fake news and distort the news" must "take the right course" or risk losing their licenses at renewal.[\[909\]](#cite_note-944)[\[910\]](#cite_note-945) Carr said broadcasters "must act in the public interest, and if they don't, they will lose their licenses," citing the public's low trust in legacy media and past election coverage problems. Trump expressed that he was "enthusiastic" about Carr's stance.[\[911\]](#cite_note-946)

Defense Secretary [Pete Hegseth](/wiki/Pete_Hegseth "Pete Hegseth") also criticized the coverage during a news conference, taking issue with CNN's reporting and suggesting emphasizing Iranian frustration rather than adding to the headlines.[\[912\]](#cite_note-947) [Democratic](/wiki/Democratic_Party_\(United_States\) "Democratic Party (United States)") lawmakers condemned the FCC's remarks as unconstitutional censorship, with many calling it "oppressive" and a violation of the First Amendment.[\[913\]](#cite_note-948)

##### Impact

Coverage of the war influenced public opinion, with the US public showing mixed support amid economic concerns.[\[914\]](#cite_note-949)\[*[needs update](/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")*\]

##### Criticism

Analysts accused Western media of failing to challenge the official narrative, with [Mondoweiss](/wiki/Mondoweiss "Mondoweiss") highlighting the flattering language that downplayed civilian casualties.[\[904\]](#cite_note-Mondoweiss-04032026-939) [Al Jazeera](/wiki/Al_Jazeera "Al Jazeera") noted the overrepresentation of voices from the pro-war [Iranian diaspora](/wiki/Iranian_diaspora "Iranian diaspora").[\[915\]](#cite_note-Al_Jazeera_English-07032026-950) Pre-war coverage was also marred by inadequate public warnings.[\[916\]](#cite_note-951)

### International

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Ilham_Aliyev_visited_Iranian_Embassy_in_Azerbaijan_to_offer_condolences_3.jpg/250px-Ilham_Aliyev_visited_Iranian_Embassy_in_Azerbaijan_to_offer_condolences_3.jpg)](/wiki/File:Ilham_Aliyev_visited_Iranian_Embassy_in_Azerbaijan_to_offer_condolences_3.jpg)

Azerbaijani president [Ilham Aliyev](/wiki/Ilham_Aliyev "Ilham Aliyev") visiting the Iranian Embassy in Baku to offer condolences for the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, 4 March 2026

[](/wiki/File:Message_from_the_President_of_the_Republic_of_Cyprus,_Mr._Nikos_Christodoulides_following_first_Iranian_strikes_on_Cyprus.webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:Message_from_the_President_of_the_Republic_of_Cyprus,_Mr._Nikos_Christodoulides_following_first_Iranian_strikes_on_Cyprus.webm)

Message (in Greek) from President of Cyprus, [Nikos Christodoulides](/wiki/Nikos_Christodoulides "Nikos Christodoulides"), following the first Iranian strikes on Cyprus on 2 March 2026

This section is an excerpt from [Reactions to the 2026 Iran war § International](/wiki/Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war#International "Reactions to the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

The [IAEA](/wiki/IAEA "IAEA") Board of Governors convened an emergency meeting as requested by the [Russian Federation](/wiki/Russian_Federation "Russian Federation") on 2 March.[\[917\]](#cite_note-952) IAEA expressed "deep concern" amid attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities, including the [Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant](/wiki/Bushehr_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant").[\[918\]](#cite_note-953) The head of the [World Health Organization](/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") condemned the attacks. The secretary general of [Amnesty International](/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") described such actions as potential war crimes.[\[919\]](#cite_note-954)

According to the founding chief prosecutor of the [International Criminal Court](/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC) [Luis Moreno Ocampo](/wiki/Luis_Moreno_Ocampo "Luis Moreno Ocampo"). the war was comparable to [Russia's war in Ukraine](/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war "Russo-Ukrainian war"), adding that the world is going from a "rules-based system" to the "rule of the man", which was "not a viable world".[\[920\]](#cite_note-955)

European Commission President ⁠[Ursula von der Leyen](/wiki/Ursula_von_der_Leyen "Ursula von der Leyen") and Council ⁠President [Antonio Costa](/wiki/Antonio_Costa "Antonio Costa") called the conflict "greatly concerning" and urged restraint.[\[921\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-2026a-956) On 1 March 2026 Von der Leyen advocated a "credible transition" of power.[\[922\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Europa-957)[\[923\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Zsiros-958) After Trump's threats to destroy Iranian infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz was not reopened on 5 April,[\[924\]](#cite_note-959) Costa denounced "any targeting of civilian infrastructure, namely energy facilities" as illegal and called for a diplomatic solution only.[\[925\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_bbc6april-960)

A spokesperson stated that [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") was closely watching, while a senior official stated that NATO's vigilance was heightened.[\[926\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Korte-961)[\[927\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Bayer-962) NATO secretary general [Mark Rutte](/wiki/Mark_Rutte "Mark Rutte") said that Europe is supportive of the war, as Iran was a threat.[\[928\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_BBC-963) He also said that he felt that the US "knows what it is doing".[\[929\]](#cite_note-964)

Some countries expressed support for the Israeli–United States actions, including [Argentina](/wiki/Argentina_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Argentina in the 2026 Iran war"), [Ukraine](/wiki/Ukraine_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Ukraine in the 2026 Iran war"), Albania,[\[930\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_westernbalkans-965) the Czech Republic,[\[931\]](#cite_note-966) Kosovo,[\[930\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_westernbalkans-965) North Macedonia,[\[930\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_westernbalkans-965) Paraguay,[\[932\]](#cite_note-967) and Papua New Guinea,[\[933\]](#cite_note-968) among other countries which made less explicity statements of support.[\[934\]](#cite_note-969)

The war was condemned by [progressive](/wiki/Progressivism "Progressivism") and left-wing parties, as well as trade unions, [anti-war](/wiki/Anti-war "Anti-war") organizations, and some [far-right](/wiki/Far-right "Far-right") parties worldwide.\[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] Some [far-right](/wiki/Far-right_politics "Far-right politics") movements at the [European Conservatives and Reformists Group](/wiki/European_Conservatives_and_Reformists_Group "European Conservatives and Reformists Group") (such as [AfD](/wiki/Alternative_for_Germany "Alternative for Germany"), [Vlaams Belang](/wiki/Vlaams_Belang "Vlaams Belang"), [ANO](/wiki/ANO_\(political_party\) "ANO (political party)"), [National Rally](/wiki/National_Rally "National Rally"), [Brothers of Italy](/wiki/Brothers_of_Italy "Brothers of Italy"), etc.) criticized the war as against [international law](/wiki/International_law "International law") and the [national interests](/wiki/National_interest "National interest") of European countries, while others (such as [Vox](/wiki/Vox_\(political_party\) "Vox (political party)"), [Reform UK](/wiki/Reform_UK "Reform UK"), [Fidesz](/wiki/Fidesz "Fidesz"), [Law and Justice](/wiki/Law_and_Justice "Law and Justice")) supported the actions in the name of the [free world](/wiki/Free_World "Free World").[\[935\]](#cite_note-970)[\[936\]](#cite_note-971)

After initially opposing war, on 16 March, Gulf countries urged the US to neutralise Iran due to Iranian strikes on their territories.[\[937\]](#cite_note-972)[\[938\]](#cite_note-973) On 19 March, several Arab states asked for a discussion in the [UN Human Rights Council](/wiki/UN_Human_Rights_Council "UN Human Rights Council") to discuss Iran's strikes on civilians and energy infrastructure in the region.[\[939\]](#cite_note-974)[\[940\]](#cite_note-975)

Iran's retaliations were condemned by Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, India, Kuwait, the Palestinian Authority, Qatar,[\[921\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-2026a-956) Saudi Arabia,[\[941\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Naar-2026-976) Syria, Turkey,[\[942\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-977) the UAE,[\[921\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-2026a-956) as well as by several other EU countries,[\[943\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Politico-EU-978) and France, Germany, and the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom_involvement_in_the_2026_Iran_war "United Kingdom involvement in the 2026 Iran war"), who issued a joint declaration. The United Kingdom permitted the US to use British military bases for defensive purposes. Portugal permitted the US to use [Lajes Field](/wiki/Lajes_Field "Lajes Field") for defensive purposes, and France sent its aircraft carrier towards the Mediterranean.[\[942\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-977) Ireland,[\[944\]](#cite_note-979) Slovenia,[\[943\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Politico-EU-978) and Vatican City.[\[945\]](#cite_note-980) In addition to condemnations,[\[943\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Politico-EU-978) Spain denied the use of its military bases for US flights connected to the offensive.[\[946\]](#cite_note-981) On 20 March 2026, the UK approved the US to use British bases to attack Iranian missile sites targeting vessels in the Strait ‌of Hormuz.[\[947\]](#cite_note-982)

Canada [abstained from joining in US-led Israel war in Iran](/wiki/Canada_and_the_2026_Iran_war "Canada and the 2026 Iran war"). On 5 March 2026, France authorized the use of French bases. Mixed reactions or calls for peace were made by South Africa,[\[948\]](#cite_note-983) Azerbaijan,[\[949\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_ArmeniaAzerbaijan-984) Lebanon.[\[950\]](#cite_note-985)[\[951\]](#cite_note-986)[\[921\]](#cite_note-Reactions_to_the_2026_Iran_war_Al_Jazeera_English-2026a-956)

In Pakistan, the [army](/wiki/Pakistan_Army "Pakistan Army") was deployed to suppress an escalation of violence during [pro-Iranian protests](/wiki/Pro-Iranian_protests_during_the_2026_Israeli%E2%80%93United_States_strikes_on_Iran "Pro-Iranian protests during the 2026 Israeli–United States strikes on Iran") in the [northern](/wiki/Northern_Pakistan "Northern Pakistan") cities of [Gilgit](/wiki/Gilgit "Gilgit") and [Skardu](/wiki/Skardu "Skardu"), especially after Shiite demonstrators attacked on 1 March the offices of the [UN Military Observer Group](/wiki/UN_Military_Observer_Group_for_India_and_Pakistan "UN Military Observer Group for India and Pakistan") at [Azad Kashmir](/wiki/Azad_Kashmir "Azad Kashmir"). Similar action was taken in [Sindh](/wiki/Sindh "Sindh") during the [attack on the US consulate in Karachi](/wiki/2026_attack_on_the_United_States_consulate_in_Karachi "2026 attack on the United States consulate in Karachi").[\[952\]](#cite_note-987) There have been movements between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan due to the [Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement](/wiki/Strategic_Mutual_Defence_Agreement "Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement") between both countries, as it "states that any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both".

On 11 March 2026, the [United Nations Security Council](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") passed [Resolution 2817](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2817 "United Nations Security Council Resolution 2817"), sponsored by [Bahrain](/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain"), which called for Iran to stop its attack on Gulf states and condemned the strikes as a violation of international law. The resolution did not mention US–Israel strikes on Iran and Lebanon.[\[953\]](#cite_note-988)[\[954\]](#cite_note-989)

#### Media coverage

Initial coverage in Arab media, including Al Jazeera, emphasized the risks of regional spread, citing attacks on Gulf states. Al Jazeera noted the overrepresentation of voices from the pro-war [Iranian diaspora](/wiki/Iranian_diaspora "Iranian diaspora") in Western media.[\[915\]](#cite_note-Al_Jazeera_English-07032026-950)

## Diplomatic efforts

See also: [Islamabad Talks](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks")

This section is an excerpt from [2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations § 2026 war](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iran%E2%80%93United_States_negotiations#2026_war "2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025%E2%80%932026_Iran%E2%80%93United_States_negotiations&action=edit)\]

On March 1, 2026, Trump claimed that Iranian leaders wanted to resume negotiations and that he had agreed.[\[955\]](#cite_note-990) The late [Ali Larijani](/wiki/Ali_Larijani "Ali Larijani"), [Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council](/wiki/Secretary_of_the_Supreme_National_Security_Council "Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council") of Iran, ruled out talks.[\[956\]](#cite_note-991)[\[957\]](#cite_note-992) Trump then wrote, on March 6: "There will be no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER!"[\[958\]](#cite_note-993) On March 21, it was reported that the US was preparing for peace talks, with six demands. However, Iran refused to negotiate, and had previously rejected several of the demands.[\[959\]](#cite_note-994)[\[960\]](#cite_note-995)

On March 23, Trump postponed the ultimatum he had given on [reopening the Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis"), citing "very good and productive conversations" with Iran.[\[961\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_iranintl-20260323-996) He said the US had been speaking to "a top person" in Iran.[\[962\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_ambiguity-997) IRGC-affiliated [Fars News](/wiki/Fars_News "Fars News") reported that no negotiations had taken place.[\[961\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_iranintl-20260323-996) [Tasnim News Agency](/wiki/Tasnim_News_Agency "Tasnim News Agency"), affiliated with the IRGC, suggested that the US was trying to sow division within Iran by proposing secret talks with only part of its political establishment.[\[963\]](#cite_note-998) *[Iran International](/wiki/Iran_International "Iran International")*, affiliated with the Iranian opposition, suggested that Trump was deliberately being vague and not naming which Iranians were negotiating, as a way to sow mistrust and division within the Iranian regime.[\[962\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_ambiguity-997) The Iranian foreign ministry said it was reviewing US proposals sent through mediators.[\[964\]](#cite_note-999)

Ebrahim Zolfaghari, spokesman for Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, rejected negotiations and said the US must accept "that regional stability is guaranteed by Iran's armed forces".[\[965\]](#cite_note-1000)

On March 25, Pakistani officials passed on a "15-point proposal" from the US to Iran.[\[966\]](#cite_note-1001) The US proposal included an end to Iran's nuclear program, limits on its missiles, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, restrictions on Iran's support for armed groups, and sanctions relief for Iran. The Iranians rejected the proposal. The Iranians issued a "5-point counter-proposal", including an end to US-Israeli attacks on Iran and pro-Iranian forces in Lebanon and Iraq, security guarantees to prevent future Israeli and US aggression, war reparations, and international recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.[\[967\]](#cite_note-1002) The US rejected the proposal.[\[968\]](#cite_note-1003)

In early April Trump threatened to destroy Iran's power plants, oil wells and desalination plants if a deal was not reached "shortly" and the strait not reopened "immediately".[\[969\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_flip-flopping-1004) On the same day, Iranian parliament speaker [Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf](/wiki/Mohammad_Bagher_Ghalibaf "Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf") said that Iran would not give in to "surrender" terms from the US. He accused Washington of sending mixed signals, saying, "The enemy publicly sends messages of negotiation and dialogue, and in secret plans for a ground attack".[\[970\]](#cite_note-1005) On March 30, the Iranian foreign ministry acknowledged they had been holding indirect talks with the US through Pakistani intermediaries.[\[971\]](#cite_note-1006) By contrast, Qatar declined an offer to lead the negotiations.[\[972\]](#cite_note-1007)[\[973\]](#cite_note-1008)

Trump claimed on April 1 that Iran had just asked the US for a ceasefire. He said the US would consider it once the Strait of Hormuz was "open, free, and clear".[\[969\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_flip-flopping-1004) The IRGC separately said that strait "will not be opened to the enemies of this nation".[\[969\]](#cite_note-2025–2026_Iran–United_States_negotiations_flip-flopping-1004) On April 5, Trump again threatened to attack Iran's power plants and bridges if the Hormuz Strait was not reopened. The following day, indirect talks in Islamabad led to a proposal for a 45-day ceasefire. Iran declined, calling for a permanent solution. An Iranian proposal, included a protocol for reopening the strait, an end to all conflicts, the lifting of sanctions, and reconstruction. Later that day, Trump said "They made a ... significant proposal. Not good enough...."[\[974\]](#cite_note-1009) On April 7, Trump threatened, "A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back", if Iran did not reach an agreement with the US.[\[975\]](#cite_note-1010)[\[976\]](#cite_note-1011) Administration officials later confirmed the post was improvisational, and not part of a national security plan.[\[977\]](#cite_note-1012)  

## Analysis

This section is an excerpt from [Analysis of the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Analysis of the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

Military analysts have generally described Iran as being more resilient to US-Israeli attacks than anticipated, and have identified several unanticipated consequences of the attacks for US global interests, chiefly the disruption of international trade brought about by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Many experts argue that the war is illegal under US law,[\[978\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_rl-1013) a claim that the Trump administration has rebuked, citing the precedent of unauthorized military actions by prior presidential administrations.[\[979\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_JustSecurity2April-1014) In [international criminal law](/wiki/International_criminal_law "International criminal law"), experts have identified the attacks as a [crime of aggression](/wiki/Crime_of_aggression "Crime of aggression"),[\[980\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_guardian2march-1015)[\[981\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_BatemanJames-1016) specifically as a [war of aggression](/wiki/War_of_aggression "War of aggression").[\[982\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_AFSC-20260309-1017)[\[983\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_OHCHR-20260312-1018) Numerous critics and analysts identified the US-Israeli attack with a more open embrace of [expansionism](/wiki/American_expansionism_under_Donald_Trump "American expansionism under Donald Trump")[\[984\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_Chaisse-2026-1019)[\[985\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_Chellaney-2026-1020) and [imperialism by the Trump administration](/wiki/American_imperialism#Trump_administration "American imperialism"),[\[986\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_Tait-2026-1021)[\[987\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_Martin-2026-1022) and a departure from the norms of the [liberal international order](/wiki/Liberal_international_order "Liberal international order").[\[988\]](#cite_note-Analysis_of_the_2026_Iran_war_bbc24march-1023)

758.  **[^](#cite_ref-793 "Jump up")** Fabian, Emanuel. ["The war in numbers: 650 Iranian missiles fired; 24 killed in Israel, West Bank; 10,800 Israeli strikes"](https://www.timesofisrael.com/650-iranian-missiles-fired-24-killed-and-10800-israeli-strikes-the-war-in-numbers/), *[The Times of Israel](/wiki/The_Times_of_Israel "The Times of Israel")*, 10 April 2026. Accessed 29 April 2026. "With a ceasefire in Iran taking effect early Wednesday morning, the full scope of the Israeli-American 40-day campaign against the Islamic Republic began to emerge.... Iran, during the fighting, launched some 650 ballistic missiles at Israel. According to the military, more than half of the missiles carried cluster bomb warheads, which spread bomblets indiscriminately over wide areas. The missile attacks killed 20 Israeli civilians and foreign nationals in Israel, along with four Palestinians in the West Bank.... In all, at least 16 missiles carrying conventional warheads — with hundreds of kilograms of explosives — struck populated areas in Israel, causing extensive damage. There were also some 50 incidents of missiles carrying cluster bomb warheads hitting populated areas, with hundreds of separate impact sites.... Casualties and losses

*   **Per US and Israel:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)United States:
        *   15 soldiers killed[\[l\]](#cite_note-26)
        *   538 military personnel wounded
        *   17+ sites damaged[\[15\]](#cite_note-27)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Flag_of_Israel.svg/40px-Flag_of_Israel.svg.png)Israel:
        *   18 soldiers and 1 contractor killed[\[m\]](#cite_note-28)
        *   28 civilians killed[\[n\]](#cite_note-29)
        *   8,594 injured (including 760 military personnel)

* * *

*   **Per Iran:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)United States:
        *   12+ [radar systems](/wiki/Radar "Radar") and [satellite terminals](/wiki/Satcom_\(satellite\) "Satcom (satellite)") destroyed or damaged[\[16\]](#cite_note-30)
        *   Multiple [AN/TPY-2s](/wiki/AN/TPY-2_transportable_radar "AN/TPY-2 transportable radar") destroyed or damaged[\[17\]](#cite_note-31)
        *   1 [THAAD](/wiki/Terminal_High_Altitude_Area_Defense "Terminal High Altitude Area Defense") radar destroyed or seriously damaged[\[18\]](#cite_note-32)
        *   1 [AN/FPS-132](/wiki/Solid_State_Phased_Array_Radar_System "Solid State Phased Array Radar System"), 1 [AN/TPS-59](/wiki/AN/FPS-117 "AN/FPS-117"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-Amoah0305-33) 1 [AN/FPS-117](/wiki/AN/FPS-117 "AN/FPS-117"),[\[20\]](#cite_note-34) 1 [AN/MPQ-64](/wiki/AN/MPQ-64_Sentinel "AN/MPQ-64 Sentinel") destroyed[\[21\]](#cite_note-35)
        *   1 [MIM-104 Patriot](/wiki/MIM-104_Patriot "MIM-104 Patriot") AN/MPQ-65 radar and 1 [AN/TPS-75](/wiki/AN/TPS-75 "AN/TPS-75") damaged[\[22\]](#cite_note-36)

*   **Per Iran:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Flag_of_Iran.svg/40px-Flag_of_Iran.svg.png)Iran:

*   *   3,468 people killed[\[o\]](#cite_note-37)
    *   26,500 injured[\[p\]](#cite_note-38)
*   **Per internal sources:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg.png)Hezbollah:
    *   1,000+ fighters killed[\[23\]](#cite_note-39)
    *   ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Flag_of_the_Amal_Movement.svg/20px-Flag_of_the_Amal_Movement.svg.png) Amal Movement:
    *   6 paramedics killed[\[24\]](#cite_note-40)[\[25\]](#cite_note-41)
    *   ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Flag_of_al-Qassam_Brigades.svg/40px-Flag_of_al-Qassam_Brigades.svg.png) Hamas:
    *   3 members killed[\[26\]](#cite_note-42)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/PMF_infobox.png/40px-PMF_infobox.png)Popular Mobilization Forces:
    *   80 fighters killed, 270 injured[\[27\]](#cite_note-43)

* * *

*   **Per [HRANA](/wiki/HRANA "HRANA"):**  
    3,636 killed (1,221 military personnel, 1,701 civilians, and 714 unclassified)[\[28\]](#cite_note-44)

* * *

*   **Per US and Israel:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Flag_of_Iran.svg/40px-Flag_of_Iran.svg.png)Iran:
    *   6,000+ military personnel killed[\[29\]](#cite_note-Bohbot150326-45)
    *   ~15,000 military personnel wounded[\[29\]](#cite_note-Bohbot150326-45)
    *   190+ ballistic missile launchers destroyed[\[30\]](#cite_note-MakoBelieve-46)
    *   155 naval vessels destroyed or damaged[\[31\]](#cite_note-47)[\[q\]](#cite_note-49)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg.png)Hezbollah:
    *   1,900 fighters killed[\[33\]](#cite_note-50)

*For naval losses, see [this list](/wiki/List_of_ships_attacked_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war")*  
*For aviation losses, see [this list](/wiki/List_of_aviation_shootdowns_and_accidents_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war")*  
*See [casualties](/wiki/Casualties_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Casualties of the 2026 Iran war") for details*.

Lebanon: 2,659 killed and 8,183 injured[\[34\]](#cite_note-51)  
Iraq: 26 soldiers and 23 civilians killed, 180 injured[\[r\]](#cite_note-52)  
Palestine: 14 killed and 15 injured[\[35\]](#cite_note-53)[\[36\]](#cite_note-54)[\[37\]](#cite_note-55)  
United Arab Emirates: 2 soldiers and 11 civilians killed,[\[s\]](#cite_note-59) 227 injured[\[41\]](#cite_note-60)[\[42\]](#cite_note-61)  
Kuwait: 4 soldiers and 6 civilians killed, 77 soldiers and 32 civilians injured[\[t\]](#cite_note-62)  
[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon](/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Force_in_Lebanon "United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon"): 6 killed[\[u\]](#cite_note-UNIFIL_killed-64) and 11 injured[\[v\]](#cite_note-UNIFIL_injured-70)[\[49\]](#cite_note-tayyar.org-71)  
Bahrain: 3 killed and 42 injured[\[w\]](#cite_note-76)  
Saudi Arabia: 3 killed and 23 injured[\[x\]](#cite_note-80)  
Oman: 3 killed and 17 injured[\[57\]](#cite_note-hindustan260302-81)[\[58\]](#cite_note-aj260305-82)[\[59\]](#cite_note-Oman-83)[\[60\]](#cite_note-84)  
France: 1 soldier killed[\[y\]](#cite_note-France-85) and 7 injured[\[y\]](#cite_note-France-85)[\[61\]](#cite_note-trt13march-86)  
Syria: 1 killed[\[62\]](#cite_note-87)  
Qatar: 20 injured[\[63\]](#cite_note-The_Peninsula_Newspaper-2026-88)[\[64\]](#cite_note-89)  
Jordan: 19 injured[\[65\]](#cite_note-90)  
Azerbaijan: 4 injured[\[66\]](#cite_note-ynet260305-91)
