Since 28 February 2026, the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Israel](/wiki/Israel "Israel") have been engaged in a war with [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") and its regional allies. The conflict began when the US and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran, targeting military and government sites and assassinating [several Iranian officials](/wiki/List_of_Iranian_officials_killed_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war"), [including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei"). The surprise attacks were launched during [negotiations between Iran and the US](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iran%E2%80%93United_States_negotiations "2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations") regarding [Iran's nuclear program](/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran"). Iran responded with missile and drone [strikes on Israel](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Israel "2026 Iranian strikes on Israel"), US bases, and US-allied [Arab countries](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Arab_countries "2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries") in [West Asia](/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"); and the [closure of the Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis"), disrupting global trade.

After the [Middle Eastern crisis](/wiki/Middle_Eastern_crisis_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)") began in 2023, Iran and Israel exchanged [missile strikes in 2024](/wiki/2024_Iran%E2%80%93Israel_conflict "2024 Iran–Israel conflict"), and again during the [Twelve-Day War](/wiki/Twelve-Day_War "Twelve-Day War") in June 2025, which resulted in a [US airstrike on Iranian nuclear sites](/wiki/2025_United_States_strikes_on_Iranian_nuclear_sites "2025 United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites"). In January 2026, Iranian security forces [massacred thousands of civilians](/wiki/2026_Iran_massacres "2026 Iran massacres") in their crackdown on the [largest Iranian protests](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests "2025–2026 Iranian protests") since [1979](/wiki/Iranian_Revolution "Iranian Revolution"). US president [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") responded by threatening military action and starting the [largest US military buildup in the region](/wiki/2026_United_States_military_buildup_in_the_Middle_East "2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East") since the [2003 US-led invasion of Iraq](/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq").[\[67\]](#cite_note-92)

Israeli–US airstrikes damaged military bases, government buildings, schools, hospitals, and heritage sites and resulted in [civilian casualties](#Civilians).[\[68\]](#cite_note-93) In retaliation, Iran launched hundreds of [drones](/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicles_in_the_Iranian_military "Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military") and ballistic missiles at Israel, US military bases in the region, and [at neighbouring Arab countries](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Arab_countries "2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries") including [Bahrain](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Bahrain "2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain"), [Jordan](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Jordan "2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan"), [Kuwait](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Kuwait "2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait"), [Oman](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Oman "2026 Iranian strikes on Oman"), [Qatar](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Qatar "2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar"), [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Saudi_Arabia "2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia"), and the [United Arab Emirates](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_United_Arab_Emirates "2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates").[\[69\]](#cite_note-94)[\[70\]](#cite_note-95) Iran and its proxies launched strikes on [Iraq's Kurdistan](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_Kurdistan_Region "2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region"). Drones or missiles also appeared to target [Azerbaijan](/wiki/2026_alleged_Iranian_strikes_on_Azerbaijan "2026 alleged Iranian strikes on Azerbaijan"), [Turkey](/wiki/2026_interceptions_of_Iranian_missiles_in_Turkey "2026 interceptions of Iranian missiles in Turkey"), and Britain's [Akrotiri military base](/wiki/2026_drone_strikes_on_Akrotiri_and_Dhekelia "2026 drone strikes on Akrotiri and Dhekelia") on Cyprus.[\[71\]](#cite_note-96) The [conflict between Hezbollah and Israel](/wiki/Hezbollah%E2%80%93Israel_conflict_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)") escalated into the [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war"), killing more than 2,000 civilians and militants.[\[72\]](#cite_note-AnadoluDeaths-97)[\[73\]](#cite_note-98) Iran has since [restricted internet access](/wiki/2026_Internet_blackout_in_Iran "2026 Internet blackout in Iran") to its people, allowing access only for government-approved users.

The [Trump administration](/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump") gave diverse [explanations for starting the war](/wiki/Rationale_for_the_2026_Iran_war "Rationale for the 2026 Iran war"):[\[74\]](#cite_note-99) to forestall Iranian retaliation after an expected Israeli attack,[\[75\]](#cite_note-100)[\[76\]](#cite_note-101)[\[77\]](#cite_note-102)[\[78\]](#cite_note-103) to stop an imminent Iranian threat, to destroy [Iran's missile capabilities](/wiki/Ballistic_missile_program_of_Iran "Ballistic missile program of Iran"), to prevent Iran from building a [nuclear weapon](/wiki/Nuclear_weapon "Nuclear weapon"),[\[79\]](#cite_note-fullStatement-104) to seize Iran's oil resources,[\[80\]](#cite_note-ft30march-105)[\[81\]](#cite_note-106) and to [achieve regime change](/wiki/Regime_change_efforts_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war") by bringing the [Iranian opposition](/wiki/Iranian_opposition "Iranian opposition") to power.[\[82\]](#cite_note-107)[\[83\]](#cite_note-108)[\[84\]](#cite_note-109)[\[85\]](#cite_note-110) Iranian and some US officials rejected claims that Iran had been preparing an attack.[\[86\]](#cite_note-Scahill-2026-111)[\[87\]](#cite_note-112) The [International Atomic Energy Agency](/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") said that, while Iran has refused to allow inspections of its damaged sites after the 2025 war, there was no evidence of an ongoing nuclear weapons program.[\[88\]](#cite_note-113) [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") secretary-general [António Guterres](/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres "António Guterres") and several uninvolved countries condemned the US–Israeli strikes; the [UN Security Council](/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council") passed [a resolution](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2817 "United Nations Security Council Resolution 2817") condemning Iran's retaliatory strikes on the Gulf states.[\[89\]](#cite_note-114) Critics of the war, including legal and international relations experts, described the US attacks as illegal under US law, an act of [imperialism](/wiki/American_imperialism "American imperialism"),[\[90\]](#cite_note-115)[\[91\]](#cite_note-116) and a violation of Iran's sovereignty[\[92\]](#cite_note-117)[\[93\]](#cite_note-118) under international law.[\[94\]](#cite_note-guardian2march-119)

[The war's economic impact](/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war") includes the world's biggest oil supply disruption since the [1970s energy crisis](/wiki/1970s_energy_crisis "1970s energy crisis"),[\[95\]](#cite_note-120) surges in oil and gas prices, disruptions in aviation and tourism, and volatility in financial markets. Oil and gas shipments were disrupted by Iran's closure of the Hormuz Strait and Israeli and Iranian attacks on energy facilities.[\[96\]](#cite_note-121)[\[97\]](#cite_note-uf-122)[\[98\]](#cite_note-123) On 19 March, the cost of the war to the US military was estimated at US$18 billion,[\[99\]](#cite_note-guardianCost-124) and [the Pentagon](/wiki/The_Pentagon "The Pentagon") requested a further US$200 billion.[\[100\]](#cite_note-i598-125) By 31 March, the cost to Arab countries was estimated at over US$120 billion.[\[101\]](#cite_note-arabCountriesCost-126) The Iranian government assessed the damage to their own economy as at least $300 billion and possibly as much as $1 trillion by 11 April.[\[102\]](#cite_note-127) The US, Israel and Iran all [implemented censorship](/wiki/Censorship_during_the_2026_Iran_war "Censorship during the 2026 Iran war") to hide the damage they had suffered.

US president [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") controversially claimed victory several times[\[103\]](#cite_note-128)[\[104\]](#cite_note-129) and [claimed](/wiki/False_or_misleading_statements_by_Donald_Trump_\(second_term\)#Claims_about_Iran "False or misleading statements by Donald Trump (second term)") the Iranian military had been destroyed.[\[105\]](#cite_note-130)[\[106\]](#cite_note-131) Trump then repeatedly threatened to destroy Iran's infrastructure and "civilization" if they did not make a deal with the US and re-open the Strait of Hormuz.[\[107\]](#cite_note-132)[\[108\]](#cite_note-133) Iran, the US and Israel agreed to a [two-week ceasefire](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire") brokered by Pakistan, beginning on 8 April.[\[109\]](#cite_note-Pager-2026-134) The ceasefire came under strain as Iran refused to re-open the Hormuz strait, blaming the [Israeli strikes in Lebanon](/wiki/8_April_2026_Lebanon_attacks "8 April 2026 Lebanon attacks").[\[110\]](#cite_note-135) After the failure of the [Islamabad Talks](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks"), Trump said he no longer cared about negotiations,[\[111\]](#cite_note-independent13april-136) and announced a [naval blockade of Iran](/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran") from 13 April.[\[112\]](#cite_note-137) A [ceasefire in Lebanon](/wiki/2026_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire "2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire") began on 16 April.[\[113\]](#cite_note-aljazeera16april-138) Iran announced that commercial shipping would be allowed through the Hormuz strait during this ceasefire,[\[114\]](#cite_note-reuters17april-139) but re-imposed restrictions when the US refused to lift its naval blockade.[\[115\]](#cite_note-business-standard-18april-140) The US Navy seized [an Iranian cargo ship](/wiki/Touska "Touska"), which Iran called a truce violation,[\[116\]](#cite_note-ndtv20april-141) and Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy any Iranian boats laying mines in the strait.[\[117\]](#cite_note-telanganatoday23april-142) Trump has extended the truce indefinitely.[\[118\]](#cite_note-aljazeera21april-143) There is currently a "dual blockade", with the US Navy blockading Iran and Iran blockading the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf").[\[119\]](#cite_note-Guardian_24_Apr_26-144) On 4 May, the US Navy began a [mission to escort ships](/wiki/Operation_Project_Freedom "Operation Project Freedom") out of the Gulf.[\[120\]](#cite_note-internazionale3may-145) The Iranian military warned this would be a breach of the truce.[\[121\]](#cite_note-aljazeera4may-146) On 6 May, President Trump announced a temporary pause in the US military's "Project Freedom" operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, indicating "great progress" toward a possible agreement with Iran. The operation will be delayed briefly to assess the potential for a "complete and final agreement" with Iran.[\[122\]](#cite_note-aljazeera6may-147) On the same day, Trump stated that if Iran fails to agree to an agreement to end the war, the U.S. will escalate bombing significantly in terms of intensity and level.[\[123\]](#cite_note-ndtv6may-148) The US military announced on the same day that it disabled an Iranian-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman for allegedly trying to breach the American blockade en route to an Iranian port.[\[124\]](#cite_note-aa6may-149)

## Background

.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}

Main articles: [Rationale for the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Rationale_for_the_2026_Iran_war "Rationale for the 2026 Iran war") and [Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Regime_change_efforts_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war")

Further information: [Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)](/wiki/Middle_Eastern_crisis_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)")

### Iran's relations with the United States and Israel

Further information: [Iran–United States relations](/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93United_States_relations "Iran–United States relations") and [Iran–Israel relations](/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_relations "Iran–Israel relations")

A US- and UK-backed [coup d'état in 1953](/wiki/1953_Iranian_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat "1953 Iranian coup d'état") deposed Iranian prime minister [Mohammad Mosaddegh](/wiki/Mohammad_Mosaddegh "Mohammad Mosaddegh") due to his [nationalization of the oil industry](/wiki/Nationalization_of_the_Iranian_oil_industry "Nationalization of the Iranian oil industry"), strengthening the rule of [Shah](/wiki/Shah "Shah") [Mohammad Reza Pahlavi](/wiki/Mohammad_Reza_Pahlavi "Mohammad Reza Pahlavi"). Israel maintained ties with Iran as part of its [alliance of the periphery](/wiki/Alliance_of_the_periphery "Alliance of the periphery") strategy. Resentment of the Shah's deference to Western interests and his autocratic rule led to the [1979 revolution](/wiki/Iranian_Revolution "Iranian Revolution") in which Pahlavi was overthrown and replaced by an [Islamic republic](/wiki/Islamic_republic "Islamic republic").[\[125\]](#cite_note-150)[\[126\]](#cite_note-151) Iran severed diplomatic ties with the US and Israel and held the [American embassy staff hostage](/wiki/Iran_hostage_crisis "Iran hostage crisis") for over a year.[\[127\]](#cite_note-News1828-152)[\[128\]](#cite_note-rishikasingh-153)

During the [Iran–Iraq War](/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "Iran–Iraq War"), the [US supported Iraq](/wiki/United_States_support_for_Iraq_during_the_Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "United States support for Iraq during the Iran–Iraq War"). In 1988, [a US warship was struck by an Iranian mine](/wiki/USS_Samuel_B._Roberts_\(FFG-58\)#1988_deployment_and_mine_strike "USS Samuel B. Roberts (FFG-58)"); the US responded by [attacking Iran's navy](/wiki/Operation_Praying_Mantis "Operation Praying Mantis"). A few months later, the US mistakenly shot down a [civilian Iranian flight](/wiki/Iran_Air_Flight_655 "Iran Air Flight 655").[\[129\]](#cite_note-MacFarquhar1926-154) Iran started a ballistic missile program to deter Iraqi [missile attacks on Iranian cities](/wiki/War_of_the_Cities "War of the Cities") and to compensate for its lack of a modern air force due to sanctions.[\[130\]](#cite_note-155)[\[131\]](#cite_note-Al-MarashiCon-156)

Starting in the 1980s, Iran began engaging in [proxy conflicts](/wiki/Proxy_conflicts "Proxy conflicts") throughout the Middle East. Iran backed [Hezbollah](/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah") in Lebanon against Israel during and after the [Lebanese Civil War](/wiki/Lebanese_Civil_War "Lebanese Civil War"). During the [Iraq War](/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), Iran supported militias fighting the US in Iraq. Along with the [Houthis](/wiki/Houthis "Houthis") in [Yemen](/wiki/Yemen "Yemen") and other groups in Syria and Palestine, these proxy groups became part of the informal '[Axis of Resistance](/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance "Axis of Resistance")' committed to countering American, Israeli, Saudi, and Emirati influence in the region.

In 2002, Iran's covert expansion of its nuclear program was first revealed. Beginning in 2006, the [United Nations Security Council](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") responded with [a series of sanctions against Iran](/wiki/International_sanctions_against_Iran#UN_sanctions_against_Iran "International sanctions against Iran"), with the US imposing [its own series of sanctions against Iran](/wiki/United_States_sanctions_against_Iran "United States sanctions against Iran"). The US and Israel conducted [a campaign of cyberwarfare](/wiki/Operation_Olympic_Games "Operation Olympic Games") against Iranian nuclear facilities to disrupt their operations, while Israel [assassinated several top Iranian nuclear scientists](/wiki/Assassinations_of_Iranian_nuclear_scientists "Assassinations of Iranian nuclear scientists").[\[129\]](#cite_note-MacFarquhar1926-154)[\[132\]](#cite_note-Le_Monde_Assassinations-157) The conflict escalated in January 2020 when President Trump ordered the [assassination of Qasem Soleimani](/wiki/Assassination_of_Qasem_Soleimani "Assassination of Qasem Soleimani"), the commander of the [Quds Force](/wiki/Quds_Force "Quds Force").[\[127\]](#cite_note-News1828-152)[\[131\]](#cite_note-Al-MarashiCon-156)

Tensions escalated following the [October 7 attacks](/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks") on Israel and the start of the [Gaza war](/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war"). Israel fought Iran-backed militias across the Middle East, including [Hamas](/wiki/Hamas "Hamas")[\[z\]](#cite_note-160), [Hezbollah](/wiki/Hezbollah%E2%80%93Israel_conflict_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)"), and the [Houthis](/wiki/Red_Sea_crisis "Red Sea crisis"). [Israeli strikes on the Iranian consulate in Damascus](/wiki/Israeli_airstrike_on_the_Iranian_consulate_in_Damascus "Israeli airstrike on the Iranian consulate in Damascus") and the [assassination of Ismail Haniyeh](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ismail_Haniyeh "Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh") were met with Iranian strikes on Israel in [April](/wiki/April_2024_Iranian_strikes_on_Israel "April 2024 Iranian strikes on Israel") and [October](/wiki/October_2024_Iranian_strikes_on_Israel "October 2024 Iranian strikes on Israel"). In June 2025, Israel launched the [Twelve-Day War](/wiki/Twelve-Day_War "Twelve-Day War") by attacking Iranian military and nuclear facilities, provoking Iranian counter-strikes. The US also [struck Iranian nuclear facilities](/wiki/United_States_strikes_on_Iranian_nuclear_sites "United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites") during the Twelve-Day War, which ended in a [ceasefire](/wiki/Twelve-Day_War_ceasefire "Twelve-Day War ceasefire").[\[135\]](#cite_note-161)

In early 2026, Israeli Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") lobbied President Donald Trump for a joint military strike on Iran, specifically targeting its leadership.[\[136\]](#cite_note-162) Following high-level meetings in February, Trump authorized "Operation Epic Fury", with reports citing [Israeli intelligence](/wiki/Israeli_intelligence_community "Israeli intelligence community") provided by Netanyahu as a decisive factor in the decision.[\[137\]](#cite_note-163)

### Iran nuclear issue

Further information: [Iran and weapons of mass destruction § Nuclear weapons](/wiki/Iran_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction#Nuclear_weapons "Iran and weapons of mass destruction")

See also: [Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons § Iran](/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons#Iran "Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons")

Iran suspended its [AMAD Project](/wiki/AMAD_Project "AMAD Project") pursuant to [Ali Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons](/wiki/Ali_Khamenei%27s_fatwa_against_nuclear_weapons "Ali Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons") in 2003. Khamenei banned nuclear weapons of any kind.[\[138\]](#cite_note-164)[\[139\]](#cite_note-165) Iran said it was not seeking nuclear weapons, and that its enrichment efforts were to generate [nuclear power](/wiki/Nuclear_power "Nuclear power") for civilian use.[\[140\]](#cite_note-166) [UN Security Council](/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council") (UNSC) concerns about Iran's [nuclear program](/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran") from 2006[\[aa\]](#cite_note-170) led to the [Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action](/wiki/Joint_Comprehensive_Plan_of_Action "Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action") (JCPOA) between Iran and the US in 2015.[\[144\]](#cite_note-171)

Despite Iran's compliance with the JCPOA,[\[145\]](#cite_note-172) Trump [withdrew the US](/wiki/United_States_withdrawal_from_the_JCPOA "United States withdrawal from the JCPOA") from the deal in 2018,[\[146\]](#cite_note-173) re-imposed [sanctions](/wiki/United_States_sanctions_against_Iran "United States sanctions against Iran"), and adopted a "[maximum pressure](/wiki/Maximum_pressure_campaign "Maximum pressure campaign")" strategy.[\[147\]](#cite_note-174) The [Biden administration](/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration") kept most of these sanctions in place, further damaging Iran's economy.[\[148\]](#cite_note-175) Trump continued the "maximum pressure" approach in his second term.[\[149\]](#cite_note-176) In September 2025, the UN reimposed [sanctions on Iran](/wiki/International_sanctions_against_Iran "International sanctions against Iran") using the ["snapback" mechanism](/wiki/Snapback_mechanism_of_sanctions_against_Iran "Snapback mechanism of sanctions against Iran"), causing the [currency](/wiki/Iranian_rial "Iranian rial") to weaken, resulting in price increases for food supplies such as meat, rice, and other staples, freezing Iranian assets abroad, suspending arms transactions, and imposing penalties related to the country's [ballistic-missile programme](/wiki/Ballistic_missile_program_of_Iran "Ballistic missile program of Iran").[\[150\]](#cite_note-177)[\[151\]](#cite_note-178) [Treasury Secretary](/wiki/Secretary_of_the_Treasury "Secretary of the Treasury") [Scott Bessent](/wiki/Scott_Bessent "Scott Bessent") labelled the collapse of the Iranian currency in December 2025 as the strategy's "grand culmination".[\[152\]](#cite_note-179)[\[153\]](#cite_note-180) At his [State of the Union Address](/wiki/2026_State_of_the_Union_Address "2026 State of the Union Address") on 24 February 2026, Trump claimed that Iran had restarted its nuclear program and was developing missiles capable of striking the US.[\[154\]](#cite_note-181) Trump's claims about Iran rebuilding its nuclear program and developing long-range ballistic missiles have contradicted both his previous claims that Iran's nuclear program was "obliterated" and US intelligence reports that Iran did not pose any military threat towards the US and needed until 2035 to build such missiles were it to do so.[\[155\]](#cite_note-182)

A few days later, the [International Atomic Energy Agency](/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") (IAEA) reported that Iran had stored [highly enriched uranium](/wiki/Highly_enriched_uranium "Highly enriched uranium") in an underground facility that was undamaged by [US bombings in 2025](/wiki/2025_United_States_strikes_on_Iranian_nuclear_sites "2025 United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites").[\[156\]](#cite_note-183) Subsequently, Iran denied the IAEA access to nuclear facilities that had been bombed, but did provide access at least once to all unaffected facilities since June 2025.[\[157\]](#cite_note-AP_News_IAEA_Post_War-184) [Mohammad Eslami](/wiki/Mohammad_Eslami "Mohammad Eslami"), the head of the [Atomic Energy Organization of Iran](/wiki/Atomic_Energy_Organization_of_Iran "Atomic Energy Organization of Iran"), said Iran would not permit inspections of facilities struck by the US until the IAEA established rules for the post-war situation, insisting on codified protocols for internationally protected facilities subjected to military attacks, and that the IAEA condemn the attacks.[\[158\]](#cite_note-185)

In February 2026, Iran informed the IAEA that normal safeguards were "legally untenable and materially impracticable," as a result of threats and "acts of aggression," leaving the IAEA unable to verify whether Iran had suspended enrichment or confirm the status of its current stockpile,[\[157\]](#cite_note-AP_News_IAEA_Post_War-184) though it found no evidence Iran was weaponizing.[\[159\]](#cite_note-186) Analysts in the UK and US have characterized Iran’s strategy as [nuclear hedging](/wiki/Nuclear_latency "Nuclear latency"), developing the technical infrastructure to assemble a weapon on short notice while stopping short of actual production.[\[160\]](#cite_note-187) The [Bulletin of Atomic Scientists](/wiki/Bulletin_of_Atomic_Scientists "Bulletin of Atomic Scientists") said that Iran was using its enrichment program and uranium stockpiles for leverage in international negotiations, and was willing to dilute or export its higher-level enriched uranium in exchange for sanctions relief and prevention of future attacks.[\[161\]](#cite_note-188)

### Israel nuclear issue

Further information: [Israel and nuclear weapons](/wiki/Israel_and_nuclear_weapons "Israel and nuclear weapons") and [Middle East nuclear weapon free zone](/wiki/Middle_East_nuclear_weapon_free_zone "Middle East nuclear weapon free zone")

Israel is [widely believed to possess nuclear weapons](/wiki/Israel_and_nuclear_weapons "Israel and nuclear weapons"), with a stockpile estimated between 90 and 400 nuclear warheads.[\[172\]](#cite_note-199) Israel is the only [nuclear-armed country](/wiki/List_of_states_with_nuclear_weapons "List of states with nuclear weapons") that [does not officially acknowledge](/wiki/Israel_and_nuclear_weapons#Policy "Israel and nuclear weapons") its nuclear weapons capability.[\[173\]](#cite_note-Kristensen-2022-200) Some scholars have argued that Israel's nuclear weapons have incentivized Iran to develop its own nuclear program, seen as maintaining a balance of [nuclear deterrence](/wiki/Deterrence_theory "Deterrence theory"), or causing a regional [nuclear arms race](/wiki/Nuclear_arms_race "Nuclear arms race").[\[174\]](#cite_note-201)[\[175\]](#cite_note-202)[\[176\]](#cite_note-203)[\[177\]](#cite_note-204) Citing security threats, Israel rejects international calls to accede to the [Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons](/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons "Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons") or to participate in negotiations of a [Middle East nuclear weapon free zone](/wiki/Middle_East_nuclear_weapon_free_zone "Middle East nuclear weapon free zone").[\[178\]](#cite_note-205)[\[179\]](#cite_note-206)[\[180\]](#cite_note-s316-207) This has frustrated both US[\[173\]](#cite_note-Kristensen-2022-200) and UK[\[181\]](#cite_note-208) diplomatic efforts on such a zone. Scholars also suggest US tacit acceptance of the Israeli nuclear weapons capability is seen as a double standard that undermines its diplomatic credibility in Middle East [nonproliferation](/wiki/Nonproliferation "Nonproliferation") negotiations.[\[182\]](#cite_note-209)[\[173\]](#cite_note-Kristensen-2022-200)[\[183\]](#cite_note-210)

## Prelude

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/President_Donald_J._Trump_Welcomes_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Benjamin_Netanyahu_to_the_White_House_%28cropped_b%29.jpg/250px-President_Donald_J._Trump_Welcomes_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Benjamin_Netanyahu_to_the_White_House_%28cropped_b%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:President_Donald_J._Trump_Welcomes_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Benjamin_Netanyahu_to_the_White_House_\(cropped_b\).jpg)

Israeli Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") successfully lobbied the [Trump administration](/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump") for military intervention.

.mw-parser-output .excerpt-hat .mw-editsection-like{font-style:normal}

This section is an excerpt from [Prelude to the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war "Prelude to the 2026 Iran war").\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war&action=edit)\]

Tensions between [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") and the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") over [Iran's nuclear program](/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran") began to intensify in January 2026 amid Iran's [massacres of Iranian civilians](/wiki/2026_Iran_massacres "2026 Iran massacres") in their crackdown of the [2025–2026 anti-government protests](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests "2025–2026 Iranian protests").[\[184\]](#cite_note-211) The US and Iran began indirect negotiations in February in Oman, but produced no agreement. The US began [amassing air and naval assets in the region](/wiki/2026_United_States_military_buildup_in_the_Middle_East "2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East") at a level not seen since the outset of the [2003 US-led invasion of Iraq](/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq"). The US government signaled that airstrikes remained an option, emphasizing that all responses were under consideration while maintaining that diplomacy was still preferred.[\[185\]](#cite_note-212) US president [Donald Trump](/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and his administration officials like Vice President [JD Vance](/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance"), Secretary of State [Marco Rubio](/wiki/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio"), and Special Envoy [Steve Witkoff](/wiki/Steve_Witkoff "Steve Witkoff") all accused Iran of building up its nuclear and missile programs to threaten the United States and its interests. Iran in turn accused the US of waging "disinformation and misinformation" campaigns against it.[\[186\]](#cite_note-Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war_vance-213)[\[187\]](#cite_note-Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war_rubio-214)[\[188\]](#cite_note-Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war_witkoff-215)[\[189\]](#cite_note-Prelude_to_the_2026_Iran_war_:86-216)

Regional actors, including [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), cautioned that any escalation could have severe consequences for the [Middle East](/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"). [Negotiations regarding the Iranian nuclear program](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iran%E2%80%93United_States_negotiations "2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations") were held in February, and on 28 February 2026 the US and Israel conducted military strikes in Iran.[\[190\]](#cite_note-217)

## Hostilities

Further information: [Timeline of the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Timeline_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Timeline of the 2026 Iran war")

### First week (28 February – 6 March)

.mw-parser-output .ambox{border:1px solid #a2a9b1;border-left:10px solid #36c;background-color:#fbfbfb;box-sizing:border-box}.mw-parser-output .ambox+link+.ambox,.mw-parser-output .ambox+link+style+.ambox,.mw-parser-output .ambox+link+link+.ambox,.mw-parser-output .ambox+.mw-empty-elt+link+.ambox,.mw-parser-output .ambox+.mw-empty-elt+link+style+.ambox,.mw-parser-output .ambox+.mw-empty-elt+link+link+.ambox{margin-top:-1px}html body.mediawiki .mw-parser-output .ambox.mbox-small-left{margin:4px 1em 4px 0;overflow:hidden;width:238px;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:88%;line-height:1.25em}.mw-parser-output .ambox-speedy{border-left:10px solid #b32424;background-color:#fee7e6}.mw-parser-output .ambox-delete{border-left:10px solid #b32424}.mw-parser-output .ambox-content{border-left:10px solid #f28500}.mw-parser-output .ambox-style{border-left:10px solid #fc3}.mw-parser-output .ambox-move{border-left:10px solid #9932cc}.mw-parser-output .ambox-protection{border-left:10px solid #a2a9b1}.mw-parser-output .ambox .mbox-text{border:none;padding:0.25em 0.5em;width:100%}.mw-parser-output .ambox .mbox-image{border:none;padding:2px 0 2px 0.5em;text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .ambox .mbox-imageright{border:none;padding:2px 0.5em 2px 0;text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .ambox .mbox-empty-cell{border:none;padding:0;width:1px}.mw-parser-output .ambox .mbox-image-div{width:52px}@media(min-width:720px){.mw-parser-output .ambox{margin:0 10%}}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .ambox{display:none!important}}

It has been suggested that portions of this section be [**split**](/wiki/Wikipedia:Splitting "Wikipedia:Splitting") out into another article. ([**Discuss**](/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#Articles_for_Operation_Epic_Fury/Operation_Roaring_Lion/Operation_True_Promise_IV? "Talk:2026 Iran war")) *(April 2026)*

Further information: [Assassination of Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei"), [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war"), [2026 Minab school attack](/wiki/2026_Minab_school_attack "2026 Minab school attack"), and [2026 Lamerd sports hall attack](/wiki/2026_Lamerd_sports_hall_attack "2026 Lamerd sports hall attack")

[](/wiki/File:President_Donald_J._Trump_on_the_United_States_Military_Major_Combat_Operations_in_Iran.webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:President_Donald_J._Trump_on_the_United_States_Military_Major_Combat_Operations_in_Iran.webm)

28 February: Trump addresses the nation about the strikes.

On 27 February at 3:38 p.m. [EST](/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone#Eastern_Standard_Time "Eastern Time Zone") (11:08 p.m. [IRST](/wiki/Iran_Standard_Time "Iran Standard Time")), Donald Trump, traveling on [Air Force One](/wiki/Air_Force_One "Air Force One") to [Corpus Christi](/wiki/Corpus_Christi,_Texas "Corpus Christi, Texas"), Texas, gave the order to proceed with Operation Epic Fury.[\[191\]](#cite_note-218)[\[192\]](#cite_note-FT01-219) US missiles, drones, and [Israeli fighter jets](/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force#Current_inventory "Israeli Air Force") began striking Iran the next day, around 9:45 a.m. IRST (1:15 a.m. EST).[\[193\]](#cite_note-220)[\[194\]](#cite_note-221) The strikes took place during active negotiations over Iran's nuclear program.[\[195\]](#cite_note-222)[\[196\]](#cite_note-223) The attacks coincided with the holy month of [Ramadan](/wiki/Ramadan "Ramadan"), during which Muslims [fast](/wiki/Islamic_fasting "Islamic fasting") from dawn to sunset.[\[197\]](#cite_note-224)

The operation was codenamed Operation Roaring Lion[\[ab\]](#cite_note-225) by Israel.[\[198\]](#cite_note-226)[\[199\]](#cite_note-227) The [Israeli Air Force](/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") (IAF) said that it had struck 500 military targets in western and central Iran in the largest combat sortie in its history.[\[200\]](#cite_note-228) Iranian naval vessels were also targeted.[\[201\]](#cite_note-229) Israel later said its initial strikes used over 1,200 bombs in 24 hours.[\[202\]](#cite_note-230) A US official said dozens of US strikes were carried out by planes based around the Middle East and from one or more aircraft carriers.[\[203\]](#cite_note-231)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/U_S_Forces_Launch_Operation_Epic_Fury_%289542157%29.jpg/250px-U_S_Forces_Launch_Operation_Epic_Fury_%289542157%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:U_S_Forces_Launch_Operation_Epic_Fury_\(9542157\).jpg)

27 February: US aircraft sit on the flight deck of [USS *Abraham Lincoln*](/wiki/USS_Abraham_Lincoln_\(CVN-72\) "USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)")

According to Iran International, quoting the [Iranian Students' News Agency](/wiki/Iranian_Students%27_News_Agency "Iranian Students' News Agency"), thousands of [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps](/wiki/Islamic_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps") (IRGC) personnel, including several senior officials,[\[204\]](#cite_note-232) were killed or wounded\[*[vague](/wiki/Wikipedia:Vagueness "Wikipedia:Vagueness")*\] as several military bases were attacked.[\[205\]](#cite_note-Iran_International-2026a-233) Several strikes hit Tehran's [Pasteur Street](/wiki/Pasteur_Street "Pasteur Street") district, where the presidential palace is, and the [National Security Council](/wiki/Supreme_National_Security_Council "Supreme National Security Council").[\[206\]](#cite_note-234)[\[207\]](#cite_note-235)

The strikes were coupled with cyberattacks on Iranian infrastructure, media, and phone apps, with messages calling on Iranians to rise up against their government.[\[208\]](#cite_note-236)[\[209\]](#cite_note-JPost_hack-237)[\[210\]](#cite_note-238) The cyberattacks resulted in a near-total internet blackout in Iran, lasting over 60 hours with connectivity dropping to as low as 1% of normal levels, disrupting government communications, state media, and public services.[\[211\]](#cite_note-239)[\[209\]](#cite_note-JPost_hack-237) [Iran has since restricted internet access](/wiki/2026_Internet_blackout_in_Iran "2026 Internet blackout in Iran") to its people, allowing access only for government-approved users.[\[212\]](#cite_note-240)[\[213\]](#cite_note-bm-241)

Israeli military officials said months-long planning preceded their strikes, allowing them to pinpoint their targets, attain "tactical surprise", and gain US support.[\[214\]](#cite_note-242) Attacking during the morning, rather than at night which was when most of Israel's previous attacks on Iran took place, added to the element of surprise.[\[215\]](#cite_note-243) After the strikes began, Israel declared a state of emergency, citing expectation of an Iranian retaliation, and warned its citizens to remain in protected areas.[\[216\]](#cite_note-Liebermann-2026-244)[\[217\]](#cite_note-245) Israel called up 20,000 reservists in addition to the 50,000 already on duty.[\[218\]](#cite_note-246) The [Israeli Ministry of Health](/wiki/Israeli_Ministry_of_Health "Israeli Ministry of Health") moved its hospital operations underground.[\[219\]](#cite_note-247) Israel warned Iranian civilians residing near military industries and infrastructure to evacuate immediately.[\[205\]](#cite_note-Iran_International-2026a-233)

At 2:30 a.m. EST on 28 February, Donald Trump released an eight-minute video statement on [Truth Social](/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social"), saying that the purpose of the US strikes in Iran was effectively\[*[vague](/wiki/Wikipedia:Vagueness "Wikipedia:Vagueness")*\] [regime change](/wiki/Regime_change "Regime change"). Trump said that Iran's "menacing activities" endangered the US and its allies. He cited the [Iran hostage crisis](/wiki/Iran_hostage_crisis "Iran hostage crisis"), support for proxies such as [Hamas](/wiki/Hamas "Hamas") and [Hezbollah](/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah"), and [its killings of protesters](/wiki/Human_rights_in_Iran "Human rights in Iran").[\[220\]](#cite_note-CBS_Major-Combat-Operations-248) Trump cited Iran calling "[Death to America](/wiki/Death_to_America "Death to America")" and its alleged history of attacking US civilians and soldiers as evidence of Iran's intent against the United States.[\[79\]](#cite_note-fullStatement-104)[\[221\]](#cite_note-249)

Trump and [Benjamin Netanyahu](/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") both warned of the potential threat of nuclear weapons in Iran and called on the Iranian people to overthrow their government.[\[220\]](#cite_note-CBS_Major-Combat-Operations-248)[\[222\]](#cite_note-250) *[The Times of Israel](/wiki/The_Times_of_Israel "The Times of Israel")* reported that Defense Minister [Israel Katz](/wiki/Israel_Katz "Israel Katz") labeled the strikes a "pre-emptive attack" intended to "remove threats to the State of Israel".[\[216\]](#cite_note-Liebermann-2026-244) Iran rejected claims that it intended to attack the United States, citing the aggressive posture of the US armed forces as evidence.[\[86\]](#cite_note-Scahill-2026-111)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/US_bases_in_the_Middle_East.svg/250px-US_bases_in_the_Middle_East.svg.png)](/wiki/File:US_bases_in_the_Middle_East.svg)

Major [US military bases and installations](/wiki/List_of_American_military_installations "List of American military installations") in the Middle East, including bases used during the strikes

Iranian forces reacted within hours by launching missiles and drones. Iran codenamed its military response .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#ebf4ff}@media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#0f4dc9}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#0f4dc9}}Operation True Promise IV.[\[ac\]](#cite_note-251)[\[ad\]](#cite_note-252) Iranian state media also dubbed the events as the Ramadan War,[\[ae\]](#cite_note-253) as the US-Israeli attacks coincided with the holy month of [Ramadan](/wiki/Ramadan "Ramadan").[\[223\]](#cite_note-254)

Iran struck Israeli targets in [Tel Aviv](/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") and [Haifa](/wiki/Haifa "Haifa")[\[224\]](#cite_note-BBC_Tehran_response-255) as well as multiple countries throughout the Persian Gulf region.[\[225\]](#cite_note-256) Major targets included Bahrain's capital [Manama](/wiki/Manama "Manama"),[\[226\]](#cite_note-257)[\[227\]](#cite_note-258) [Kuwait International Airport](/wiki/Kuwait_International_Airport "Kuwait International Airport"), the United Arab Emirates' capital [Abu Dhabi](/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"),[\[228\]](#cite_note-259)[\[229\]](#cite_note-260) [Riyadh](/wiki/Riyadh "Riyadh") and [Eastern Province](/wiki/Eastern_Province,_Saudi_Arabia "Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia") in Saudi Arabia,[\[230\]](#cite_note-261) and [Erbil International Airport](/wiki/Erbil_International_Airport "Erbil International Airport") and the [US Consulate General in Erbil](/wiki/Consulate_General_of_the_United_States_in_Erbil "Consulate General of the United States in Erbil") in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.[\[231\]](#cite_note-262)

Iran reported striking the US bases of [Al Udeid Air Base](/wiki/Al_Udeid_Air_Base "Al Udeid Air Base") in Qatar, [Ali Al Salem Air Base](/wiki/Ali_Al_Salem_Air_Base "Ali Al Salem Air Base") in Kuwait,[\[232\]](#cite_note-263) [Al Dhafra Air Base](/wiki/Al_Dhafra_Air_Base "Al Dhafra Air Base") in the UAE, and the US Navy [Fifth Fleet](/wiki/Fifth_Fleet "Fifth Fleet") headquarters in Bahrain.[\[233\]](#cite_note-264) Local sources said Iran used [Shahed drones](/wiki/Shahed_drones "Shahed drones"), which are among the weapons most used by Iran and its proxies, including Hamas and Hezbollah.[\[234\]](#cite_note-265) On 1 or 2 March, Iran struck the radar bases for US [THAAD](/wiki/Terminal_High_Altitude_Area_Defense "Terminal High Altitude Area Defense") missile defense systems in Jordan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, destroying at least one of them.[\[235\]](#cite_note-266)

Israel launched a new wave of strikes against Iranian targets.[\[236\]](#cite_note-Reuters-2026-267) Iran launched missiles and drones on Bahrain, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.[\[237\]](#cite_note-268)[\[238\]](#cite_note-269) The United Kingdom reported "two missiles fired in the direction of Cyprus", but that they "don't believe they were targeted at Cyprus". However, the presidents of Cyprus and [Northern Cyprus](/wiki/Northern_Cyprus "Northern Cyprus") both denied the claims that any missiles were fired at Cyprus.[\[239\]](#cite_note-270)[\[240\]](#cite_note-271)[\[241\]](#cite_note-272) Two oil tankers, the [Palau](/wiki/Palau "Palau")\-flagged *Skylight* and the [Marshall Islands](/wiki/Marshall_Islands "Marshall Islands")\-flagged *MKD VYOM*, were targeted off the coast of Oman.[\[242\]](#cite_note-273)[\[243\]](#cite_note-274)[\[244\]](#cite_note-275) Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz slowed to a standstill,[\[245\]](#cite_note-276) with 150 freight ships, including many oil tankers, stalled.[\[246\]](#cite_note-277)

To avert further Iranian strikes, the [E3](/wiki/EU_three#E3 "EU three") (the UK, France, and Germany) resolved to back, if needed, "proportionate military defensive measures" against drones and ballistic missiles, signaling the potential for direct involvement.[\[247\]](#cite_note-278) British prime minister [Keir Starmer](/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer") said that US can use British bases for "defensive" strikes on Iran[\[248\]](#cite_note-279) and disclosed that Ukrainian and other specialists would aid Gulf efforts to foil Iranian drone strikes.[\[249\]](#cite_note-280) [CNN](/wiki/CNN "CNN") reported that Saudi Crown Prince Salman, with US backing, vowed to employ military force against further Iranian incursions, calling Iranian strikes "cowardly" due to Saudi airspace being closed to US and Israeli attackers.[\[250\]](#cite_note-281) On 1 March, Trump announced that the US had accepted an Iranian proposal to further negotiations.[\[251\]](#cite_note-282) However, Ali Larijani subsequently ruled out talks.[\[252\]](#cite_note-283)

[](/wiki/File:Epic_Fury_Strike_compilation_\(997855\).webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:Epic_Fury_Strike_compilation_\(997855\).webm)

2 March: Montage of [US Central Command](/wiki/US_Central_Command "US Central Command") strikes

Trump issued letters to Congress leaders according to the 1973 [War Powers Resolution](/wiki/War_Powers_Resolution "War Powers Resolution").[\[253\]](#cite_note-mang-284)

On 2 March, the [US embassy in Kuwait](/wiki/US_embassy_in_Kuwait "US embassy in Kuwait") was struck and subsequently closed indefinitely; no casualties were reported.[\[254\]](#cite_note-285)[\[255\]](#cite_note-Reals-286) The US-flagged tanker *Stena Imperative* and the Honduras-flagged tanker *Athe Nova* were also struck.[\[256\]](#cite_note-287) A senior official and advisor to the IRGC commander said he would set fire to any ship coming through the Strait of Hormuz, and added that no oil will leave the area.[\[257\]](#cite_note-288)

Qatar shot down two [Iranian Su-24 bombers](/wiki/Sukhoi_Su-24 "Sukhoi Su-24"), making it the first nation to shoot down an Iranian aircraft in the conflict.[\[258\]](#cite_note-289) The Qatari Ministry of Defense announced that [Ras Laffan Industrial City](/wiki/Ras_Laffan_Industrial_City "Ras Laffan Industrial City") and [Mesaieed Industrial Area](/wiki/Mesaieed_Industrial_Area "Mesaieed Industrial Area") were struck by two Iranian drones.[\[259\]](#cite_note-bloomberg4march-290) On 6 March, it was reported that according to satellite imagery analysis by both *[Bloomberg](/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News")* and the Energy Economics and Society Research Institute in Tokyo, Ras Laffan, the main gas facility in Qatar, appeared to have not been damaged before the "unprecedented shutdown" which sent fuel prices higher.[\[260\]](#cite_note-291)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Attack_on_Sanandaj_Residential_Areas_1.jpg/250px-Attack_on_Sanandaj_Residential_Areas_1.jpg)](/wiki/File:Attack_on_Sanandaj_Residential_Areas_1.jpg)

2 March: Damage to residential buildings in [Sanandaj](/wiki/Sanandaj "Sanandaj"), Iranian Kurdistan

The United States and Israel attacked the [Natanz Nuclear Facility](/wiki/Natanz_Nuclear_Facility "Natanz Nuclear Facility")[\[261\]](#cite_note-292) and the Iranian media reported damage to the Khatam-al-Anbia and Gandhi hospitals.[\[262\]](#cite_note-293) A [friendly fire](/wiki/Friendly_fire "Friendly fire") incident took place when the pilot of an [F/A-18](/wiki/F/A-18 "F/A-18") of the [Kuwait Air Force](/wiki/Kuwait_Air_Force "Kuwait Air Force") shot down three US [F-15E](/wiki/F-15E "F-15E") fighters.[\[263\]](#cite_note-294)[\[264\]](#cite_note-295)[\[265\]](#cite_note-296)[\[255\]](#cite_note-Reals-286) Israel and Hezbollah exchanged strikes.[\[266\]](#cite_note-Kleinbaum-2026-297) Hezbollah began firing rockets and missiles on Israel in retaliation for the killing of Khamenei.[\[267\]](#cite_note-298)[\[268\]](#cite_note-299) Hezbollah later claimed that the attack was a "defensive act" after over a year of Israeli [attacks](/wiki/Hezbollah%E2%80%93Israel_conflict_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)") despite [a 2024 truce](/wiki/2024_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire_agreement "2024 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire agreement").[\[269\]](#cite_note-300) It added that it restarted fighting to force Israel to stop its aggression and evacuate from [seized Lebanese territories](/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Lebanese_conflict "Israeli–Lebanese conflict"), emphasizing that the move was unrelated to the war.[\[270\]](#cite_note-301)

Lebanon banned military activities by Hezbollah after the attacks.[\[271\]](#cite_note-302) An IDF spokesperson issued an emergency statement stating that the attack is to be considered "an official declaration of war by Hezbollah", vowing to "neutralize" the threat.[\[266\]](#cite_note-Kleinbaum-2026-297) Israel struck [southern Lebanon](/wiki/Southern_Lebanon "Southern Lebanon"),[\[272\]](#cite_note-303)[\[273\]](#cite_note-304)[\[274\]](#cite_note-305) Beirut, and the [Beqaa Valley](/wiki/Beqaa_Valley "Beqaa Valley").[\[266\]](#cite_note-Kleinbaum-2026-297) The IDF said that it killed the head of Hezbollah's intelligence headquarters [Hussein Makled](/w/index.php?title=Hussein_Makled&action=edit&redlink=1 "Hussein Makled (page does not exist)") in the strikes.[\[275\]](#cite_note-306)[\[276\]](#cite_note-307) In Lebanon, the IDF killed Adham Adnan al-Othman, the head of Palestinian Islamic Jihad's armed wing, [Al-Quds Brigades](/wiki/Al-Quds_Brigades "Al-Quds Brigades"), in Lebanon.[\[277\]](#cite_note-308)

The Royal Air Force station at [Akrotiri](/wiki/RAF_Akrotiri "RAF Akrotiri"), Cyprus, was targeted by a drone strike around midnight local time, with one causing minor damage.[\[278\]](#cite_note-309)[\[279\]](#cite_note-310)[\[280\]](#cite_note-311)[\[281\]](#cite_note-312) Another strike on Cyprus led to [Greece](/wiki/Greece "Greece") announcing that they would deploy frigates and [F-16s](/wiki/F-16 "F-16") to defend Cyprus from any further strikes by Iran.[\[282\]](#cite_note-313) The pro-Iran militant group [Guardians of the Blood Brigade](/wiki/Iraqi_Guardians_of_Blood_Brigades "Iraqi Guardians of Blood Brigades") claimed responsibility for attacks on the US [Victory Base](/wiki/Victory_Base_Complex "Victory Base Complex") near [Baghdad International Airport](/wiki/Baghdad_International_Airport "Baghdad International Airport") and [Erbil](/wiki/Erbil "Erbil"), [Kurdistan Region](/wiki/Kurdistan_Region "Kurdistan Region"), Iraq.[\[50\]](#cite_note-Stepansky-2026-72)[\[283\]](#cite_note-314)[\[284\]](#cite_note-315) The [Islamic Resistance in Iraq](/wiki/Islamic_Resistance_in_Iraq "Islamic Resistance in Iraq") claimed responsibility for over 23 drone strikes on US assets in Erbil.[\[285\]](#cite_note-316)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Attack_around_Enghelab_Square_1.jpg/250px-Attack_around_Enghelab_Square_1.jpg)](/wiki/File:Attack_around_Enghelab_Square_1.jpg)

3 March: [Enghelab Square](/wiki/Enghelab_Square "Enghelab Square"), Tehran

On 3 March, US and Israeli strikes reportedly destroyed the [Supreme National Security Council](/wiki/Supreme_National_Security_Council "Supreme National Security Council") (SNSC) headquarters,[\[286\]](#cite_note-317) the [Expediency Discernment Council](/wiki/Expediency_Discernment_Council "Expediency Discernment Council") building in Tehran,[\[287\]](#cite_note-318) and what Israeli officials described as an underground nuclear weapons facility called Min Zadai.[\[288\]](#cite_note-319) The proximity of these strikes to the [Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant](/wiki/Bushehr_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant") (about 12 km (7.5 mi) away) prompted the Russian agency [Rosatom](/wiki/Rosatom "Rosatom") to suspend construction on new units and evacuate non-essential staff due to a loss of communication with Iranian officials.[\[289\]](#cite_note-320)

US officials said US forces severely damaged Iran's naval capabilities, mainly in the Gulf of Oman, where several Iranian warships have reportedly been destroyed and key bases hit.[\[290\]](#cite_note-321)[\[291\]](#cite_note-322) Debris from an airstrike damaged [Golestan Palace](/wiki/Golestan_Palace "Golestan Palace"), a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site"),[\[292\]](#cite_note-323) causing UNESCO to issue a statement that damaging UNESCO property is against international law.[\[293\]](#cite_note-324)

Israel Katz [authorized a ground invasion of Lebanon](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war") on 3 March.[\[294\]](#cite_note-325)[\[295\]](#cite_note-326) They were later followed by a ground incursion in southern Lebanon with forces from the [91st Division](/wiki/91st_Division_\(Israel\) "91st Division (Israel)") with the goal to establish a "security layer" for the Israeli residents of northern settlements against Hezbollah, expecting to destroy their infrastructure in the [Israel-Lebanon border](/wiki/Israel-Lebanon_border "Israel-Lebanon border"). The [Lebanese government](/wiki/Lebanese_government "Lebanese government") reported that such Israeli [preventive attacks](/wiki/Preventive_attack "Preventive attack") reached [Kfarkela](/wiki/Kfarkela "Kfarkela") and [Qouzah](/wiki/Al-Qaouzah "Al-Qaouzah"), provoking the [Lebanese army](/wiki/Lebanese_army "Lebanese army") to do a redeployment from newly established border posts amid escalating Israeli activity in violation of the [2024 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire agreement](/wiki/2024_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire_agreement "2024 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire agreement").[\[296\]](#cite_note-327) Israel also reported that it killed [Daoud Alizadeh](/w/index.php?title=Daoud_Alizadeh&action=edit&redlink=1 "Daoud Alizadeh (page does not exist)"), the commander of the Quds Force's Lebanon branch, in Tehran.[\[297\]](#cite_note-328)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Attack_on_residential_homes_in_central_Tehran_1.jpg/250px-Attack_on_residential_homes_in_central_Tehran_1.jpg)](/wiki/File:Attack_on_residential_homes_in_central_Tehran_1.jpg)

4 March: Buildings in Tehran damaged by US-Israeli strikes

Western diplomats and other sources told *[The Jerusalem Post](/wiki/The_Jerusalem_Post "The Jerusalem Post")* that Qatar had struck Iran after Iran had attempted to strike Doha's airport and Qatar shot down two Iranian [Su-24](/wiki/Su-24 "Su-24") bombers;[\[298\]](#cite_note-wsj3march-329) [Channel 12](/wiki/Channel_12_\(Israel\) "Channel 12 (Israel)") also reported Qatari strikes.[\[299\]](#cite_note-330) Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson [Majed al-Ansari](/wiki/Majed_al-Ansari "Majed al-Ansari") denied the accusation that Qatar had joined the "campaign targeting Iran".[\[300\]](#cite_note-331) An IRGC general warned it would hit all economic hubs in the Middle East,[\[301\]](#cite_note-332)[\[302\]](#cite_note-333) and Abbas Araghchi said that any defensive European military involvement would be considered an act of war.[\[303\]](#cite_note-334)[\[304\]](#cite_note-335)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Operation-Roaring-Lion-0011.jpg/250px-Operation-Roaring-Lion-0011.jpg)](/wiki/File:Operation-Roaring-Lion-0011.jpg)

An Israeli Air Force [F-35I](/wiki/F-35I "F-35I") "Adir" shot down an Iranian [Yak-130](/wiki/Yak-130 "Yak-130"), the first kill of a crewed aircraft by an [F-35](/wiki/F-35 "F-35").

On 4 March, US secretary of state Marco Rubio announced that the US-Israeli attacks on Iran would increase in their intensity.[\[305\]](#cite_note-336) Israel attacks hit the [Basij](/wiki/Basij "Basij") headquarters.[\[306\]](#cite_note-337) [Mojtaba Khamenei](/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei "Mojtaba Khamenei") survived an airstrike.[\[307\]](#cite_note-338) The IDF announced that an [F-35I](/wiki/F-35I "F-35I") "Adir" shot down a Russian-made Iranian [Yak-130](/wiki/Yak-130 "Yak-130") fighter jet over Tehran, the first time that an F-35 has ever shot down a crewed fighter jet in air-to-air combat and the first time the Israeli Air Force shot down an aircraft since 1985.[\[308\]](#cite_note-339)

Iran launched strikes against the [Al Udeid Air Base](/wiki/Al_Udeid_Air_Base "Al Udeid Air Base"),[\[309\]](#cite_note-340) as well as [Aramco's Ras Tanura](/wiki/2026_Aramco_refinery_attack "2026 Aramco refinery attack") oil refining facility.[\[310\]](#cite_note-341) The United States ordered the evacuation of non-essential workers in Cyprus in anticipation of Iranian strikes and issued a travel warning for the country.[\[311\]](#cite_note-342)\[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*\][\[312\]](#cite_note-343) A ballistic missile launched from Iranian territory was intercepted by [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") integrated air defense systems as it entered Turkish airspace, marking a significant escalation in the regional conflict.[\[313\]](#cite_note-344) Turkey asserted its right to self-defense after the missile landed in [Dörtyol](/wiki/D%C3%B6rtyol "Dörtyol"), [Hatay Province](/wiki/Hatay_Province "Hatay Province"),[\[314\]](#cite_note-345) and NATO secretary general [Mark Rutte](/wiki/Mark_Rutte "Mark Rutte") stated that the alliance was committed to defending Turkey.[\[315\]](#cite_note-346)

[](/wiki/File:Indian_Ocean_Iranian_vessel_\(998184\).webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:Indian_Ocean_Iranian_vessel_\(998184\).webm)

4 March: [USS *Charlotte*](/wiki/USS_Charlotte_\(SSN-766\) "USS Charlotte (SSN-766)") [torpedoed](/wiki/Sinking_of_IRIS_Dena "Sinking of IRIS Dena") [IRIS *Dena*](/wiki/IRIS_Dena "IRIS Dena")

An Iranian Navy frigate, [IRIS *Dena*](/wiki/IRIS_Dena "IRIS Dena"), [was sunk](/wiki/Sinking_of_IRIS_Dena "Sinking of IRIS Dena") in the Indian Ocean by [United States Navy](/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") submarine [USS *Charlotte*](/wiki/USS_Charlotte_\(SSN-766\) "USS Charlotte (SSN-766)"), about 40 nautical miles (74 km; 46 mi) south of [Galle](/wiki/Galle "Galle"), Sri Lanka. The vessel was returning to Iran following its participation in the [International Fleet Review 2026](/wiki/International_Fleet_Review_2026 "International Fleet Review 2026") and the multilateral [Exercise MILAN](/wiki/Milan_\(naval_exercise\) "Milan (naval exercise)") at [Visakhapatnam](/wiki/Visakhapatnam "Visakhapatnam"), India.[\[316\]](#cite_note-347)[\[317\]](#cite_note-348)[\[318\]](#cite_note-349) The exercise required participating ships not to carry any ammunition, and the US likely knew the *Dena* was defenseless, since it also sent a maritime patrol aircraft to participate.[\[319\]](#cite_note-350) It was the first ship sunk by a submarine in active combat since the [Falklands War](/wiki/Falklands_War "Falklands War"), and the first by an American submarine since [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[\[af\]](#cite_note-Cheonan-353)[\[322\]](#cite_note-354) According to the Iranian army, 104 Iranians were killed and 32 were injured from this attack.[\[323\]](#cite_note-355)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Armada_Espa%C3%B1ola_F105_Crist%C3%B3bal_Col%C3%B3n.jpg/250px-Armada_Espa%C3%B1ola_F105_Crist%C3%B3bal_Col%C3%B3n.jpg)](/wiki/File:Armada_Espa%C3%B1ola_F105_Crist%C3%B3bal_Col%C3%B3n.jpg)

The frigate [*Cristóbal Colón*](/wiki/Spanish_frigate_Crist%C3%B3bal_Col%C3%B3n "Spanish frigate Cristóbal Colón"), sent by Spain to protect Cyprus from aerial threats

The government of Azerbaijan said on 5 March that [two drones from Iran struck](/wiki/2026_alleged_Iranian_strikes_on_Azerbaijan "2026 alleged Iranian strikes on Azerbaijan") Azerbaijan's [Nakhchivan exclave](/wiki/Nakhchivan_exclave "Nakhchivan exclave")[\[324\]](#cite_note-Reuters-2026b-356) damaging an airport and injuring two civilians.[\[325\]](#cite_note-357) Keir Starmer confirmed that the UK's bases on Cyprus would be used to defend the airspace of Jordan from Iranian drones,[\[326\]](#cite_note-358)[\[327\]](#cite_note-359) while Italy, the Netherlands and Spain confirmed that they would be sending warships to defend Cyprus.[\[328\]](#cite_note-360)[\[329\]](#cite_note-361)[\[330\]](#cite_note-362) Ireland stated that they would be willing to protect Cyprus and join the European defense coalition that had mobilized around the island if requested.[\[331\]](#cite_note-363) The IDF killed Hamas official Wassim Attallah al-Ali in [Beddawi](/wiki/Beddawi "Beddawi"), Lebanon.[\[332\]](#cite_note-364)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Airstrike_on_the_residential_town_of_Shahid_Boroujerdi_20_Avash.webp/250px-Airstrike_on_the_residential_town_of_Shahid_Boroujerdi_20_Avash.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Airstrike_on_the_residential_town_of_Shahid_Boroujerdi_20_Avash.webp)

6 March: The aftermath of US-Israeli airstrikes in Tehran

Trump said on 6 March that there are "no time limits" for how long the war will continue for,[\[333\]](#cite_note-365) and Hegseth stated that the war has "only just begun".[\[334\]](#cite_note-366) The Iranian tanker [IRIS *Bushehr*](/wiki/IRIS_Bushehr "IRIS Bushehr") was interned by the [Sri Lanka Navy](/wiki/Sri_Lanka_Navy "Sri Lanka Navy"), marking the first instance of a warship being interned in a neutral country since World War II.[\[335\]](#cite_note-367)

### Second week (7–13 March)

Further information: [2026 Qeshm Island desalination plant attack](/wiki/2026_Qeshm_Island_desalination_plant_attack "2026 Qeshm Island desalination plant attack") and [2026 Iranian supreme leader election](/wiki/2026_Iranian_supreme_leader_election "2026 Iranian supreme leader election")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/P20260307DT-1619_The_Dignified_Transfer_of_Remains_of_Six_U.S._Soldiers.jpg/250px-P20260307DT-1619_The_Dignified_Transfer_of_Remains_of_Six_U.S._Soldiers.jpg)](/wiki/File:P20260307DT-1619_The_Dignified_Transfer_of_Remains_of_Six_U.S._Soldiers.jpg)

Six dead US soldiers from the [2026 Port Shuaiba drone attack](/wiki/2026_Port_Shuaiba_drone_attack "2026 Port Shuaiba drone attack") are transferred to the US on 7 March 2026.

On 7 March, the US sent a third aircraft carrier, [USS *George H. W. Bush*](/wiki/USS_George_H._W._Bush "USS George H. W. Bush"), to the Middle East.[\[336\]](#cite_note-368)[\[337\]](#cite_note-369)[\[338\]](#cite_note-370) The British aircraft carrier [HMS *Prince of Wales*](/wiki/HMS_Prince_of_Wales_\(R09\) "HMS Prince of Wales (R09)") was placed on advanced readiness to defend British interests in the region.[\[339\]](#cite_note-371) Pezeshkian told reporters on 7 March that Iran would stop striking neighbors from 7 March onwards unless an attack originated from there.[\[340\]](#cite_note-372) Despite this, [Dubai International Airport](/wiki/Dubai_International_Airport "Dubai International Airport") was later attacked by Iranian drones.[\[341\]](#cite_note-373) [NDTV](/wiki/NDTV "NDTV") reported that following a week's hostilities, Iran might only have around one thousand ballistic missiles left.[\[342\]](#cite_note-374) On 7 March, ballistic missiles were fired from Bahrain toward Iran, likely by US forces.[\[343\]](#cite_note-Missiles_fired_from_Bahrain-375)

On 8 March, Khamenei's second son, [Mojtaba](/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei "Mojtaba Khamenei"), was [designated](/wiki/2026_Iranian_supreme_leader_election "2026 Iranian supreme leader election") as Iran's new supreme leader.[\[344\]](#cite_note-376) Also on 8 March, US Central Command posted a message on [X](/wiki/X_\(social_network\) "X (social network)") in Persian and Arabic which "strongly urge\[s\] civilians in Iran to stay at home" and alleging that "\[t\]he Iranian regime is knowingly endangering innocent lives by using heavily populated civilian areas to conduct military operations, including launching one-way attack drones and ballistic missiles".[\[345\]](#cite_note-377)

Israeli airstrikes hit some of Iran's oil storage facilities, killing four people.[\[346\]](#cite_note-378) Strikes on fuel depots near Tehran caused a "river of fire" to pour out along the streets in the surrounding area,[\[347\]](#cite_note-379) and the city became engulfed in a cloud of thick black smoke, causing black toxic [acidic](/wiki/Acid_rain "Acid rain") rain to fall in the surrounding area.[\[348\]](#cite_note-b673-380) Residents were advised by Iranian authorities to stay indoors, wear masks when outside, and conserve food and fuel.[\[349\]](#cite_note-381) Kuwait reported that two of its officers were killed while performing duties.[\[350\]](#cite_note-382)[\[351\]](#cite_note-383) The [Saudi Civil Defense](/wiki/Saudi_Civil_Defense "Saudi Civil Defense") agency said that a strike on a compound in [Al-Kharj](/wiki/Al-Kharj "Al-Kharj") killed two people and injured 12 others.[\[352\]](#cite_note-384) [US Central Command](/wiki/US_Central_Command "US Central Command") announced the death of a seventh US service member from an Iranian attack.[\[353\]](#cite_note-385)

The United Kingdom's Ministry of Defense confirmed that its forces had intercepted an Iranian drone headed towards Iraq. Additionally, the Ministry declared their intention to send a [Merlin helicopter](/wiki/Merlin_helicopter "Merlin helicopter") to the region to help aid in detecting future aerial threats.[\[354\]](#cite_note-386) According to the [Iranian Red Crescent Society](/wiki/Iranian_Red_Crescent_Society "Iranian Red Crescent Society"), a total of 65 schools and 32 medical facilities (such as hospitals and pharmacies) have been targeted since the war started, and more than 10,000 civilian sites have been damaged.[\[355\]](#cite_note-387) On 9 March, NATO confirmed the interception of a second ballistic missile over Turkish air space,[\[356\]](#cite_note-388) landing in the area of [Gaziantep](/wiki/Gaziantep "Gaziantep").[\[357\]](#cite_note-389) Meanwhile, Turkey deployed six F-16s and air defence systems to [Northern Cyprus](/wiki/Northern_Cyprus "Northern Cyprus") to ensure its security.[\[358\]](#cite_note-390)

Trump claimed that "the war is very complete, pretty much", after speaking with Russian president Vladimir Putin,[\[359\]](#cite_note-391) and said "we already won the war in many ways."[\[360\]](#cite_note-392) He additionally claimed that the Strait of Hormuz was open but also expressed interest in taking it over from Iran.[\[361\]](#cite_note-393) Trump later went back on some of his comments during a press conference held later that day, supporting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in stating that the war was just the "beginning of building a new country" and that it would end "soon".[\[362\]](#cite_note-394) However, Trump also said that the US will have the "most intense day" of strikes on Tuesday.[\[363\]](#cite_note-395) Following Syrian president Ahmed al-Sharaa's support for the Lebanon's objective to disarm Hezbollah,[\[364\]](#cite_note-Middle_East_Eye-2-396) the group [targeted](/wiki/2026_strikes_on_Syria_during_the_Iran_War "2026 strikes on Syria during the Iran War") the city of [Inkhil](/wiki/Inkhil "Inkhil") in Syria.[\[365\]](#cite_note-397) About a dozen [B-1B bombers](/wiki/Rockwell_B-1_Lancer "Rockwell B-1 Lancer") arrived at bases in Europe. Five landed at the Fairford Royal Air Force base, UK, joining three [B-52 bombers](/wiki/B-52_bombers "B-52 bombers"), while three others were redirected to [Ramstein Air Base](/wiki/Ramstein_Air_Base "Ramstein Air Base"), Germany.[\[366\]](#cite_note-398)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Strait_of_Hormuz_Transits.webp/250px-Strait_of_Hormuz_Transits.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Strait_of_Hormuz_Transits.webp)

Strait of Hormuz transits dropped significantly since the start of the war.[\[367\]](#cite_note-399)

[GPS jamming](/wiki/GPS_jamming "GPS jamming") of uncertain origin has disrupted navigation of ships near the Strait of Hormuz, which may lead to disastrous accidents for oil tankers.[\[368\]](#cite_note-400) The [United States Department of State](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") (supported by [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"))[\[369\]](#cite_note-401) designated the [Muslim Brotherhood](/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood "Muslim Brotherhood") branch in [Sudan](/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") (a [Sudanese Islamist](/wiki/Sudanese_Islamist "Sudanese Islamist") organization) as a [terrorist organization](/wiki/Terrorist_organization "Terrorist organization") due to its nexus with the [Axis of Resistance](/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance "Axis of Resistance").[\[370\]](#cite_note-402)\[*[failed verification](/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")*\] Members of their militia fought alongside the IRGC due to the contacts established with the [Al-Bara' ibn Malik Battalion](/wiki/Al-Bara%27_ibn_Malik_Battalion "Al-Bara' ibn Malik Battalion") during the [Iranian intervention in Sudan](/w/index.php?title=Iranian_intervention_in_Sudan&action=edit&redlink=1 "Iranian intervention in Sudan (page does not exist)").[\[371\]](#cite_note-403) On 10 March, a senior IRGC commander stated that Iran was only firing missiles with payloads of 1,000 kg or more.[\[372\]](#cite_note-ndtv10march-404) AFP reported that Iran's attacks were the "most intense and heaviest" since the start of the war.[\[373\]](#cite_note-405) This shows a shift in tactics from saturating air defences to high-impact penetration strikes.[\[372\]](#cite_note-ndtv10march-404) On the same day, top American general [Dan Caine](/wiki/Dan_Caine "Dan Caine") acknowledged that Iran was fighting back, but not harder than the U.S. expected before the war.[\[374\]](#cite_note-406)

Following the Syrian presidency's support for the disarmament of Hezbollah and a campaign of mobilization by the Syrian army on the Lebanese border,[\[364\]](#cite_note-Middle_East_Eye-2-396)[\[375\]](#cite_note-407) shells from Lebanon landed in the town of [Serghaya](/wiki/Serghaya "Serghaya"), 20 km (12 mi) from Damascus where the [Syrian Armed Forces](/wiki/Syrian_Armed_Forces "Syrian Armed Forces") forces presided.[\[376\]](#cite_note-408) The strikes were confirmed by the Operations Authority of the [Syrian Army](/wiki/Syrian_Army "Syrian Army").[\[377\]](#cite_note-409) Later in the day, Israel issued an urgent evacuation notice to southern suburbs of Beirut.[\[378\]](#cite_note-410)

US admiral [Brad Cooper](/wiki/Brad_Cooper_\(admiral\) "Brad Cooper (admiral)") reported that Iran's ballistic missile launch rate fell 90% from day one of the war and their drone launch rate fell 83%.[\[379\]](#cite_note-411) Defense analyst AJ Jaff reported that the missile launch rate fell 92% (480 to 40) and the drone launch rate fell 92% (720 to 60).[\[380\]](#cite_note-jpost10march-412) On 11 March 11 B-1 and three B-52 US bombers were deployed to [RAF Fairford](/wiki/RAF_Fairford "RAF Fairford") in the UK, where long-range photography showed bombs being prepared for loading. This followed US war secretary Pete Hegseth's statement that it was the "most intense day of strikes inside Iran", though the targets of the mission remain unknown.[\[381\]](#cite_note-413)

A branch of [Bank Sepah](/wiki/Bank_Sepah "Bank Sepah") in Tehran was hit by a strike, prompting the IRGC to warn that in the future, they could retaliate by striking US or Israeli banks in the region.[\[382\]](#cite_note-414) Iran hit [Stryker](/wiki/Stryker_Corporation "Stryker Corporation"), a US-based medical supply company with a cyber attack.[\[383\]](#cite_note-415) On 12 March, [UNICEF](/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") reported that more than 1,100 children were injured or killed (200 reportedly killed in Iran, 91 in Lebanon, 4 in Israel, and 1 in Kuwait), hundreds of thousands displaced, and millions unable to attend schools from the violence of the war since it started. It also noted that these numbers will likely increase.[\[384\]](#cite_note-416)

Iranian deputy [intelligence minister](/wiki/Ministry_of_Intelligence_\(Iran\) "Ministry of Intelligence (Iran)") Akbar Ghaffari was killed in an airstrike.[\[385\]](#cite_note-417) An Iranian attack set two oil tankers on fire off the Iraqi coast, killing one person and prompting Iraq to suspend all oil terminal operations.[\[386\]](#cite_note-418) The historical [Safavid](/wiki/Safavid "Safavid")\-era building of [Rashk-e Jenan](/wiki/Rashk-e_Jenan "Rashk-e Jenan"), also known as the Rashk Palace, was destroyed by direct US-Israeli strikes.[\[387\]](#cite_note-419) Other buildings that were damaged according to Ruhollah Seyed al-Asgari, the deputy director of cultural heritage for Isfahan province, include [Chehel Sotoun](/wiki/Chehel_Sotoun "Chehel Sotoun") pavilion, the [Rakib Khaneh Mansion](/w/index.php?title=Rakib_Khaneh_Mansion&action=edit&redlink=1 "Rakib Khaneh Mansion (page does not exist)"), the [Timurid Hall](/w/index.php?title=Timurid_Hall&action=edit&redlink=1 "Timurid Hall (page does not exist)"), the [Ashraf Hall](/w/index.php?title=Ashraf_Hall&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ashraf Hall (page does not exist)") and the windows of [Ali Qapu](/wiki/Ali_Qapu "Ali Qapu") palace.[\[388\]](#cite_note-420) Many of the affected buildings and monuments were legally protected by the [Blue Shield International](/wiki/Blue_Shield_International "Blue Shield International"),[\[389\]](#cite_note-421) which called damaging such sites a war crime.[\[390\]](#cite_note-422) Six French soldiers were injured in a drone strike at a base in Mala Qara, Iraqi Kurdistan. French president [Emmanuel Macron](/wiki/Emmanuel_Macron "Emmanuel Macron") announced on 13 March that one French soldier was killed in the attack.[\[391\]](#cite_note-lm13march-423)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Salalah_Port_Ablaze.jpg/250px-Salalah_Port_Ablaze.jpg)](/wiki/File:Salalah_Port_Ablaze.jpg)

Satellite imagery of black smoke rising from the [Port of Salalah](/wiki/Port_of_Salalah "Port of Salalah") on 13 March during the [2026 Iranian strikes on Oman](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Oman "2026 Iranian strikes on Oman").

Also on 13 March, to help deal with the economic costs of the war, the US temporarily lifted restrictions on the sale of Russian oil. However, oil prices have barely been affected by this.[\[392\]](#cite_note-Cooper-424) Iran announced a coordinated offensive by IRGC Navy, the Iranian Army, and Hezbollah against Israel and US bases.[\[393\]](#cite_note-425) Israel reported that 58 people have been hospitalized due to injuries following a missile strike.[\[392\]](#cite_note-Cooper-424) Iran again targeted Gulf countries with missiles and drones, causing oil prices to rise. Bahrain reported attacks on fuel tanks. Two people were injured when a "hostile drone" struck a residential building in Kuwait. The Kuwaiti authorities also stated that defense equipment and the country's main international airport were attacked, and six power lines were reported to have gone out of service. AFP reported that explosions were heard in downtown Dubai. At the same time, the British Maritime Trade Operations Agency said a container ship was attacked 35 nautical miles (65 kilometers) north of Jebel Ali in the UAE. According to Al Jazeera Arabic, sirens went off in every city across Jordan.[\[394\]](#cite_note-426)

For the third time in the war, ballistic missiles entered Turkish air space and were intercepted, with explosions heard in the proximity of the city of [Adana](/wiki/Adana "Adana") as well as sirens from Incirlik Air Base.[\[395\]](#cite_note-427) Israel struck several IRGC checkpoints in Iran. According to [Reuters](/wiki/Reuters "Reuters"), Israel attacked the checkpoints after receiving tip-offs by on the ground informants. Reuters also reported Israel had struck positions of the Basij used to suppress Iranian protests.[\[396\]](#cite_note-428)

### Third week (14–20 March)

Further information: [2026 Kharg Island attack](/wiki/2026_Kharg_Island_attack "2026 Kharg Island attack"), [Assassination of Ali Larijani](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Larijani "Assassination of Ali Larijani"), and [2026 South Pars field attack](/wiki/2026_South_Pars_field_attack "2026 South Pars field attack")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/%D8%AC%D8%B2%DB%8C%D8%B1%D9%87_%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%DA%A9-_%D8%B7%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%B9%D8%AA_%D9%88_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%B9%D8%AA-10.jpg/250px-%D8%AC%D8%B2%DB%8C%D8%B1%D9%87_%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%DA%A9-_%D8%B7%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%B9%D8%AA_%D9%88_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%B9%D8%AA-10.jpg)](/wiki/File:%D8%AC%D8%B2%DB%8C%D8%B1%D9%87_%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%DA%A9-_%D8%B7%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%B9%D8%AA_%D9%88_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%B9%D8%AA-10.jpg)

[Kharg Island](/wiki/Kharg_Island "Kharg Island") in 2015; the fires on the towers are a normal part of oil refining.

As of the third week, analysts found little evidence of significant defections or desertions in the Iranian military;[\[ag\]](#cite_note-438) military defections have been considered a necessary condition for [regime change](/wiki/Regime_change "Regime change").[\[406\]](#cite_note-439) The US [conducted a large-scale attack](/wiki/2026_Kharg_Island_attack "2026 Kharg Island attack") on [Kharg Island](/wiki/Kharg_Island "Kharg Island"), a key oil export hub home to 90 percent of Iran's oil exports. Over 90 military sites were targeted while the oil infrastructure was not targeted "for reasons of decency", according to Trump. Oil prices have risen over 40 percent since the start of the war.[\[407\]](#cite_note-440) According to CENTCOM, around 90 military targets were struck, while the island's oil infrastructure was not targeted.[\[408\]](#cite_note-441) On 14 March, [Kata'ib Hezbollah](/wiki/Kata%27ib_Hezbollah "Kata'ib Hezbollah") security commander Abu Ali al-Askari was killed in an airstrike in Baghdad, according to the group.[\[409\]](#cite_note-442)

The first two floors of the [Royal Tulip Al Rasheed Hotel](/wiki/Royal_Tulip_Al_Rasheed_Hotel "Royal Tulip Al Rasheed Hotel") in Baghdad's [Green Zone](/wiki/Green_Zone "Green Zone") were hit by a drone whilst hosting a European Union and Saudi Arabian delegation. The attack was not claimed by anyone; however, due to the proximity of a similar attack that had happened 48 hours earlier on the US embassy in Baghdad, there were suspicions of it being an Iranian attack.[\[410\]](#cite_note-443)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Missile_interception_fragments_of_an_Iranian_missile_hit_Haifa_oil_refineries_in_Haifa_Bay%2C_March%2C_19_2026.jpg/250px-Missile_interception_fragments_of_an_Iranian_missile_hit_Haifa_oil_refineries_in_Haifa_Bay%2C_March%2C_19_2026.jpg)](/wiki/File:Missile_interception_fragments_of_an_Iranian_missile_hit_Haifa_oil_refineries_in_Haifa_Bay,_March,_19_2026.jpg)

An Iranian missile hit Haifa oil refineries in [Haifa Bay](/wiki/Haifa_Bay "Haifa Bay"), 19 March 2026

On 16 March, both China and US-aligned [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") nations in Europe rejected Trump's call to provide military support to reopen the [Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz "Strait of Hormuz").[\[411\]](#cite_note-444)[\[412\]](#cite_note-445) Trump rebuked his NATO allies, calling their decision a "very foolish mistake".[\[413\]](#cite_note-446) On 17 March, Trump made a statement on [Truth Social](/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social") renouncing NATO's assistance, and unexpectedly, US allies in the Indo-Pacific, namely Japan, South Korea, and [Australia](/wiki/Australian_involvement_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Australian involvement in the 2026 Iran war"), for refusing to join US-led attacks on [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") during the war.[\[414\]](#cite_note-447)[\[415\]](#cite_note-448)[\[416\]](#cite_note-449)[\[417\]](#cite_note-450) In the same statement, Trump declared that the United States "\[does\] not need the help of anyone" regarding the war.[\[418\]](#cite_note-451)
