In the early morning of 17 March, several senior Iranian officials, including [Ali Larijani](/wiki/Ali_Larijani "Ali Larijani") and Basij chief [Gholamreza Soleimani](/wiki/Gholamreza_Soleimani "Gholamreza Soleimani") were [targeted by Israeli airstrikes](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Larijani "Assassination of Ali Larijani").[\[419\]](#cite_note-Iran_International-2026-452)[\[420\]](#cite_note-453) Both their deaths were later confirmed by Iranian state media.[\[421\]](#cite_note-sk-454) In response, Iran launched a missile barrage that killed two Israeli civilians in [Ramat Gan](/wiki/Ramat_Gan "Ramat Gan").[\[422\]](#cite_note-455) The same day, Israel launched a ground invasion of [southern Lebanon](/wiki/Southern_Lebanon "Southern Lebanon").[\[423\]](#cite_note-456)

On 18 March, in a major escalation,[\[424\]](#cite_note-blowup-457) Israel [struck](/wiki/2026_South_Pars_field_attack "2026 South Pars field attack") the [South Pars natural gas field](/wiki/South_Pars/North_Dome_Gas-Condensate_field "South Pars/North Dome Gas-Condensate field") in the Persian Gulf and its neighboring refineries in Iran with US coordination.[\[425\]](#cite_note-oj-458) In retaliation, Iran attacked the world's largest LNG production facility in Qatar. Trump claimed he was not aware of the South Pars attack, promised that there would be no more Israeli attacks on Iranian oil infrastructure, and threatened Iran not to continue attacking Qatari energy infrastructure.[\[424\]](#cite_note-blowup-457)[\[426\]](#cite_note-459) On the same day, Israel said it had killed Iranian intelligence minister [Esmaeil Khatib](/wiki/Esmaeil_Khatib "Esmaeil Khatib") in an overnight airstrike.[\[427\]](#cite_note-460) Pezeshkian confirmed Khatib's killing on the same day.[\[428\]](#cite_note-461) A hair salon in [Beit Awwa](/wiki/Beit_Awwa "Beit Awwa") was [struck by a projectile](/wiki/2026_Beit_Awwa_salon_strike "2026 Beit Awwa salon strike"), killing four women and injuring six,[\[429\]](#cite_note-462) with Israeli authorities stating that it was most likely [cluster munitions](/wiki/Cluster_munitions "Cluster munitions") and Palestinian authorities saying it was an errant Israeli interceptor.[\[430\]](#cite_note-463)[\[431\]](#cite_note-464)

[](/wiki/File:F-35_Lightning_II_fighter_jet_hit_over_Iran_2026.webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:F-35_Lightning_II_fighter_jet_hit_over_Iran_2026.webm)

Video of suspected Iranian strike on a USAF F-35, released by [Tasnim News Agency](/wiki/Tasnim_News_Agency "Tasnim News Agency"), 19 March 2026, the first case of a damaged stealth fighter in combat

On 19 March, a US [F-35](/wiki/F-35 "F-35") made an emergency landing after a suspected hit by Iranian forces.[\[432\]](#cite_note-465)[\[433\]](#cite_note-cnn19march-466) A [BAZAN Group](/wiki/BAZAN_Group "BAZAN Group") refinery in Haifa was hit during a broader Iranian missile attack on the area as a retaliation for Israeli attacks on South Pars gas facilities.[\[434\]](#cite_note-467)[\[435\]](#cite_note-468) Netanyahu insisted that "You can't make a revolution from the air" and that "there must be a ground component — I won't share with you all the options", implying that there was a potential for limited assault operations involving soldiers on the ground in Iran.[\[436\]](#cite_note-469) The US began [an aerial campaign](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_campaign "2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign") against Iranian vessels and drones in the Strait of Hormuz as part of an effort to reopen it to international shipping.[\[437\]](#cite_note-470)

### Fourth week (21–27 March)

Further information: [2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_campaign "2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign")

Admiral [Brad Cooper](/wiki/Brad_Cooper_\(admiral\) "Brad Cooper (admiral)") said that the US military had so far struck more than 8,000 Iranian military targets, including 130 vessels.[\[438\]](#cite_note-471) On 21 March, the US conducted strikes on the [Natanz Nuclear Facility](/wiki/Natanz_Nuclear_Facility "Natanz Nuclear Facility") using [bunker buster](/wiki/Bunker_buster "Bunker buster") bombs to target the site.[\[439\]](#cite_note-472) Russia condemned the strikes on Natanz as a "blatant violation of international law," while the [International Atomic Energy Agency](/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") (IAEA) urged military restraint "to avoid any risk of a nuclear accident".[\[440\]](#cite_note-473) In response, Iran struck the southern Israeli town of [Dimona](/wiki/Dimona "Dimona"), injuring at least 78 people.[\[441\]](#cite_note-474) Iran said that it targeted the [Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center](/wiki/Shimon_Peres_Negev_Nuclear_Research_Center "Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center").[\[442\]](#cite_note-475)[\[443\]](#cite_note-476)

Citing unnamed US officials, CNN and *The Wall Street Journal* reported that Iran unsuccessfully attempted to strike the joint US–UK military base at [Diego Garcia](/wiki/Diego_Garcia "Diego Garcia") on the [Chagos Islands](/wiki/Chagos_Archipelago "Chagos Archipelago") in the [British Indian Ocean Territory](/wiki/British_Indian_Ocean_Territory "British Indian Ocean Territory").[\[444\]](#cite_note-477) The report said one of the missiles broke apart mid-flight, while another was intercepted by a [SM-3](/wiki/SM-3 "SM-3") air defence missile launched by a US warship.[\[445\]](#cite_note-478)[\[446\]](#cite_note-479) Israel said that Iran used a two-stage [intercontinental ballistic missile](/wiki/Intercontinental_ballistic_missile "Intercontinental ballistic missile") to target the island.[\[447\]](#cite_note-480)[\[448\]](#cite_note-481) Iran denied launching missiles towards Diego Garcia, saying that it was an Israeli false flag attack.[\[449\]](#cite_note-482) No evidence has been presented that the alleged Iranian missiles neared Diego Garcia or that one was intercepted.[\[450\]](#cite_note-483)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Operation-Roaring-Lion-0065.jpg/250px-Operation-Roaring-Lion-0065.jpg)](/wiki/File:Operation-Roaring-Lion-0065.jpg)

Israeli troops near the Lebanese border on 21 March 2026

The [Houthi movement](/wiki/Houthis "Houthis") in [Yemen](/wiki/Yemen "Yemen") warned that it would respond to any escalation against Iran, including [efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_campaign "2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign"). It specifically warned the two Arab countries offering to join the Strait of Hormuz campaign—Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates—that they "will be the first to lose in this battle".[\[451\]](#cite_note-484) The Houthis further threatened to join the war in the event that US allies joined the attack on Iran or if the US and Israel used the [Red Sea](/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea") to carry out operations.[\[452\]](#cite_note-485) Lebanon's government expelled the Iranian ambassador.[\[453\]](#cite_note-sl-486)

Trump issued an ultimatum to Iran, threatening to strike its [power plants](/wiki/Power_plants "Power plants") unless it opened the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours.[\[454\]](#cite_note-487) Iran doubled down, threatening to "completely" close the Strait of Hormuz and strike vital infrastructure across the region such as energy and [desalination](/wiki/Desalination "Desalination") facilities critical for drinking water.[\[455\]](#cite_note-488) [Iranian opposition](/wiki/Iranian_opposition "Iranian opposition") figure and former crown prince [Reza Pahlavi](/wiki/Reza_Pahlavi "Reza Pahlavi") called on Trump and Netanyahu to target the military while sparing civilian infrastructure which "Iranians will need to rebuild our country."[\[456\]](#cite_note-489) Halfway through the deadline, Trump announced that he was postponing strikes against Iranian power plants for five days,[\[457\]](#cite_note-490) and said the US was negotiating with Iran to end the war.[\[458\]](#cite_note-491) Iran denied the talks ever took place or were taking place and called the president "deceitful".[\[459\]](#cite_note-492) Iran rejected the 15-point peace plan presented by the US.[\[460\]](#cite_note-493)[\[461\]](#cite_note-494) Iran asserted that Lebanon must be included as part of a ceasefire deal, thereby making a ceasefire conditional on an end to the [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war") against Hezbollah.[\[462\]](#cite_note-495)

On 24 March, Israel or its allies shot down an Iranian missile crossing above Lebanon at high altitude, according to the Lebanese army, which also confirmed that the missile was not targeting Lebanon. This was the first time during the current conflict when a shootdown of an Iranian missile took place over Lebanese territory.[\[463\]](#cite_note-496)[\[464\]](#cite_note-497)

A US strike on the Habbaniya military base—which hosts units from the [Popular Mobilization Forces](/wiki/Popular_Mobilization_Forces "Popular Mobilization Forces")—in [Al Anbar Governorate](/wiki/Al_Anbar_Governorate "Al Anbar Governorate") killed seven members of the [Iraqi Armed Forces](/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces "Iraqi Armed Forces") and injured 13 others. In response, Iraqi prime minister [Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani](/wiki/Mohammed_Shia%27_al-Sudani "Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani") summoned the US embassy's [chargé d'affaires](/wiki/Charg%C3%A9_d%27affaires "Chargé d'affaires") in Baghdad.[\[465\]](#cite_note-498) Iranian state media threatened that Iran could seize Bahraini and Emirati territory if the US "makes any mistakes", while signaling its readiness to open a new front in Yemen by closing the [Bab al-Mandab](/wiki/Bab-el-Mandeb "Bab-el-Mandeb") with the [Houthis](/wiki/Houthis "Houthis").[\[466\]](#cite_note-499)[\[467\]](#cite_note-500) Israel said it killed Iran's top naval commander, [Alireza Tangsiri](/wiki/Alireza_Tangsiri "Alireza Tangsiri"), purportedly as part of an effort to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Katz said Tangsiri was "directly responsible" for the closure of.[\[468\]](#cite_note-501)[\[469\]](#cite_note-502)[\[470\]](#cite_note-503)

On 27 March, a day after Trump and Hegseth announced the "neutralization" of Iran's military, an Iranian missile and drone strike on [Prince Sultan Air Base](/wiki/Prince_Sultan_Air_Base "Prince Sultan Air Base") damaged several US refueling aircraft and injured at least 15 US soldiers. An [E-3 Sentry](/wiki/Boeing_E-3_Sentry "Boeing E-3 Sentry") was also damaged by the strike.[\[471\]](#cite_note-504)[\[472\]](#cite_note-505)[\[473\]](#cite_note-apnews27march-506) Military analyst Cedric Leighton described the attack as a "a serious blow to \[US\] surveillance capabilities".[\[474\]](#cite_note-507) Iran showed no signs of ceding its control over the Strait of Hormuz.[\[475\]](#cite_note-508) The same day, Iran blocked two Chinese ships from entering the strait and sought to formalize fees for ships passing through it.[\[476\]](#cite_note-509)[\[477\]](#cite_note-510) Despite pushes for talks, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz publicly vowed to "intensify and expand" Israeli attacks in Iran.[\[478\]](#cite_note-511) The same day, the [Shahid Khondab Heavy Water Complex](/wiki/IR-40 "IR-40") in Arak, which has in the past been used to test uranium enrichment, and the [Ardakan yellowcake production plant](/wiki/Nuclear_facilities_in_Iran#Ardakan "Nuclear facilities in Iran") in Yazd Province were confirmed to have been damaged in Israeli airstrikes.[\[479\]](#cite_note-struckmarch2026-512)[\[480\]](#cite_note-march2026struckairstrike-513)

### Fifth week (28 March – 3 April)

Further information: [2026 Houthi strikes on Israel](/wiki/2026_Houthi_strikes_on_Israel "2026 Houthi strikes on Israel") and [Karaj B1 bridge attack](/wiki/Karaj_B1_bridge_attack "Karaj B1 bridge attack")

The Houthis joined the war on 28 March [launching a ballistic missile](/wiki/2026_Houthi_strikes_on_Israel "2026 Houthi strikes on Israel") towards Israel.[\[481\]](#cite_note-514) The Houthis said that they had launched ballistic missiles targeting "sensitive" military sites in Israel, and vowed to continue the attacks "until the aggression on all resistance fronts stops". The missile was intercepted and no casualties were reported.[\[482\]](#cite_note-515) The Houthis subsequently launched a second missile at [Eilat](/wiki/Eilat "Eilat").[\[483\]](#cite_note-516) In response, the internationally recognized [Yemeni government](/wiki/Presidential_Leadership_Council "Presidential Leadership Council") condemned Iran's "frequent attempts to drag Yemen" into conflict "through its terrorist militias".[\[484\]](#cite_note-517) On the same day, 2,500 US marines from the [31st Marine Expeditionary Unit](/wiki/31st_Marine_Expeditionary_Unit "31st Marine Expeditionary Unit") arrived in the Middle East. They are intended to be part of the effort to open the Strait of Hormuz.[\[485\]](#cite_note-518)

[US Central Command](/wiki/US_Central_Command "US Central Command") stated that it had struck over 11,000 targets in Iran since the beginning of the war. On 28 March, joint US–Israeli airstrikes severely damaged several residential and civilian facilities, including the [Iran University of Science and Technology](/wiki/Iran_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Iran University of Science and Technology").[\[486\]](#cite_note-519) In response, Iran threatened to attack Israeli and American colleges across the Middle East.[\[487\]](#cite_note-520) Airstrikes also struck a 10,000-cubic-meter water reservoir in [Haftkel](/wiki/Haftkel "Haftkel"), in [Khuzestan province](/wiki/Khuzestan_province "Khuzestan province").[\[488\]](#cite_note-521)

An Iranian missile struck a chemical plant in the [Ne'ot Hovav](/wiki/Ne%27ot_Hovav "Ne'ot Hovav") industrial zone, injuring one person and causing fears of a hazardous leak.[\[489\]](#cite_note-522) A convoy of the Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces was seen entering [Khorramshahr](/wiki/Khorramshahr "Khorramshahr") in southwestern Iran.[\[490\]](#cite_note-iranintl28march-523) Eleven-year-old child soldier [Alireza Jafari](/wiki/Alireza_Jafari_\(child_soldier\) "Alireza Jafari (child soldier)") died following an Israeli drone strike.[\[491\]](#cite_note-524)

On 29 March, Trump stated that he would prefer to "take the oil in Iran". He proposed taking Iran's oil export center, [Kharg Island](/wiki/Kharg_Island "Kharg Island"), claiming that the United States could capture the territory "very easily", and implying that the US could occupy it for some time.[\[80\]](#cite_note-ft30march-105)

On 30 March, Trump said on Truth Social that if a deal was not reached soon and the Strait of Hormuz reopened, the US would conclude the war by destroying all of Iran's power plants, oil wells, Kharg Island, and possibly all its desalinization plants,[\[492\]](#cite_note-525) although the feasibility and strategic value of some of Trump's threats were contested.[\[493\]](#cite_note-526) On the same day Turkey and NATO intercepted the fourth missile directed towards Turkish territory. Iran denied firing a missile at Turkey, claiming that it was a [false flag](/wiki/False_flag "False flag") attack.[\[494\]](#cite_note-527)[\[495\]](#cite_note-528) The US began flying [B-52 bombers](/wiki/Boeing_B-52_Stratofortress "Boeing B-52 Stratofortress") over Iranian territory for the first time, indicating its confidence of [air supremacy](/wiki/Air_supremacy "Air supremacy") over Iran.[\[496\]](#cite_note-529) The US used bombers to target an ammunition depot and air base in [Isfahan](/wiki/Isfahan "Isfahan"), causing vast explosions.[\[497\]](#cite_note-530) U.S-allied Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain reportedly pushed Trump to continue the war until there are significant changes in Iran's leadership.[\[498\]](#cite_note-531) American journalist [Shelly Kittleson](/wiki/Shelly_Kittleson "Shelly Kittleson") was kidnapped in Baghdad by [Kata'ib Hezbollah](/wiki/Kata%27ib_Hezbollah "Kata'ib Hezbollah")—the strongest faction within the PMF—who demanded that the Iraqi government release several detained members of the group.[\[499\]](#cite_note-532)

On 1 April, [Mehr News Agency](/wiki/Mehr_News_Agency "Mehr News Agency"), a semi-official Iranian government news outlet, reported that policy expert and former foreign minister [Kamal Kharazi](/wiki/Kamal_Kharazi "Kamal Kharazi") was seriously injured and his wife was killed in an airstrike which hit his home.[\[500\]](#cite_note-533) Iranian officials described the attack as an attempt to derail diplomacy, noting that Kharazi was overseeing a possible meeting between Iranian officials and US vice president [JD Vance](/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance").[\[501\]](#cite_note-534) Airstrikes on the strategically important [Hengam Island](/wiki/Hengam_Island "Hengam Island") in the Strait of Hormuz caused seven injuries.[\[502\]](#cite_note-535) Trump indicated that he was no longer concerned about Iran's enriched uranium buried underground.[\[503\]](#cite_note-536) Netanyahu asserted that the US–Israeli strikes have eliminated Iran's ability to produce nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles, thereby removing "two existential threats" to Israel.[\[504\]](#cite_note-537) The Iranian president Pezeshkian published an open letter to US citizens.[\[505\]](#cite_note-538)

Late in the day on 1 April, Trump made a speech addressing the nation, in which he said that the strikes have "dramatically curtailed" Iranian missile and drone systems, and added that the attacks on Iran will escalate over the next two to three weeks to "bring them back to the [Stone Ages](/wiki/Stone_Age "Stone Age"), where they belong".[\[506\]](#cite_note-539)

On 2 April, [two US strikes](/wiki/Karaj_B1_bridge_attack "Karaj B1 bridge attack") on the [B1 bridge](/wiki/Karaj_B1_bridge "Karaj B1 bridge") between Tehran and [Karaj](/wiki/Karaj "Karaj"), which was described as the highest bridge in the Middle East, reportedly killed eight people and wounded 95 others, causing it to collapse.[\[507\]](#cite_note-540) Trump gloated on the attack, which experts assessed as a possible [war crime](/wiki/War_crime "War crime").[\[508\]](#cite_note-france24-2april-541) At the time of the attack, many Iranian families had been gathered in the parks below the bridge to celebrate [Sizdah Be-dar](/wiki/Sizdah_Be-dar "Sizdah Be-dar").[\[509\]](#cite_note-542)

Iran revealed major damage to the century-old medical center [Pasteur Institute of Iran](/wiki/Pasteur_Institute_of_Iran "Pasteur Institute of Iran"). US Defense Secretary Hegseth boasted of "death and destruction from the sky all day long".[\[508\]](#cite_note-france24-2april-541) The IDF also announced that one of its strikes in the [Kermanshah](/wiki/Kermanshah "Kermanshah") area of Iran killed Iranian ballistics missile chief Makram Atimi and several battalion commanders from Atimi's central Iranian ballistic missile unit.[\[510\]](#cite_note-543)[\[511\]](#cite_note-544) An Iranian ballistic missile strike damaged an Israeli drone factory in [Petah Tikva](/wiki/Petah_Tikva "Petah Tikva").[\[512\]](#cite_note-calcalistech3april-545)[\[513\]](#cite_note-546)[\[514\]](#cite_note-547)

On 3 April, Iranian forces shot down a US Air Force [F-15E Strike Eagle](/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_F-15E_Strike_Eagle "McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle") fighter jet over the country, with the wreckage falling in the [Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province](/wiki/Kohgiluyeh_and_Boyer-Ahmad_province "Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province") of Iran,[\[515\]](#cite_note-548) prompting a [search and rescue](/wiki/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") mission by US helicopters.[\[516\]](#cite_note-549) The pilot was rescued that same day, but the [WSO](/wiki/Weapon_systems_officer "Weapon systems officer") remained missing and was [rescued alive 48 hours later](/wiki/2026_United_States_F-15E_rescue_operation_in_Iran "2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran").[\[517\]](#cite_note-ap-f515e-rescue-550)

A US [A-10 "Warthog"](/wiki/Fairchild_Republic_A-10_Thunderbolt_II "Fairchild Republic A-10 Thunderbolt II") aircraft was downed and its single crew member ejected near the Strait of Hormuz and was rescued.[\[518\]](#cite_note-551) Iran released a video showing shooting down the aircraft using surface-to-air missile.[\[519\]](#cite_note-552)

On the same day, Tehran's [Shahid Beheshti University](/wiki/Shahid_Beheshti_University "Shahid Beheshti University") was hit by airstrikes, making the total number of universities hit to more than 30, according to the Iranian Minister of Science.[\[520\]](#cite_note-553)

### Sixth week (4–7 April)

Further information: [2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran](/wiki/2026_United_States_F-15E_rescue_operation_in_Iran "2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran") and [Destruction of the Rafi'-Nia synagogue](/wiki/Destruction_of_the_Rafi%27-Nia_synagogue "Destruction of the Rafi'-Nia synagogue")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/2026-04-07_Trump_%E2%80%93_A_whole_civilization_will_die_tonight_2026-04-07_192815.png/250px-2026-04-07_Trump_%E2%80%93_A_whole_civilization_will_die_tonight_2026-04-07_192815.png)](/wiki/File:2026-04-07_Trump_%E2%80%93_A_whole_civilization_will_die_tonight_2026-04-07_192815.png)

7 April 2026 [Truth Social](/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social") post in which Trump threatened, "A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again."

On 4 April, explosions were reported at an auxiliary building of the [Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant](/wiki/Bushehr_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant") as well as the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Zone in [Mahshahr](/wiki/Bandar-e_Mahshahr "Bandar-e Mahshahr"), Iran.[\[521\]](#cite_note-554) The airstrikes in Mahshahr killed at least five and injured 170 others.[\[522\]](#cite_note-555) An Iranian missile strike hit in the vicinity of the IDF's [HaKirya](/wiki/HaKirya "HaKirya") headquarters in Tel Aviv.[\[523\]](#cite_note-jpost4april-556)

On 5 April, after heavy fighting, the second stranded crew member from the F-15E downed on 3 April was recovered by US forces in a [rescue operation](/wiki/2026_United_States_pilot_rescue_operation_in_Iran "2026 United States pilot rescue operation in Iran"), which resulted in damage to helicopters, the shooting down of an [A-10 Thunderbolt II](/wiki/A-10_Thunderbolt "A-10 Thunderbolt"),[\[524\]](#cite_note-557) and the destruction of two [C-130 Hercules](/wiki/C-130 "C-130"), three IRGC members killed, and several American service members injured.[\[517\]](#cite_note-ap-f515e-rescue-550)

On 6 April, the IRGC announced that the head of the IRGC's intelligence organisation, Major General [Majid Khademi](/wiki/Majid_Khademi "Majid Khademi"), had been killed in a joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike. Their statement claimed that Khademi had "played a major role in Iran's intelligence and security apparatus over nearly five decades".[\[525\]](#cite_note-ii-khademi-558) Israel claimed that [Yazdan Mir](/w/index.php?title=Yazdan_Mir&action=edit&redlink=1 "Yazdan Mir (page does not exist)"), a high-ranking commander of the IRGC [Quds Force](/wiki/Quds_Force "Quds Force"), had also been killed in the attacks.[\[526\]](#cite_note-6-4-toi-airstrikes-559)

On the same day, before Trump's deadline for targeting Iranian infrastructure,[\[527\]](#cite_note-560) Israel carried out strikes on the South Pars Petrochemical facility in [Asaluyeh](/wiki/Asaluyeh "Asaluyeh"), Iran.[\[528\]](#cite_note-south-pars-waspo-561) The [Israeli Air Force](/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") claimed that "85% of Iran's petrochemical exports" had been taken offline by now.[\[529\]](#cite_note-south-pars-toi-562)

At least 34 people, including six children, were killed in US-Israeli airstrikes across Iran, including against [Sharif University of Technology](/wiki/Sharif_University_of_Technology "Sharif University of Technology") and residential areas. Iranian vice president and reformist politician [Mohammad Reza Aref](/wiki/Mohammad_Reza_Aref "Mohammad Reza Aref"), who is also an alumnus of the university, described the alleged use of a [bunker-buster bomb](/wiki/Bunker-buster_bomb "Bunker-buster bomb") as a "symbol of Trump’s madness and ignorance".[\[530\]](#cite_note-aljazeera6april-563)

[](/wiki/File:Members_of_the_Tehran_Jewish_community_navigating_the_site_where_the_Rafi%27-Nia_synagogue_was_destroyed.webm "Play video")[](/wiki/File:Members_of_the_Tehran_Jewish_community_navigating_the_site_where_the_Rafi%27-Nia_synagogue_was_destroyed.webm)

Members of the Tehran Jewish community navigating the site where the Rafi'-Nia synagogue [was destroyed](/wiki/Destruction_of_the_Rafi%27-Nia_synagogue "Destruction of the Rafi'-Nia synagogue")

On 7 April, The Rafi'-Nia synagogue in central Tehran was [destroyed in an airstrike](/wiki/Destruction_of_the_Rafi%27-Nia_synagogue "Destruction of the Rafi'-Nia synagogue").[\[531\]](#cite_note-564) Israel said that the building was destroyed due to collateral damage and that it was never meant to be the direct target of the airstrike.[\[532\]](#cite_note-565) The same day, US forces began strikes on [Kharg Island](/wiki/Kharg_Island "Kharg Island").[\[533\]](#cite_note-566) In response, Iran said its restraint in targeting oil infrastructure in the region would no longer apply.[\[534\]](#cite_note-567) Trump posted to [Truth Social](/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social") that "a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again",[\[535\]](#cite_note-568) causing international concern that Trump would use nuclear weapons. The Secretary General of Amnesty International said that Trump’s statement "may constitute a threat to commit genocide".[\[536\]](#cite_note-569) Multiple [right-wing](/wiki/Right-wing_politics "Right-wing politics") commentators and many Democrats condemned the post, and some [called for him to be removed](/wiki/Efforts_to_impeach_Donald_Trump "Efforts to impeach Donald Trump") through the [25th Amendment](/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution").[\[537\]](#cite_note-Ferguson_2026-570)[\[538\]](#cite_note-571) The White House denied considering using nuclear weapons.[\[539\]](#cite_note-572) The White House later said that "only the president knows" what he would do on Iran.[\[540\]](#cite_note-573)

### Ceasefire (8 April – present)

Main articles: [2026 Iran war ceasefire](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire"), [8 April 2026 Lebanon attacks](/wiki/8_April_2026_Lebanon_attacks "8 April 2026 Lebanon attacks"), [Islamabad Talks](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks"), and [2026 United States naval blockade of Iran](/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran")

On 7 April at 6:32 p.m. [Eastern Time](/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") in the US (8 April, 1:32 a.m. [in Israel](/wiki/Israel_Summer_Time "Israel Summer Time") and 8 April, 2:02 a.m. [in Iran](/wiki/Iran_Standard_Time "Iran Standard Time")), President Trump announced on Truth Social that the US and Iran had reached [an agreement](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire") based on the 10-point proposal mediated by Pakistani Prime Minister [Shehbaz Sharif](/wiki/Shehbaz_Sharif "Shehbaz Sharif") and Field Marshal [Asim Munir](/wiki/Asim_Munir "Asim Munir"),[\[541\]](#cite_note-574) writing on Truth Social that Iran had sent the US a 10-point proposal, which the US believes is a "workable basis on which to negotiate".[\[542\]](#cite_note-PoliticoCeasefire-575) The US, Israel, and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, under which Iran would also re-open the Strait of Hormuz; while the announcement occurred on 7 April in Washington, the acceptance and official implementation took effect on 8 April local time in the Middle East.[\[543\]](#cite_note-576)

After the ceasefire announcement, Iran's [Lavan Island](/wiki/Lavan_Island "Lavan Island") oil refinery and [Sirri Island](/wiki/Sirri_Island "Sirri Island") crude export facilities were struck by an "enemy attack". No party claimed responsibility.[\[544\]](#cite_note-577) In response, Iran continued to conduct missile and drone strikes on Gulf Arab states such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain.[\[545\]](#cite_note-578)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/8_April_2026_Isreali_attacks_on_Beirut_%282%29.jpg/250px-8_April_2026_Isreali_attacks_on_Beirut_%282%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:8_April_2026_Isreali_attacks_on_Beirut_\(2\).jpg)

Aftermath of [8 April 2026 Israeli attacks](/wiki/8_April_2026_Lebanon_attacks "8 April 2026 Lebanon attacks") on Beirut, Lebanon

Israel and the US assert that the ceasefire does not include Lebanon,[\[546\]](#cite_note-579)[\[547\]](#cite_note-580) contradicting the Pakistani mediators and Iran.[\[548\]](#cite_note-581) Hezbollah said that it halted attacks on Israel and on Israeli soldiers in Lebanon.[\[549\]](#cite_note-582) Despite the ceasefire, Israel launched "[Operation Eternal Darkness](/wiki/April_8,_2026_Lebanon_attacks "April 8, 2026 Lebanon attacks")", which Israel said included wide-ranging operation targeting all of Hezbollah's command and control centers in southern Lebanon, [Beirut](/wiki/Beirut "Beirut") and the [Beqaa Valley](/wiki/Beqaa_Valley "Beqaa Valley").[\[550\]](#cite_note-583) These were the largest attacks since the start of the war,[\[551\]](#cite_note-584) killing at least 357 people and injuring more than 1,200 others.[\[552\]](#cite_note-585)[\[553\]](#cite_note-586) In Beirut alone, at least 92 people were killed and at least 742 others were injured.[\[554\]](#cite_note-587) In response, Iran threatened to attack Israel "if the aggressions against dear Lebanon are not brought to an immediate end",[\[555\]](#cite_note-588) Iranian media later said that Iran paused Hormuz traffic over Israeli attacks in Lebanon.[\[556\]](#cite_note-589) Hezbollah claimed responsibility for launching rockets towards northern Israel as a response to "cease-fire violations".[\[557\]](#cite_note-590)

On 11 April, Trump said that American forces had started "[clearing](/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_campaign "2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign")" the Strait of Hormuz.[\[558\]](#cite_note-591) Iran claimed that an American ship on its way to the strait turned back after being warned.[\[559\]](#cite_note-592) *[The Wall Street Journal](/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")* reported that several US Navy [destroyers](/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer") entered the strait for the first time since the war began. A US official described it as an "operation that focused on freedom of navigation through international waters”. The Iranian government reportedly threatened to attack the ships, accusing the US of a ceasefire violation.[\[560\]](#cite_note-593)[\[561\]](#cite_note-594) US [Central Command](/wiki/United_States_Central_Command "United States Central Command") said the ships are taking part in [minesweeping](/wiki/Minesweeping "Minesweeping").[\[562\]](#cite_note-595) On the same day, the [talks between the US and Iran](/wiki/Islamabad_Talks "Islamabad Talks")—the highest-level discussions between the two countries since the [1979 Islamic Revolution](/wiki/1979_Islamic_Revolution "1979 Islamic Revolution")—were held in [Islamabad](/wiki/Islamabad "Islamabad"), Pakistan, lasting 21 hours, after which [JD Vance](/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") announced that no agreement had been reached, stating that Iran had refused "to accept our terms."[\[563\]](#cite_note-596) Afterwards, Trump said that he no longer cared about negotiations with Iran.[\[111\]](#cite_note-independent13april-136)

Trump declared that the US Navy would begin [its own blockade](/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran") of "all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz" from 13 April. He also said the US Navy would stop any ships that paid tolls to Iran.[\[564\]](#cite_note-597) However, [United States Central Command](/wiki/United_States_Central_Command "United States Central Command") clarified that the blockade would only be enforced on ships travelling to or from Iranian ports.[\[565\]](#cite_note-598) The [IRGC Navy](/wiki/Islamic_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps_Navy "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy") said that any military vessel approaching the strait would be considered a ceasefire violation and would meet a "severe response."[\[566\]](#cite_note-599) Trump threatened to strike any fast-attack ships of the IRGC Navy, similar to how the US carried out [strikes against alleged drug traffickers](/wiki/United_States_strikes_on_alleged_drug_traffickers_during_Operation_Southern_Spear "United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear") during [Operation Southern Spear](/wiki/Operation_Southern_Spear "Operation Southern Spear").[\[567\]](#cite_note-600)

According to a US analyst, Iran had 13 days of oil storage capacity, forcing it to shut down its oil fields thereafter and potentially damaging them.[\[568\]](#cite_note-sleiman14april-601) The same analyst estimated the loss of import and export capacity to $435 million USD per day.[\[568\]](#cite_note-sleiman14april-601)

On 14 April, at least four Iranian-linked ships traveled through the Strait of Hormuz, despite the US blockade, according to public transponder data seen by [BBC Verify](/wiki/BBC_Verify "BBC Verify").[\[569\]](#cite_note-602)[\[570\]](#cite_note-603) Those ships later stopped or turned around, after presumed interception by the US Navy, according to shipping data firms and the *[Sydney Morning Herald](/wiki/Sydney_Morning_Herald "Sydney Morning Herald")*.[\[571\]](#cite_note-604) Later that day, a US official said that eight oil tankers sailing to or from Iranian ports had been intercepted since the start of the blockade, adding that all tankers complied with orders.[\[572\]](#cite_note-wsj14april-605) Tankers leaving [Chabahar Port](/wiki/Chabahar_Port "Chabahar Port") were contacted by a US [destroyer](/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer"), while [Boeing P-8 Poseidon](/wiki/Boeing_P-8_Poseidon "Boeing P-8 Poseidon") patrol aircraft were also used to intercept tankers.[\[572\]](#cite_note-wsj14april-605) On 16 April, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General [Dan Caine](/wiki/Dan_Caine "Dan Caine"), announced that 13 oil tankers had been intercepted by the US Navy in its blockade of Iran, with all ships complying with US directions and no boarding needed.[\[573\]](#cite_note-DOD-16042026-606)

On 16 April, President Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to a [ten-day truce](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war_ceasefire "2026 Lebanon war ceasefire").[\[113\]](#cite_note-aljazeera16april-138)

As a result of the ceasefire in Lebanon, on 17 April, Iran announced that passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz would be allowed during the truce.[\[114\]](#cite_note-reuters17april-139) Despite this, President Trump said that the US blockade of ships traveling to or from Iranian ports would continue.[\[574\]](#cite_note-607) As a result of the US decision to continue its blockade, Iran announced that it would re-impose restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz.[\[575\]](#cite_note-608)[\[576\]](#cite_note-609)[\[115\]](#cite_note-business-standard-18april-140) Meanwhile, the US stated that its blockade had intercepted 23 ships traveling to or from Iranian ports.[\[577\]](#cite_note-610)

On 19 April, Trump sent two negotiators to Pakistan, saying that planned talks were Iran's "last chance" to reach a deal.[\[578\]](#cite_note-611) He threatened that Iran would be "blown up" if the negotiations fail, saying the US will target power plants and bridges.[\[579\]](#cite_note-612)

The US Navy seized [an Iranian cargo ship](/wiki/Touska "Touska") on 19 April, saying it was attempting to evade their blockade. Trump said that a US [guided-missile destroyer](/wiki/Guided-missile_destroyer "Guided-missile destroyer") fired at the ship, damaging its [engine room](/wiki/Engine_room "Engine room").[\[580\]](#cite_note-613)[\[581\]](#cite_note-614) Iran called this seizure a breach of the ceasefire, which was due to end on 22 April.[\[116\]](#cite_note-ndtv20april-141) Iran retaliated by launching drones at US ships, although no damage was reported.[\[582\]](#cite_note-615)

On 21 April, the Pentagon said that US soldiers boarded a sanctioned tanker in the Indo-Pacific region as part of an effort to disrupt ships providing support to Iran.[\[583\]](#cite_note-616) Trump said the US military intercepted a "gift from China" to Iran. The Chinese foreign ministry stated that it "opposes any malicious association".[\[584\]](#cite_note-617) The same day, Trump claimed the three [Iranian nuclear sites](/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran") are being watched by the [US Space Force](/wiki/US_Space_Force "US Space Force").[\[585\]](#cite_note-618) JD Vance was expected to visit Islamabad for talks on 22 April, but the talks were paused by the US due to it not receiving a response from Iran.[\[586\]](#cite_note-619)

A day before the ceasefire was due to end on 22 April, Trump said he will not extend the truce unless Iran agrees to a deal and said the US military was "raring to go", warning that bombing would resume soon.[\[587\]](#cite_note-620) Hours before the ceasefire was due to end, Trump extended the truce, saying he did so at Pakistan's request, to allow time for an Iranian proposal to be submitted.[\[118\]](#cite_note-aljazeera21april-143)

Hours after the ceasefire was extended, the Iranian Revolutionary Guard announced that it had seized two container ships and fired on one of them, causing "serious damage to the bridge". This was in response to the US seizing an Iranian ship three days earlier.[\[588\]](#cite_note-621) On 22–23 April, three Iranian oil tankers were reportedly intercepted by the US in the eastern Indian Ocean[\[589\]](#cite_note-622) and an Iranian-linked oil tanker was seized by the US.[\[590\]](#cite_note-623) Later, Iranian state media reported that air defenses in Tehran engaged "small drones, micro-UAVs".[\[591\]](#cite_note-624) On 23 April, Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy any Iranian boats laying mines in the Hormuz strait.[\[117\]](#cite_note-telanganatoday23april-142)

Despite the Iranian seizure of two cargo ships,[\[119\]](#cite_note-Guardian_24_Apr_26-144) Trump claimed on 23 April that the US fully controlled the Strait of Hormuz and said that he is the one keeping the strait closed, because opening it would allow Iran to "make $500 million a day".[\[592\]](#cite_note-625) *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* described the situation as a "dual blockade", saying that while the US Navy was able to blockade Iranian ports, it had not been able to stop the Iranian blockade or open the strait to US allies.[\[119\]](#cite_note-Guardian_24_Apr_26-144) The same day, Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to a three-week extension of the ceasefire.[\[593\]](#cite_note-626)

On 24 April, Iran said that it seized a ship suspected of collaborating with American military after the ship committed violations and ignored warnings.[\[594\]](#cite_note-627) On 25 April, Trump said that he canceled the US negotiators' trip to Pakistan for negotiations with Iran.[\[595\]](#cite_note-628)

On 1 May, Trump issued letters to congressional leaders according to the 1973 [War Powers Resolution](/wiki/War_Powers_Resolution "War Powers Resolution") limiting conflicts to 60 days, that hostilities had ended so far, but conflict remains.[\[253\]](#cite_note-mang-284) On 3 May, Trump said that [the US will help free up ships in the Strait of Hormuz](/wiki/Operation_Project_Freedom "Operation Project Freedom") beginning the next morning.[\[120\]](#cite_note-internazionale3may-145)

On 4 May, the Iranian military warned the US to keep out of Hormuz.[\[121\]](#cite_note-aljazeera4may-146) The UAE and Oman said that they had intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones on the same day.[\[596\]](#cite_note-aljazeera4may2-629)[\[597\]](#cite_note-auto-630) Iranian state media claimed that the Iranian navy fired two missiles and hit an American naval frigate in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM denied that the missiles struck the ship.[\[598\]](#cite_note-economictimes4may-631)[\[599\]](#cite_note-632) CENTCOM later reported that it destroyed six small boats launched by the Iranian military towards ships in the Strait of Hormuz.[\[598\]](#cite_note-economictimes4may-631) The UAE said that an Iranian drone strike on an oil processing plant in [Fujairah](/wiki/Fujairah "Fujairah") caused a fire, injuring three Indian citizens.[\[600\]](#cite_note-633) On 5 May, the UAE said that it dealt with missile and drone attacks from Iran for the second consecutive day. Iran denied conducting attacks against the UAE in recent days.[\[601\]](#cite_note-634) On 6 May, President Trump announced a temporary halt in the US military's "Project Freedom" operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" toward a potential agreement with Iran. Trump stated that the operation will be paused for "a short period" to determine whether a "complete and final agreement" with Iran could be achieved.[\[122\]](#cite_note-aljazeera6may-147) On the same day, Trump warned that if Iran does not agree to an agreement to end the war, the United States will resume bombing at a "much higher level and intensity".[\[123\]](#cite_note-ndtv6may-148) The US military said on the same day that it crippled an Iranian-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman after it allegedly attempted to breach the American blockade and cruise toward an Iranian port.[\[124\]](#cite_note-aa6may-149)

## Strikes and casualties

Main article: [Casualties of the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Casualties_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Casualties of the 2026 Iran war") Further information: [List of attacks during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/List_of_attacks_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of attacks during the 2026 Iran war"), [List of aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/List_of_aviation_shootdowns_and_accidents_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war"), and [List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/List_of_ships_attacked_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war")

### Iran

See also: [Air campaign in Iranian Kurdistan](/wiki/Air_campaign_in_Iranian_Kurdistan "Air campaign in Iranian Kurdistan")

The US and Israel eliminated many Iranian commanders and leaders on the war's first day due to a successful deception. IT caused Iran to believe that strikes were not imminent. Thus, groups of senior Iranian officials continued gathering in person. These gatherings were targeted in initial strikes. One part of the deception was information about a US F-22 deployment leaked to hide that preparations were more advanced at other bases.[\[602\]](#cite_note-Estrin-2026-635)[\[603\]](#cite_note-Avraham-2026-636) Calls between Trump and Netanyahu before the war were not publicised to diminish the possibility of an Iranian first strike.[\[603\]](#cite_note-Avraham-2026-636)

[IDF Spokesperson](/wiki/IDF_Spokesperson%27s_Unit "IDF Spokesperson's Unit") Brigadier General [Effie Defrin](/wiki/Effie_Defrin "Effie Defrin") stated that months of joint US and Israeli "strategic and operational deception" of satellite imagery led up to the war. This encompassed planes and other facilities. The night of the initial strike he and [IDF Chief of Staff](/wiki/Chief_of_the_General_Staff_\(Israel\) "Chief of the General Staff (Israel)") Lieutenant General [Eyal Zamir](/wiki/Eyal_Zamir "Eyal Zamir") took their official cars home from [IDF Headquarters](/wiki/HaKirya "HaKirya").[\[602\]](#cite_note-Estrin-2026-635) They came back without them so that satellite imagery would show that their base did not appear full nor warplanes appear armed and ready.[\[604\]](#cite_note-637)[\[605\]](#cite_note-638) Three separate gatherings of Iranian regime officials were hit within half a minute of each other in the opening strike.[\[603\]](#cite_note-Avraham-2026-636)

#### Assassination of Ali Khamenei

Main article: [Assassination of Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Ali_Khamenei_2026.02.12_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Ali_Khamenei_2026.02.12_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Ali_Khamenei_2026.02.12_\(cropped\).jpg)

Khamenei on 12 February 2026, 16 days before his assassination

On 28 February 2026, [Ali Khamenei](/wiki/Ali_Khamenei "Ali Khamenei"), the [supreme leader of Iran](/wiki/Supreme_leader_of_Iran "Supreme leader of Iran"), [was assassinated](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei") in an Israeli air attack.[\[606\]](#cite_note-639)\[*[better source needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")*\][\[603\]](#cite_note-Avraham-2026-636) On 1 March, Iranian state media announced Khamenei's death.[\[607\]](#cite_note-640) The IRGC-controlled [Fars News Agency](/wiki/Fars_News_Agency "Fars News Agency"), announced that Khamenei's daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law [Zahra Haddad-Adel](/wiki/Zahra_Haddad-Adel "Zahra Haddad-Adel") had also been killed.[\[608\]](#cite_note-641)[\[609\]](#cite_note-642)[\[610\]](#cite_note-643) The Iranian government declared 40 days of mourning.[\[611\]](#cite_note-644)

#### Military and officials

Main article: [List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/List_of_Iranian_officials_killed_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war")

The initial dead included Iranian defense minister [Aziz Nasirzadeh](/wiki/Aziz_Nasirzadeh "Aziz Nasirzadeh"), and four top [Ministry of Intelligence](/wiki/Ministry_of_Intelligence_\(Iran\) "Ministry of Intelligence (Iran)") officials.[\[612\]](#cite_note-645)

Additional senior officials included [Salah Asadi](/wiki/Salah_Asadi "Salah Asadi"), head of intelligence for Iran's emergency command, [Mohammad Shirazi](/wiki/Mohammad_Shirazi_\(general\) "Mohammad Shirazi (general)"), head of Khamenei's military office, head of the [Organization of Defensive Innovation and Research](/wiki/Organization_of_Defensive_Innovation_and_Research "Organization of Defensive Innovation and Research") (SPND) [Hossein Jabal Amelian](/wiki/Hossein_Jabal_Amelian "Hossein Jabal Amelian"), former SPND head [Reza Mozaffari Nia](/wiki/Reza_Mozaffari_Nia "Reza Mozaffari Nia"),[\[205\]](#cite_note-Iran_International-2026a-233) and chief of staff [Abdolrahim Mousavi](/wiki/Abdolrahim_Mousavi "Abdolrahim Mousavi"), among 40 official as reported by intelligence and military sources.[\[613\]](#cite_note-646)

On 13 March, IDF estimated that between 3,000 and 4,000 Iranian soldiers and commanders had been killed.[\[614\]](#cite_note-647)

On 17 March, Israel [assassinated Ali Larijani](/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Larijani "Assassination of Ali Larijani"), [secretary of](/wiki/Secretary_of_the_Supreme_National_Security_Council "Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council") Iran's [Supreme National Security Council](/wiki/Supreme_National_Security_Council "Supreme National Security Council").[\[421\]](#cite_note-sk-454) IRGC commander [Mohammad Pakpour](/wiki/Mohammad_Pakpour "Mohammad Pakpour") and [Defence Council](/wiki/Iranian_Defence_Council "Iranian Defence Council") secretary [Ali Shamkhani](/wiki/Ali_Shamkhani "Ali Shamkhani") were reported dead in late March.[\[615\]](#cite_note-648)

On 18 March, the [Hengaw Organization for Human Rights](/wiki/Hengaw_Organization_for_Human_Rights "Hengaw Organization for Human Rights") estimated that 5,300+ members of the Iranian military had been killed.[\[616\]](#cite_note-649)

On 31 March, [Iran International](/wiki/Iran_International "Iran International") reported that at least 4,700 security forces had been killed.[\[617\]](#cite_note-650)

On 6 April, the head of IRGC intelligence, Major General Majid Khademi, was assassinated in a joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike.[\[525\]](#cite_note-ii-khademi-558)

As of 7 April, [Human Rights Activists in Iran](/wiki/Human_Rights_Activists_in_Iran "Human Rights Activists in Iran") (HRANA), a US-based [non-governmental organization](/wiki/Non-governmental_organization "Non-governmental organization"), reported 3,636 documented war deaths, including 1,701 civilians, 1,221 military personnel, and 714 unclassified. According to HRANA, "\[i\]t is believed that military casualties are significantly higher than the figures reported in \[its\] reports" as confirmations depend largely on government data. Its count largely reflects reports of military personnel present in urban areas.[\[618\]](#cite_note-HRANA-651)

#### Civilians

Further information: [2026 Minab school attack](/wiki/2026_Minab_school_attack "2026 Minab school attack"), [2026 Lamerd sports hall attack](/wiki/2026_Lamerd_sports_hall_attack "2026 Lamerd sports hall attack"), and [2026 Karaj B1 bridge attack](/wiki/2026_Karaj_B1_bridge_attack "2026 Karaj B1 bridge attack")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Shajareh_Tayyebeh_school_in_Minab_photos_from_Mehr_%283%29.jpg/250px-Shajareh_Tayyebeh_school_in_Minab_photos_from_Mehr_%283%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Shajareh_Tayyebeh_school_in_Minab_photos_from_Mehr_\(3\).jpg)

Rescuers and residents searching through the rubble of the [Minab girls' elementary school](/wiki/2026_Minab_school_attack "2026 Minab school attack"), destroyed by the United States

On the first day of the war, the Shajareh Tayyebeh girl's elementary school in [Minab](/wiki/Minab "Minab") was [hit by an American attack](/wiki/2026_Minab_school_attack "2026 Minab school attack"), according to Iran.[\[619\]](#cite_note-652) The school was located near[\[ah\]](#cite_note-656) the Sayyid al-Shuhada military complex,[\[623\]](#cite_note-657) of which it had once been a part.[\[622\]](#cite_note-Browne-2026-655)[\[624\]](#cite_note-658) While the number killed was not independently confirmed,[\[625\]](#cite_note-BBC_News-2026b-659) Iranian state media reported that more than 175 people, mostly children, were killed while 95 were wounded.[\[626\]](#cite_note-660) Video showed a Tomahawk missile hitting a building adjacent to the school;[\[627\]](#cite_note-661) preliminary findings from an American military investigation indicated that the strike resulted from outdated targeting data.[\[628\]](#cite_note-662)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Damages_caused_by_attacks_on_Tehran_22_Avash_25_esfand_1404.webp/250px-Damages_caused_by_attacks_on_Tehran_22_Avash_25_esfand_1404.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Damages_caused_by_attacks_on_Tehran_22_Avash_25_esfand_1404.webp)

Damage to a residential structure in Tehran following aerial attacks on 15 March 2026

At least 20 civilians, mostly families who gathered after breaking their [fast](/wiki/Islamic_fasting "Islamic fasting") at Ramadan,[\[629\]](#cite_note-BBCd4xo-663) were killed in Tehran's Niloofar Square on 1 or 2 March, according to Iranian-state media.[\[630\]](#cite_note-664) On 3 March, the [Iranian Red Crescent Society](/wiki/Iranian_Red_Crescent_Society "Iranian Red Crescent Society") said that over 600 civilians had been killed[\[631\]](#cite_note-665) while HRANA reported 1,097 civilian deaths.[\[632\]](#cite_note-666) On 7 March, the Red Crescent reported that over 6,668 civilian "units" had been targeted by US-Israeli strikes, including 5,535 residential units, 1,041 commercial units, 14 medical centers, 65 schools, and 13 centers affiliated with the Red Crescent.[\[633\]](#cite_note-667) The Middle East Eye, an anti-Israel news outlet, reported that the US used [double tap](/wiki/Double_tap_strike "Double tap strike") airstrikes,[\[634\]](#cite_note-668)[\[635\]](#cite_note-669) although the US denies this. As of 23 March, HRANA estimated that at least 15% of the casualties were under age 18.[\[636\]](#cite_note-670)

An Israeli airstrike on 9 March in [Resalat](/wiki/Resalat_\(district\) "Resalat (district)") neighbourhood of Tehran destroyed a [Basij](/wiki/Basij "Basij")\-affiliated building as well as three residential buildings, killing 40 to 50. According to a BBC analysis, Israel used [Mark 82](/wiki/Mark_82 "Mark 82") bombs in the attack.[\[629\]](#cite_note-BBCd4xo-663)

As of 27 March, Iran has reported damage to at least 120 [historical sites](/wiki/History_of_Iran "History of Iran").[\[637\]](#cite_note-671)

The [deadly attack on residential buildings and a sports hall](/wiki/2026_Lamerd_sports_hall_attack "2026 Lamerd sports hall attack") in the town of [Lamerd](/wiki/Lamerd "Lamerd") killed 21 including 4 children and injured 100.[\[638\]](#cite_note-672)

#### Institutions

The initial attack targeted Leadership House. On 2 March, video footage released by Iran International showed the destroyed IRGC Malek-Ashtar building in Tehran following a joint US-Israel missile strike.[\[639\]](#cite_note-673) On 3 March, the complex of [Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting](/wiki/Islamic_Republic_of_Iran_Broadcasting "Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting") (IRIB), the state broadcaster's headquarters, was hit in an Israeli air operation.[\[640\]](#cite_note-674)[\[641\]](#cite_note-675)

Iranian state-linked media indicated that Iran's parliament building was targeted.[\[642\]](#cite_note-676) On 3 March, Israeli forces bombed the [Assembly of Experts](/wiki/Assembly_of_Experts "Assembly of Experts") office building in [Qom](/wiki/Qom "Qom").[\[643\]](#cite_note-677)[\[644\]](#cite_note-678)

#### Infrastructure

By 5 March, the World Health Organization had identified 13 Iranian health sites hit, as well as one in Lebanon.[\[645\]](#cite_note-679) The Iranian Foreign Minister said that the US [had struck a desalination plant](/wiki/2026_Qeshm_Island_desalination_plant_attack "2026 Qeshm Island desalination plant attack") on [Qeshm Island](/wiki/Qeshm_Island "Qeshm Island"), disrupting water supply to 30 villages, but both the US and Israel denied an attack.[\[646\]](#cite_note-680)[\[348\]](#cite_note-b673-380) The [Russian consulate in Isfahan](/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_of_Russia#Asia "List of diplomatic missions of Russia") was damaged.[\[647\]](#cite_note-681)

### United States

On 1 March, six US soldiers were killed amid more than 30 injured in an Iranian drone attack near [Camp Arifjan](/wiki/Camp_Arifjan "Camp Arifjan") in Port Shuaiba, [Kuwait](/wiki/Kuwait "Kuwait"). Those killed were soldiers of the [United States Army Reserve](/wiki/United_States_Army_Reserve "United States Army Reserve") assigned to the [103rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command](/wiki/103rd_Expeditionary_Sustainment_Command "103rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command"), headquartered in [Des Moines, Iowa](/wiki/Des_Moines,_Iowa "Des Moines, Iowa").[\[648\]](#cite_note-682) On 4 March, US Marine Corps Lance Corporal Kevin Melendez died in Saudi Arabia in a non-hostile incident.[\[649\]](#cite_note-RC1-683) On 8 March, [CENTCOM](/wiki/CENTCOM "CENTCOM") reported that a [National Guard](/wiki/National_Guard_\(United_States\) "National Guard (United States)") soldier died during a medical emergency.[\[650\]](#cite_note-684) Sgt. Benjamin N. Pennington, a soldier of the [1st Space Brigade](/wiki/1st_Space_Brigade "1st Space Brigade") wounded in an attack against [Prince Sultan Air Base](/wiki/Prince_Sultan_Air_Base "Prince Sultan Air Base") in Saudi Arabia on 1 March, died from his injuries on 9 March.[\[651\]](#cite_note-685)

Six American airmen were killed on 12 March when their [KC-135](/wiki/KC-135 "KC-135") aerial refueling aircraft crashed in western Iraq. CENTCOM said that the crash was not the result of hostile action, but had resulted during an incident involving another US aircraft. By 13 March, the US military publicly announced that about 140 American servicemen had been injured.[\[652\]](#cite_note-AP1-686) A 27 March attack on Prince Sultan Air Base damaged "multiple" refueling aircraft and destroyed a [Boeing E-3 Sentry](/wiki/Boeing_E-3_Sentry "Boeing E-3 Sentry"), as well as wounding at least 15 US soldiers.[\[653\]](#cite_note-687)[\[654\]](#cite_note-688)[\[473\]](#cite_note-apnews27march-506)

The [USS *Gerald R. Ford*](/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford "USS Gerald R. Ford"), the largest aircraft carrier in theatre, was damaged by a fire that broke out 12 March. The [US Navy](/wiki/US_Navy "US Navy") said the fire had injured multiple sailors,[\[ai\]](#cite_note-Ford-693) started in a laundry area and was not combat-related.[\[659\]](#cite_note-694) The carrier had been dealing with other mechanical issues, including a malfunctioning sewage treatment system, since before it arrived in the Middle East.[\[660\]](#cite_note-695) According to multiple reports on 17–18 March, *Gerald R. Ford* paused launching airstrikes and sailed toward the [Crete Naval Base](/wiki/Crete_Naval_Base "Crete Naval Base") for repairs.[\[656\]](#cite_note-usni170326-690)

Many US military bases near Iran were rendered "all but uninhabitable" due to Iranian strikes. Within the war's first two weeks, Iran's attacks caused $800 million in damage to bases. Affected bases include [Al-Sader](/w/index.php?title=Al-Sader_base&action=edit&redlink=1 "Al-Sader base (page does not exist)") and [Al-Ruwais](/w/index.php?title=Al-Ruwais_base&action=edit&redlink=1 "Al-Ruwais base (page does not exist)") in the UAE, the [naval base in Bahrain](/wiki/Naval_Support_Activity_Bahrain "Naval Support Activity Bahrain"), [Ali Al-Salem](/wiki/Ali_Al_Salem_Air_Base "Ali Al Salem Air Base") in Kuwait, [Al-Udeid](/wiki/Al_Udeid_Air_Base "Al Udeid Air Base") in Qatar, and [Prince Sultan](/wiki/Prince_Sultan_Air_Base "Prince Sultan Air Base") in Saudi Arabia. According to unnamed officials, the damage degraded the US's military ability in the war. Many US servicemembers relocated to "hotels and office spaces", which raised concerns of the US using civilians as [human shields](/wiki/Human_shields "Human shields"). An attack on a hotel in Bahrain injured two Pentagon employees.[\[661\]](#cite_note-696)

### Israel

Main article: [2026 Iranian strikes on Israel](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Israel "2026 Iranian strikes on Israel")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Dankal_shelter_2.jpg/250px-Dankal_shelter_2.jpg)](/wiki/File:Dankal_shelter_2.jpg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Houses_in_Nesher_hit_by_shrapnel_from_Missile_parts_of_a_Multiple_independently_targetable_reentry_vehicl%2C_fired_from_Iran_on_March_24%2C_2026_at_00.22_AM_04.jpg/250px-Houses_in_Nesher_hit_by_shrapnel_from_Missile_parts_of_a_Multiple_independently_targetable_reentry_vehicl%2C_fired_from_Iran_on_March_24%2C_2026_at_00.22_AM_04.jpg)](/wiki/File:Houses_in_Nesher_hit_by_shrapnel_from_Missile_parts_of_a_Multiple_independently_targetable_reentry_vehicl,_fired_from_Iran_on_March_24,_2026_at_00.22_AM_04.jpg)

**Left:** Civilians sheltering in a converted light rail station in [Tel Aviv](/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") on 6 March  
**Right:** Homes in [Nesher](/wiki/Nesher "Nesher") damaged by shrapnel from Iranian cluster munitions on 24 March

[](/wiki/File:Civil_defense_siren_and_missile_explosions_sounds_in_Israel_during_Iran_war_2026.ogg "Play audio")Duration: 1 minute and 51 seconds.1:51[](/wiki/File:Civil_defense_siren_and_missile_explosions_sounds_in_Israel_during_Iran_war_2026.ogg)

Civil defense siren and missile explosions sounds in central Israel, 5 March 2026

The first attack struck a residential building, leaving one Israeli injured.[\[662\]](#cite_note-697) [Magen David Adom](/wiki/Magen_David_Adom "Magen David Adom") reported that Iran's initial attacks had left 89 injured, with three directly wounded and the rest indirectly, most of them civilians.[\[663\]](#cite_note-698) On 28 February, a direct hit in [Tel Aviv](/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") killed a woman and injured 22 others, one seriously.[\[664\]](#cite_note-699) On 1 March, a strike hit a synagogue and residential buildings in [Beit Shemesh](/wiki/Beit_Shemesh "Beit Shemesh"), killing nine and injuring 49 others.[\[665\]](#cite_note-700) On 9 March, two workers were killed in [Yehud](/wiki/Yehud,_Israel "Yehud, Israel"), outside of Tel Aviv, after they were struck by submunitions from an Iranian missile equipped with a [cluster bomb](/wiki/Cluster_bomb "Cluster bomb") warhead.[\[666\]](#cite_note-701)[\[667\]](#cite_note-702)

On 17 March, a cluster munition from an Iranian missile hit an apartment building in [Ramat Gan](/wiki/Ramat_Gan "Ramat Gan") and killed two residents. A statement from the [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps](/wiki/Islamic_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps") called the barrage "revenge for the blood of martyr Dr. Ali Larijani and his companions", who had been killed the day before.[\[668\]](#cite_note-703) According to [CNN](/wiki/CNN "CNN"), the use of cluster munitions violates international law. N.R. Jenzen-Jones of [Armament Research Services](/wiki/Armament_Research_Services "Armament Research Services") stated that this type of warhead is being used "primarily to sow terror amongst a civilian population".[\[669\]](#cite_note-704)

The executive director of the [Arms Control Association](/wiki/Arms_Control_Association "Arms Control Association") called the Iranian use of cluster munitions at residential sections of [Israel](/wiki/Israel "Israel") during the war as deliberate, saying that "Iran appears to be launching them into relatively populated areas, probably with the goal of producing potential civilian harm."[\[670\]](#cite_note-705) Neither Iran nor Israel is party to the [Convention on Cluster Munitions](/wiki/Convention_on_Cluster_Munitions "Convention on Cluster Munitions"),[\[671\]](#cite_note-706) and both Israel and Iran are among 17 countries that either produce cluster munitions, or reserve the right to do so.[\[672\]](#cite_note-707)

On 4 April, an Iranian missile strike hit in the vicinity of [the IDF's Kirya headquarters in Tel Aviv](/wiki/HaKirya "HaKirya").[\[523\]](#cite_note-jpost4april-556)

### Lebanon

Main article: [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war")

More than 2,000 people were killed and over 4,000 were wounded by Israeli strikes in Lebanon,[\[72\]](#cite_note-AnadoluDeaths-97) and Lebanon states more than one million people,[\[673\]](#cite_note-708) 1/6th of the population,[\[674\]](#cite_note-709) were displaced.[\[675\]](#cite_note-710) During the war, six [United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon](/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Force_in_Lebanon "United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon") peacekeepers were killed[\[u\]](#cite_note-UNIFIL_killed-64) and 11 were injured.[\[v\]](#cite_note-UNIFIL_injured-70)[\[49\]](#cite_note-tayyar.org-71)

### Iraq

Main articles: [Iraq in the 2026 Iran war](/wiki/Iraq_in_the_2026_Iran_war "Iraq in the 2026 Iran war") and [2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_Kurdistan_Region "2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region")

In Iraq, two members of the Iran-backed [Popular Mobilization Forces](/wiki/Popular_Mobilization_Forces "Popular Mobilization Forces") (PMF) were killed and three injured in a US-Israeli attack on 28 February.[\[676\]](#cite_note-711) A later report estimated three dead.[\[677\]](#cite_note-712) On 1 and 2 March, the United States and Israel conducted several attacks on Iranian-backed Iraqi militias to degrade their military capabilities.[\[678\]](#cite_note-713)

### Iranian attacks on US-allied Arab countries

Further information: [2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Arab_countries "2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Drone_attacks_and_strikes_in_the_UAE.webp/250px-Drone_attacks_and_strikes_in_the_UAE.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Drone_attacks_and_strikes_in_the_UAE.webp)

[Drone attacks and strikes in the UAE](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_United_Arab_Emirates "2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/EAS_warning_sent_to_phones_during_the_Iranian_stikes.png/250px-EAS_warning_sent_to_phones_during_the_Iranian_stikes.png)](/wiki/File:EAS_warning_sent_to_phones_during_the_Iranian_stikes.png)

An emergency alert sent to UAE residents shortly before Dubai International Airport was struck at around 12:30 A.M. local time, 28 February[\[679\]](#cite_note-714)

In addition to Israel, Iran launched strikes against multiple US-allied Arab countries. Iranian strikes against [Bahrain](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Bahrain "2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain") killed three.[\[680\]](#cite_note-715) Strikes against [Kuwait](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Kuwait "2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait") killed four soldiers and four civilians.[\[681\]](#cite_note-716) Strikes against [Oman](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Oman "2026 Iranian strikes on Oman") killed three.[\[682\]](#cite_note-717) Strikes against [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Saudi_Arabia "2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia") killed two.[\[683\]](#cite_note-718) Strikes against the [United Arab Emirates](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_the_United_Arab_Emirates "2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates") killed two soldiers and six civilians.[\[684\]](#cite_note-719)

Iran also struck [Qatar](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Qatar "2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar"),[\[685\]](#cite_note-720) [Azerbaijan](/wiki/2026_Iran_strikes_on_Azerbaijan "2026 Iran strikes on Azerbaijan"),[\[324\]](#cite_note-Reuters-2026b-356) and the [Akrotiri and Dhekelia](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Akrotiri_and_Dhekelia "2026 Iranian strikes on Akrotiri and Dhekelia") [British Overseas Territory](/wiki/British_Overseas_Territory "British Overseas Territory") on [Cyprus](/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Cyprus "2026 Iranian strikes on Cyprus").[\[686\]](#cite_note-721)

The Iranian attacks affected military infrastructure from [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") countries in the region, "including an Italian installation in Iraq and Kuwait, and a French naval facility in the United Arab Emirates".[\[687\]](#cite_note-722)

## Direct impacts

### Iran

Main article: [Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran](/wiki/Impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war_on_Iran "Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran")

#### Leadership

See also: [2026 Iranian supreme leader election](/wiki/2026_Iranian_supreme_leader_election "2026 Iranian supreme leader election")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_%28cropped%29.jpg/120px-Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Masoud_Pezeshkian_2025_\(cropped\).jpg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_%28Cropped%29.jpg/120px-Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_%28Cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Gholam_Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i_2023_\(Cropped\).jpg)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg/120px-Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg)](/wiki/File:Alireza_Arafi_13990824_0146818_crop.jpg)

The three members of the [Interim Leadership Council](/wiki/Interim_Leadership_Council "Interim Leadership Council") – President [Masoud Pezeshkian](/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian "Masoud Pezeshkian"), Chief Justice [Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i](/wiki/Gholam-Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i "Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i") and Ayatollah [Alireza Arafi](/wiki/Alireza_Arafi "Alireza Arafi")

The death of Ali Khamenei triggered an election for a new supreme leader. Under the terms of Iran's constitution, an [Interim Leadership Council](/wiki/Interim_Leadership_Council "Interim Leadership Council") was established on 1 March to exercise the functions of Iran's [head of state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") until a new supreme leader is elected.[\[236\]](#cite_note-Reuters-2026-267)

[Mojtaba Khamenei](/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei "Mojtaba Khamenei") was elected on 8 March 2026 to replace his father as supreme leader,[\[722\]](#cite_note-757) and the IRGC, as well as Iran's top leaders, including [Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf](/wiki/Mohammad_Bagher_Ghalibaf "Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf"), [Ali Larijani](/wiki/Ali_Larijani "Ali Larijani"), and [Masoud Pezeshkian](/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian "Masoud Pezeshkian"),[\[723\]](#cite_note-Sabah-2026-758) pledged their allegiance to him.[\[724\]](#cite_note-759)

In late March, the NYT described Iran's leadership as paralyzed with severely disrupted decision-making process. It also reported that the damage to communications infrastructure caused paranoia and internal power struggles.[\[725\]](#cite_note-760)

#### Civilian life

See also: [2025–2026 Iranian protests § After the strikes](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests#After_the_strikes "2025–2026 Iranian protests")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp/250px-Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp.png)](/wiki/File:Tehran_-_The_Fourth_Day_of_War_4_Avash.webp)

Residents in Tehran on the third day of US-Israeli airstrikes, 3 March 2026

According to UN Human Rights Chief [Volker Türk](/wiki/Volker_T%C3%BCrk "Volker Türk"), the "reckless" war is disproportionately impacting civilians in the Middle East and beyond.[\[726\]](#cite_note-761)

138,000 civilian sites in Iran were damaged during the conflict, with estimated time of reconstruction being 2 to 5 years.[\[727\]](#cite_note-762)

As the US and Israel executed joint strikes targeting Iranian military and institutional targets, Iran's capital reportedly became a [ghost town](/wiki/Ghost_town "Ghost town"), as civilians feared going outside or to their daily jobs.[\[728\]](#cite_note-763) Reports have emerged that prisoners in [Evin Prison](/wiki/Evin_Prison "Evin Prison") have been receiving limited bread and water since the onset of the war.[\[729\]](#cite_note-764) After the strikes, schools were ordered closed while banks and government offices remained in operation at reduced capacity. Local media reported that subway and bus services would remain operational.[\[730\]](#cite_note-765)

Amid the renewed "near total" [internet blackout in Iran](/wiki/2026_Internet_blackout_in_Iran "2026 Internet blackout in Iran"), [NetBlocks](/wiki/NetBlocks "NetBlocks") reported that internet connectivity in Iran dropped to 4% of ordinary levels.[\[625\]](#cite_note-BBC_News-2026b-659)[\[731\]](#cite_note-766)[\[732\]](#cite_note-767) While the internet blackout has exceeded 240 hours, making it the second longest ever, the government started handing out "white sim cards", which bypass filters, to government supporters, in order to allow them to promote its messaging.[\[733\]](#cite_note-768)[\[213\]](#cite_note-bm-241) As news of Khamenei's death broke, security forces were deployed to prevent an uprising, with footage showing them opening fire on celebrants in the streets[\[734\]](#cite_note-769)[\[735\]](#cite_note-770)[\[736\]](#cite_note-771) and shooting at people chanting behind the windows of their homes.[\[737\]](#cite_note-772)

During the first two weeks of March 2026, over 70,000 [Afghan refugees](/wiki/Afghans_in_Iran "Afghans in Iran") returned to Afghanistan, frequently under forced circumstances, exacerbating the country's [severe humanitarian crisis](/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_hunger_crisis_in_Afghanistan "2025–2026 hunger crisis in Afghanistan").[\[738\]](#cite_note-773) Arafat Jamal, the UNHCR Representative in Afghanistan, noted that they faced limited options amid the [military confrontations between Afghanistan and Pakistan](/wiki/2026_Afghanistan%E2%80%93Pakistan_War "2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan War").[\[739\]](#cite_note-774)

According to *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*, the war has overshadowed the executions of political prisoners in Iran, including those involved in the mass protests of January 2026, allowing Iran to continue carrying out death sentences and other severe punishments with little international scrutiny.[\[740\]](#cite_note-775)

#### Military

On 26 March, it was reported that children as young as 12 years of age may join Iran's war support, leading to concerns of the use of [child soldiers](/wiki/Child_soldiers "Child soldiers").[\[741\]](#cite_note-776)[\[742\]](#cite_note-777)[\[743\]](#cite_note-778) Days later, rights groups stated an 11-year-old was killed while on duty at a Tehran checkpoint.[\[744\]](#cite_note-779)

On 29 March, footage showed Iraq's [Popular Mobilization Forces](/wiki/Popular_Mobilization_Forces "Popular Mobilization Forces") deployed in Iran.[\[745\]](#cite_note-780)[\[746\]](#cite_note-781)[\[490\]](#cite_note-iranintl28march-523)

#### Kurdish–Iranian crisis

Further information: [2026 Kurdish–Iranian crisis](/wiki/2026_Kurdish%E2%80%93Iranian_crisis "2026 Kurdish–Iranian crisis")

According to *[The Wall Street Journal](/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")*, Trump had been open to supporting armed militias, particularly [Kurds in Iran](/wiki/Kurds_in_Iran "Kurds in Iran") that have been [in armed conflict with Tehran for decades](/wiki/Kurdish_separatism_in_Iran "Kurdish separatism in Iran")[\[298\]](#cite_note-wsj3march-329) and have historically been a regional ally of the United States.[\[747\]](#cite_note-782) However, Trump later said he had ruled out sending the Kurds to Iran.[\[748\]](#cite_note-783)

#### Cultural heritage sites

Main article: [Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran War](/wiki/Destruction_of_cultural_heritage_sites_during_the_2026_Iran_War "Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran War")

Multiple historic and cultural sites, including [UNESCO World Heritage Sites](/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Sites "UNESCO World Heritage Sites"), were damaged during the war. The most affected was [Chehel Sotoun](/wiki/Chehel_Sotoun "Chehel Sotoun") and its rich *[ayeneh-kari](/wiki/Ayeneh-kari "Ayeneh-kari")*.[\[749\]](#cite_note-784) On 2 March, a strike on [Arg Square](/wiki/Arg_Square "Arg Square") damaged nearby [Golestan Palace](/wiki/Golestan_Palace "Golestan Palace"), prompting [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") to issue a statement of concern.[\[750\]](#cite_note-785)[\[751\]](#cite_note-786) On 5 March, the [Azadi Sport Complex](/wiki/Azadi_Sport_Complex "Azadi Sport Complex") was bombed.[\[752\]](#cite_note-787) An 8 March strike on [Falak-ol-Aflak](/wiki/Falak-ol-Aflak "Falak-ol-Aflak"), which was marked with a [blue shield emblem](/wiki/Hague_Convention_for_the_Protection_of_Cultural_Property_in_the_Event_of_Armed_Conflict "Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict"), damaged several sections of the site.[\[753\]](#cite_note-ArtNewspaper310-788) Strikes on [Isfahan](/wiki/Isfahan "Isfahan") on 9 March damaged [Naqsh-e Jahan Square](/wiki/Naqsh-e_Jahan_Square "Naqsh-e Jahan Square"), Chehel Sotoun, [Ali Qapu](/wiki/Ali_Qapu "Ali Qapu"), the [Shah Mosque](/wiki/Shah_Mosque_\(Isfahan\) "Shah Mosque (Isfahan)"), [Jameh Mosque](/wiki/Jameh_Mosque_of_Isfahan "Jameh Mosque of Isfahan"), and [Teymouri Hall](/wiki/Natural_History_Museum_of_Isfahan "Natural History Museum of Isfahan").[\[754\]](#cite_note-789)[\[753\]](#cite_note-ArtNewspaper310-788) On 11 March, UNESCO urged protection for Iran's [heritage sites](/wiki/Heritage_sites "Heritage sites") and World Heritage Sites that have been damaged or are under high risk due to the war, alongside other [historic sites](/wiki/Historic_site "Historic site") in Israel, Lebanon, and across the Middle East.[\[755\]](#cite_note-790)

### Israel

Israel declared a nationwide [state of emergency](/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency"), saying that the strikes on Iran were the largest that it had ever launched.[\[216\]](#cite_note-Liebermann-2026-244)[\[756\]](#cite_note-791) Israeli schools and workspaces were closed and public gatherings were canceled.[\[757\]](#cite_note-792)

In the 40 days from the start of the war through the [8 April ceasefire](/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire"), there were a total of 650 missile attacks from Iran to Israel, the majority of which carried cluster munitions. About 16 of the missiles that made it past Israeli missile defenses carried conventional warheads, while 50 had cluster munitions. The attacks killed a total of 24 people, all of them civilians, and resulted in more than 7,000 injuries. Of the 24 civilians killed, 14 were struck by warheads with conventional explosive warheads and 10 were victims of cluster submunitions; two of the deaths were inside a sheltered space, with the other fatalities being people in unprotected areas.[\[758\]](#cite_note-793)

### Palestine

See also: [Gaza war](/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war")

The Israeli [Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories](/wiki/Coordinator_of_Government_Activities_in_the_Territories "Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories") closed multiple aid crossings in the [Gaza Strip](/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip"), specifically interrupting free circulation on the [Egypt–Gaza border](/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Gaza_border "Egypt–Gaza border").[\[759\]](#cite_note-794) Israeli forces suspended [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") humanitarian movements and postponed planned rotations of international humanitarian staff, including medical evacuations and the return of people into Gaza, which the [United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs](/wiki/United_Nations_Office_for_the_Coordination_of_Humanitarian_Affairs "United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs") condemned.[\[760\]](#cite_note-795)

[Israeli settler violence](/wiki/Israeli_settler_violence "Israeli settler violence") against [Palestinians](/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") in [occupied West Bank](/wiki/Occupied_West_Bank "Occupied West Bank") has increased; settlers have taken advantage of curbs on movement imposed during the renewed [Israeli state of emergency](/wiki/Israeli_state_of_emergency "Israeli state of emergency"). The renewed blocking of West Bank roads in the context of the [2026 Lebanon war](/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war") has delayed medics from assisting injured Palestinians.[\[761\]](#cite_note-796) The EU stated on 10 March that the Israeli actions were unacceptable and urged the Israeli authorities to make immediate efforts to prevent the violence against Palestinian civilians under [international law](/wiki/International_law "International law"), warning that "impunity for such acts risks provoking further violence".[\[762\]](#cite_note-797)
