Help Wikipedia 

Or browse the **[Help menu](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Menu "Help:Menu")** or the **[Help directory](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Directory "Help:Directory")** to find help pages.  
For **interactive assistance** related to using and editing Wikipedia, see the **[help desk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Help_desk "Wikipedia:Help desk")** and the **[Teahouse](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:TH/Q "Wikipedia:TH/Q")**.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/OOjs_UI_icon_article-ltr.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_article-ltr.svg.png)

## **Read** or **find** an article

The **[Readers' FAQ](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:FAQ/Readers "Wikipedia:FAQ/Readers")** and our **[about page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:About "Wikipedia:About")** contain the most commonly sought information about Wikipedia.

For simple searches, there is a search bar at the top of every page. Type what you are looking for in the box. Suggested matches will appear in a dropdown list. Select any page in the list to go to that page. Or, select the "Search" button, or press .mw-parser-output .keyboard-key{border:1px solid #aaa;border-radius:0.2em;box-shadow:0.1em 0.1em 0.2em rgba(0,0,0,0.1);background-color:var(--background-color-neutral-subtle,#f8f9fa);background-image:linear-gradient(to bottom,var(--background-color-neutral,#eaecf0),var(--background-color-neutral-subtle,#f8f9fa),var(--background-color-neutral,#eaecf0));color:var(--color-base,#202122);padding:0.1em 0.3em;font-family:inherit;font-size:0.85em}↵ Enter, to go to a full search result. For advanced searches, see **[Help:Searching](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Searching "Help:Searching")**.

There are other ways to browse and explore Wikipedia articles; many can be found at **[Wikipedia:Contents](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contents "Wikipedia:Contents")**. See our **[disclaimer](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:General_disclaimer "Wikipedia:General disclaimer")** for cautions about Wikipedia's limitations.

For **[mobile access](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Mobile_access "Help:Mobile access")**, press the [**mobile view**](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Help:Contents&mobileaction=toggle_view_mobile) link at the very bottom of every [**desktop view**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Contents) page.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr.svg.png)

## **Edit** an article

Contributing is easy: see **[how to edit a page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Editing "Help:Editing")**. For a quick summary on participating, see **[contributing to Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contributing_to_Wikipedia "Wikipedia:Contributing to Wikipedia")**, and for a friendly tutorial, see **[our introduction](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction "Help:Introduction")**. The **[Simplified Ruleset](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Simplified_ruleset "Wikipedia:Simplified ruleset")** outlines our key policies and guidelines, while the **[Simplified Manual of Style](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:SMOS "Wikipedia:SMOS")** and **[Cheatsheet](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Cheatsheet "Help:Cheatsheet")** can remind you of basic **[wiki markup](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Wikitext "Help:Wikitext")**.

**[Be bold](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Be_bold "Wikipedia:Be bold")** in improving articles! When adding facts, please **[provide references](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_referencing/1 "Help:Introduction to referencing/1")** so others may verify them. If you are affiliated with the article subject, please see our **[conflict of interest guide](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Plain_and_simple_conflict_of_interest_guide "Wikipedia:Plain and simple conflict of interest guide")**.

The **[simple guide to vandalism cleanup](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Simple_guide_to_vandalism_cleanup "Help:Simple guide to vandalism cleanup")** can help you undo malicious edits.

If you're looking for places you can help out, the **[Task Center](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Task_Center "Wikipedia:Task Center")** is the place to go, or check out what else is happening at the **[community portal](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "Wikipedia:Community portal")**. You can practice editing and experiment in a **[sandbox](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Sandbox "Wikipedia:Sandbox")**your **[sandbox](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:MyPage/sandbox "Special:MyPage/sandbox")**.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/OOjs_UI_icon_bell.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_bell.svg.png)

## **Report a problem** with an article

If there is a problem with an article about yourself, a family member, a friend or a colleague, please read **[Biographies of living persons/Help](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Biographies_of_living_persons/Help "Wikipedia:Biographies of living persons/Help")**.

If you spot a problem with an article, you can fix it directly, by clicking on the "Edit" link at the top of that page. **[See the "edit an article" section of this page](#edit-heading)** for more information.

If you don't feel ready to fix the article yourself, post a message on the article's **[talk page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Talk_page_guidelines "Wikipedia:Talk page guidelines")**. This will bring the matter to the attention of others who work on that article. There is a "Talk" link at the beginning of *every* article page.

You can **[contact us](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us_-_Readers "Wikipedia:Contact us - Readers")**. If it's an article about you or your organization, see **[Contact us – Subjects](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us_-_Subjects "Wikipedia:Contact us - Subjects")**.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/OOjs_UI_icon_add.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_add.svg.png)

## **Create a new article** or **upload media**

Check **[Your first article](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Your_first_article "Wikipedia:Your first article")** to see if your topic is appropriate, then the **[Article wizard](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard "Wikipedia:Article wizard")** will walk you through creating the article.

Once you have created an article, see **[Writing better articles](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_better_articles "Wikipedia:Writing better articles")** for guidance on how to improve it and what to include (like reference **[citations](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")**).

For contributing images, audio or video files, see the **[Introduction to uploading images](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_uploading_images/1 "Help:Introduction to uploading images/1")**. Then the **[Upload wizard](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:File_Upload_Wizard "Wikipedia:File Upload Wizard")** will guide you through that process.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/OOjs_UI_icon_help.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_help.svg.png)

## **FAQ** and **interactive help**

Answers to common problems can be found at **[frequently asked questions](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:FAQ "Wikipedia:FAQ")**.

Or check out **[where to ask questions or make comments](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Questions "Wikipedia:Questions")**.

New users should seek help at the **[Teahouse](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Teahouse "Wikipedia:Teahouse")** if they're having problems while editing Wikipedia.

More complex questions can be posed at the **[Help desk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Help_desk "Wikipedia:Help desk")**. Volunteers will respond as soon as they're able.

Or [**ask for help on your talk page**](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:MyTalk&action=edit&section=new&preload=Help:Contents/helpmepreload&preloadtitle=Help+me%21) and a volunteer will visit you there!

You can get live help with editing in the **[help chatroom](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:IRC_help_disclaimer "Wikipedia:IRC help disclaimer")**.

For help with technical issues, ask at the **[Village pump](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Village_pump_\(technical\) "Wikipedia:Village pump (technical)")**.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/OOjs_UI_icon_references-ltr.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_references-ltr.svg.png)

## **Factual questions**

If **[searching Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search "Special:Search")** has not answered your question (*for example, questions like "Which country has the world's largest fishing fleet?"*), try the **[Reference Desk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reference_desk "Wikipedia:Reference desk")**. Volunteers there will attempt to answer your questions on any topic, or point you toward the information you need.

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/OOjs_UI_icon_lightbulb.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_lightbulb.svg.png)

## **Tip** of the day

**Sister projects & interwiki linking**

If you want to write a [dictionary](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictionary "Dictionary") definition, [recipe](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recipe "Recipe") or [quotation](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quotation "Quotation") archive, consider using one of Wikipedia's [sister projects](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Sister_projects "Wikipedia:Sister projects"), such as [Wiktionary](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiktionary "Wiktionary") or [Wikiquote](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikiquote "Wikiquote"). These are more specialised, as they focus on a particular type of page. Links can be made to these pages by adding the project name as a [namespace](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Namespace "Wikipedia:Namespace") ("Wikiquote:", "Wikibooks:", "Wiktionary:"), or using the shortcuts ("Q:", "B:", and "Wikt:", respectively). .mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap}.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li{display:inline-block}.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li span{font-weight:bold}.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li>div{display:inline-block;vertical-align:middle;padding:6px 4px}.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li>div:first-child{text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .sister-projects-wikt-icon-dark{display:none}@media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .sister-projects-wikt-icon-dark{display:inline}html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .sister-projects-wikt-icon-light{display:none}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .sister-projects-wikt-icon-dark{display:inline}html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .sister-projects-wikt-icon-light{display:none}}@media(min-width:360px){.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li{width:33%;min-width:20em;white-space:nowrap;flex:1 0 25%}.mw-parser-output #sister-projects-list li>div:first-child{min-width:50px}} Wikipedia is written by volunteer editors and hosted by the [Wikimedia Foundation](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Foundation "Wikimedia Foundation"), a non-profit organization that also hosts a range of other volunteer [projects](https://wikimediafoundation.org/our-work/wikimedia-projects/ "foundationsite:our-work/wikimedia-projects/"):

Introduction to Wikipedia

**[Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia") is [made](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges") by [people like **you**](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikipedians "Wikipedia:Wikipedians").**

This page takes you through a set of tutorials aimed at *complete newcomers* who wish to contribute. It covers all the basics, and each tutorial takes only a few minutes, so you can become a proficient [Wikipedian](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikipedians "Wikipedia:Wikipedians") quickly.

[Get started](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_Wikipedia "Help:Introduction to Wikipedia")  
[Policies and Guidelines](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_policies_and_guidelines/1 "Help:Introduction to policies and guidelines/1")

* * *

  

**There are two methods to edit Wikipedia:**  

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Source_editor_logo.svg/250px-Source_editor_logo.svg.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_editing_with_Wiki_Markup/1 "Help:Introduction to editing with Wiki Markup/1")

The **[wiki markup source editor](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Wikitext "Help:Wikitext")** shows the underlying page source code. It works like a plain text file, indicating links and other items using simple code like this: `[[Earth]]`.

[Editing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_editing_with_Wiki_Markup/1 "Help:Introduction to editing with Wiki Markup/1")  
[Referencing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_referencing_with_Wiki_Markup/1 "Help:Introduction to referencing with Wiki Markup/1")  
[Images](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_images_with_Wiki_Markup/1 "Help:Introduction to images with Wiki Markup/1")  
[Tables](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_tables_with_Wiki_Markup/1 "Help:Introduction to tables with Wiki Markup/1")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/VisualEditor-logo.svg/250px-VisualEditor-logo.svg.png)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_editing_with_VisualEditor/1 "Help:Introduction to editing with VisualEditor/1")

**[VisualEditor](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:VisualEditor "Help:VisualEditor")** is the easier way of editing that works more like a word processor and hides the underlying source code. Links and other items are edited using toolbar and pop-up interfaces.

[Editing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_editing_with_VisualEditor/1 "Help:Introduction to editing with VisualEditor/1")  
[Referencing](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_referencing_with_VisualEditor/1 "Help:Introduction to referencing with VisualEditor/1")  
[Images](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_images_with_VisualEditor/1 "Help:Introduction to images with VisualEditor/1")  
[Tables](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_tables_with_VisualEditor/1 "Help:Introduction to tables with VisualEditor/1")

[Talk pages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_talk_pages/1 "Help:Introduction to talk pages/1")  
[Navigating Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_navigating_Wikipedia/1 "Help:Introduction to navigating Wikipedia/1")  
[Manual of Style](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_the_Manual_of_Style "Help:Introduction to the Manual of Style")  
[Conclusion](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction/Conclusion "Help:Introduction/Conclusion")

  
[View all as single page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction/All "Help:Introduction/All")

This page provides a listing of current collaborations, tasks, and news about English Wikipedia. New to [Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia")? See the [contributing to Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contributing_to_Wikipedia "Wikipedia:Contributing to Wikipedia") page or [our tutorial](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Introduction "Help:Introduction") for everything you need to know to get started. For a listing of [internal project pages](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:ADMINP "Wikipedia:ADMINP") of interest, see the [department directory](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Department_directory "Wikipedia:Department directory").

## Community bulletin board

This section is [transcluded](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Transclusion "Help:Transclusion") from [Wikipedia:Community bulletin board](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_bulletin_board "Wikipedia:Community bulletin board"). ([edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Community_bulletin_board&action=edit) | [history](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Community_bulletin_board&action=history))

show

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/Ambox_notice.png/20px-Ambox_notice.png) How to add to the community bulletin board

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1d/Information_icon4.svg/40px-Information_icon4.svg.png)

The community bulletin board has 2 sections that can be used by Wikipedians for announcements: "Events and projects" and "WikiProject notices". In general, keep it **concise** (under 2 lines), refrain from **fancy formatting**, and new entries should be placed at the **top** of their section.

*   Before editing, make sure you are on [Wikipedia:Community bulletin board](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_bulletin_board "Wikipedia:Community bulletin board"), not Wikipedia:Community portal, where the board is transcluded.
*   **Events and projects**: In this section, only organized events, projects, and/or competitions should be listed. These are organized by how often they occur:
    *   The **Yearly** section is for uncommon events, like events that only occur every year, once, or irregularly. The **Monthly** section is for events that occur each month, or are always ongoing.
*   **WikiProject notices**: In this section, any announcement, request for help or other notice from a WikiProject should be listed here.
    *   Entries should be signed, and ordered from newest to oldest.
    *   Entries are to be removed after a period of **6 months**.

Welcome to the **community bulletin board**, which is a page used for announcements from [WikiProjects](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikiproject "Wikipedia:Wikiproject") and other groups. Included here are coordinated efforts, events, projects, and other general announcements.

*   [Dashboard](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Dashboard "Wikipedia:Dashboard")
*   [News](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:News "Wikipedia:News")
*   [Task Center](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Task_Center "Wikipedia:Task Center")
*   [Goings-on](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Goings-on "Wikipedia:Goings-on")
*   [Meetups](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Meetups "Wikipedia:Meetups")
*   [In the media](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikipedia_in_the_media "Wikipedia:Wikipedia in the media")
*   [Mailing lists](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Mailing_lists "Wikipedia:Mailing lists")

**Monthly or continuous events**

*   **[Monthly contest, WikiProject Military history](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Military_history/Contest "Wikipedia:WikiProject Military history/Contest").** The contest department of the Military history WikiProject aims to motivate increased quality in military history articles by offering a form of friendly competition for project members making improvements to them. The primary contest available is a simple rolling competition that awards points for improving articles. The contest runs from the first to last day of each month.
*   **Guild of Copy Editors: drive**. **The** [May 2026 backlog drive](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Guild_of_Copy_Editors/Backlog_elimination_drives/May_2026 "Wikipedia:WikiProject Guild of Copy Editors/Backlog elimination drives/May 2026") **is a one-month-long effort by the [**Guild of Copy Editors**](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Guild_of_Copy_Editors "Wikipedia:WikiProject Guild of Copy Editors") to reduce the backlog of articles that require copy editing: those carrying the {{[copy edit](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Copy_edit "Template:Copy edit")}} tag (also {{[awkward](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Awkward "Template:Awkward")}}, {{[copy edit section](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Copy_edit_section "Template:Copy edit section")}}, {{[inappropriate person](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Inappropriate_person "Template:Inappropriate person")}}, {{[copy edit inline](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Copy_edit_inline "Template:Copy edit inline")}}, and their redirects), and those listed on the [GOCE Requests page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:GOCE/REQ "Wikipedia:GOCE/REQ"). It began on 1 May, 00:00 (UTC), and will end on 31 May, 23:59 (UTC).**

**Weekly highlight**

*   The [Article guidance](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Article_guidance "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Article guidance") team invites experienced editors of [pilot Wikipedias](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Article_guidance/Pilot_wikis_and_collaborators "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Article guidance/Pilot wikis and collaborators")—Arabic, Bangla, Japanese, Portuguese, Persian, Turkish, Simple English, Spanish, and French—to help translate and adapt [sample outlines](https://b24e11a4f1.catalyst.wmcloud.org/wiki/Category:Pages_using_article_guidance). These outlines will guide editors in creating clear, well-structured, and policy-compliant articles when using [the feature](https://b24e11a4f1.catalyst.wmcloud.org/wiki/Special:NewArticle) once it is launched in May 2026. [Simple instructions](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Article_guidance#Adapting_a_sample_outline_in_a_Wikipedia "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Article guidance") on how to translate and adapt the outlines are available.

**Updates for editors**

*   The [Product and Technology Advisory Council](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Product_and_Technology_Advisory_Council "m:Special:MyLanguage/Product and Technology Advisory Council") has published [draft recommendations](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Product_and_Technology_Advisory_Council/May_2026_draft_PTAC_recommendation_for_feedback "m:Special:MyLanguage/Product and Technology Advisory Council/May 2026 draft PTAC recommendation for feedback") on a model that affiliates can follow when contributing to the technical space. Community members are invited to provide feedback on the recommendation until May 8th [on the talk page](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Talk:Product_and_Technology_Advisory_Council/May_2026_draft_PTAC_recommendation_for_feedback "m:Talk:Product and Technology Advisory Council/May 2026 draft PTAC recommendation for feedback").
*   The number of available thumbnail size preferences in MediaWiki is being reduced to three standardized options—Small (180px), Regular (250px), and Large (400px), as part of ongoing efforts to improve performance and reduce strain on thumbnail services. As a result, existing preferences will be mapped to the nearest new size (for example, smaller selections like 120px or 150px will render at 180px, while larger ones like 300px or 360px will render at 400px). The preferences interface will soon be updated to reflect these changes, and users who wish to opt out or provide feedback can do so. [\[1\]](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T424909)
*   From now on, even when a permission expires automatically, users will receive an Echo notification similar to the standard notification for permission changes. There is a difference between this and [Global reminder bot](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Global_reminder_bot "m:Special:MyLanguage/Global reminder bot") in that the latter reminds users a week *before* the rights are due to expire, so that they can renew the rights.
*   ![Recurrent item](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Reload_icon_with_two_arrows.svg/20px-Reload_icon_with_two_arrows.svg.png) View all 32 community-submitted tasks that were [resolved last week](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/Recently_resolved_community_tasks "m:Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/Recently resolved community tasks"). For example, the problem where the ULS language selector in [Special:Translate](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Translate "m:Special:Translate") would scroll vertically when it shouldn't, has been resolved. Previously, when users opened the "Translate to English" dropdown and typed certain inputs, the dialog would scroll vertically by a few pixels even when there was enough space to display all results. The dropdown no longer shifts unnecessarily when filtering languages. [\[2\]](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T358864)
*   The [Global Watchlist](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:GlobalWatchlist "m:Special:GlobalWatchlist"), which lets you view your watchlists from multiple wikis on a single page, continues to improve. For example, watchlists for Wikibase sites such as [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/ "d:") now support [EntitySchema](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Extension:EntitySchema "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Extension:EntitySchema") elements for better tracking. The Live Updates mode now refreshes the special page every 60 seconds to comply with the updated [global API rate limits](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia APIs/Rate limits") for improved real-time responsiveness. Additionally, a directionality bug that displayed links as "changes 3" instead of "3 changes" in mixed-direction lists has been fixed. [\[3\]](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T415450)[\[4\]](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T424422)[\[5\]](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T418091)

**Updates for technical contributors**

*   The second phase of [global API rate limits](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia APIs/Rate limits") has been rolled out to reduce the [impact of AI crawlers](https://diff.wikimedia.org/2026/03/26/quo-vadis-crawlers-progress-and-whats-next-on-safeguarding-our-infrastructure/ "diffblog:2026/03/26/quo-vadis-crawlers-progress-and-whats-next-on-safeguarding-our-infrastructure/") and ensure fair, sustainable access to Wikimedia resources, prioritising human and mission-aligned traffic. [Limits](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits#Limits "mw:Special:MyLanguage/Wikimedia APIs/Rate limits") have been shifted from per-hour to per-minute, producing smoother traffic patterns and more predictable API load. Community users are not expected to be affected, and no action is required. Early indications show some User-Agent-based requestors are adjusting behaviour, and around 64% of automated API traffic has been identified. Monitoring continues, and Wikimedia Enterprise remains available for commercial support.
*   ![Recurrent item](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Reload_icon_with_two_arrows.svg/20px-Reload_icon_with_two_arrows.svg.png) Detailed code updates later this week: [MediaWiki](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/MediaWiki_1.47/wmf.1 "mw:MediaWiki 1.47/wmf.1")

***[Tech news](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News "m:Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News")** prepared by [Tech News writers](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/Writers "m:Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/Writers") and posted by [bot](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/User:MediaWiki_message_delivery "m:Special:MyLanguage/User:MediaWiki message delivery") • [Contribute](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News#contribute "m:Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News") • [Translate](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/2026/19 "m:Special:MyLanguage/Tech/News/2026/19") • [Get help](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Tech "m:Tech") • [Give feedback](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Talk:Tech/News "m:Talk:Tech/News") • [Subscribe or unsubscribe](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Global_message_delivery/Targets/Tech_ambassadors "m:Global message delivery/Targets/Tech ambassadors").*

hide

**Sister projects & interwiki linking**

If you want to write a [dictionary](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictionary "Dictionary") definition, [recipe](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recipe "Recipe") or [quotation](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quotation "Quotation") archive, consider using one of Wikipedia's [sister projects](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Sister_projects "Wikipedia:Sister projects"), such as [Wiktionary](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiktionary "Wiktionary") or [Wikiquote](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikiquote "Wikiquote"). These are more specialised, as they focus on a particular type of page. This wizard will guide you through a questionnaire prompting you for the appropriate copyright and sourcing information for each file. Please ensure you understand [copyright](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Copyrights "Wikipedia:Copyrights") and the [image use policy](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Image_use_policy "Wikipedia:Image use policy") before proceeding.

**You do not have JavaScript enabled**

Sorry, in order to use this uploading script, JavaScript must be enabled. You can still use the plain [Special:Upload](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Upload "Special:Upload") page to upload files to the English Wikipedia without JavaScript.

**You are not currently logged in.**

Sorry, in order to use this uploading script and to upload files, you need to be logged in with your named account. Please **[log in](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Wikipedia%3AFile+Upload+Wizard&returntoquery=withJS%3DMediaWiki%253AFileUploadWizard.js)** and then try again.

**Your account has not become confirmed yet.**

Sorry, in order to upload files on the English Wikipedia, you need to have a [confirmed account](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:AUTOCONFIRM "Wikipedia:AUTOCONFIRM"). Normally, your account will become confirmed automatically once you have made 10 edits and four days have passed since you created it.

You may already be able to upload files on the [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/ "commons:"), but you can't do it on the English Wikipedia just yet. If the file you want to upload has a free license, please go to Commons and upload it there.

**Important note:** if you don't want to wait until you are autoconfirmed, you may ask somebody else to upload a file for you at [Wikipedia:Files for upload](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Files_for_upload "Wikipedia:Files for upload").

In very rare cases an administrator may make your account confirmed manually through a request at [Wikipedia:Requests for permissions/Confirmed](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requests_for_permissions/Confirmed "Wikipedia:Requests for permissions/Confirmed").

## Step 2: Describe your file

Please provide a clear, descriptive name by which your file will be known on Wikipedia.

 

  
This name must be unique across the whole of Wikipedia, so please make it informative and easy to recognize.  
It's no problem to use a fairly long name. It may also include spaces, commas and most other punctuation marks.  
Please also note that file names are case sensitive (with the exception of the first letter).  
**Good:** "City of London, skyline from London City Hall, Oct 2008.jpg". **Bad**: "Skyline.jpg", "DSC0001234.jpg".

Sorry, a few special characters and character combinations cannot be used in the filename for technical reasons. This goes especially for **# < > \[ \] | : { } /**  and **\~~~**. Your filename has been modified to avoid these. Please check if it is okay now.

The filename you chose seems to be very short, or overly generic. Please don't use:

*   Titles that consist only of very generic descriptive words (e.g. "Sunset.jpg", "Townhall.jpg")
*   Titles that consist only of a person's first or last name, when that name is likely to be shared by many others (e.g. "John.jpg", "Miller.jpg")
*   Titles that consist of mere numbers, of the kind often produced by digital cameras ("DSC\_001234", "IMGP0345"), or random strings like those sometimes found on the web ("30996951316264l.jpg")

**Thank you for offering to upload a free work.**

Wikipedia loves free files. However, we would love it even more if you uploaded them on our sister project, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/ "commons:"). Files uploaded on Commons can be used immediately here on Wikipedia as well as on all its sister projects. Uploading files on Commons works just the same as here. **Do not** use this section for any of the following:

*   a scan or photograph you made of a painting, drawing, printed page or other item originally created by somebody else. The copyright belongs to the original creator, not to you.
*   a screenshot or other kind of capture of a video, computer screen, TV programme or other kind of visual media.
*   a picture you created by modifying or copying some other picture or by combining several preexisting pictures made by somebody else.
*   a picture given to you by somebody else.
*   a picture you found somewhere on the Internet.

Editors who falsely declare such items as their "own work" **will be blocked from editing**.

**Please don't upload it.**

Really, please don't. Even if you think it would make for a great addition to an article. We really take these copyright rules very seriously on Wikipedia. Note that media is *assumed* to be fully-copyrighted unless shown otherwise; the burden is on the uploader.

In particular, please don't upload:

*   any file you simply found on some website, without knowing who its author or copyright owner is.
*   any file you found somewhere, even if you have good reason to believe it has a copyright owner who would not mind us using it, but you don't have an explicit licensing statement from them.
*   any file that was released for publicity purposes by its owners but doesn't have a fully-free license for free re-use for all purposes.
*   any file credited to a commercial image agency, such as Reuters, AP or Getty Images. Such files normally cannot be used even under the "Fair Use" rules, except in rare cases.
*   any file that is licensed for use exclusively on Wikipedia, or is free except that the free license excludes commercial use.

If you are in any doubt, please ask some experienced editors for advice before uploading. People will be happy to assist you at [Wikipedia:Media copyright questions](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Media_copyright_questions "Wikipedia:Media copyright questions"). Thank you.

See [Wikipedia:Picture tutorial](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Picture_tutorial "Wikipedia:Picture tutorial") for more detailed help on how to insert and position images in pages.

Please leave your feedback, comments, bug reports or suggestions on the [talk page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia_talk:File_upload_wizard "Wikipedia talk:File upload wizard").

This page contains a list of [special pages](/wiki/Help:Special_page "Help:Special page"). Most of the content of these pages is automatically generated and cannot be edited. To suggest a change to the parts that *can* be edited, find the appropriate text on [Special:AllMessages](/wiki/Special:AllMessages "Special:AllMessages") and then request your change on the talk page of the message (using {{[editprotected](/wiki/Template:Edit_fully-protected "Template:Edit fully-protected")}} to draw the attention of administrators).

You can also see what message names are used on a page by adding `?uselang=qqx` to the end of its URL, e.g. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:SpecialPages?uselang=qqx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:SpecialPages?uselang=qqx) will show `(specialpages-summary)` in place of this message, which allows you to find [MediaWiki:Specialpages-summary](/wiki/MediaWiki:Specialpages-summary "MediaWiki:Specialpages-summary").

For an index of special pages, see [Help:SpecialPages](/wiki/Help:SpecialPages#Alphabetical_order "Help:SpecialPages").

See also [the list by category](https://tools.wmflabs.org/bambots/cwb/bycat/Israel.html) and [the tool's wiki page](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:CleanupWorklistBot "User:CleanupWorklistBot").

*   ***[Expand](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_better_articles "Wikipedia:Writing better articles")* :** [Ayala Procaccia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayala_Procaccia "Ayala Procaccia"), [Diamond industry in Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_industry_in_Israel "Diamond industry in Israel"), [Edna Arbel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edna_Arbel "Edna Arbel"), [Levin Kipnis](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levin_Kipnis "Levin Kipnis"), [Rami Kleinstein](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Kleinstein "Rami Kleinstein"), [Sephardic Haredim](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardic_Haredim "Sephardic Haredim"), [Zman Tel Aviv](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zman_Tel_Aviv "Zman Tel Aviv"), [Nachum Heiman](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nachum_Heiman "Nachum Heiman"), [Public Defence (Israel)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Defence_\(Israel\) "Public Defence (Israel)"), [Prisoner of Zion](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_Zion "Prisoner of Zion"), [Trial of Benjamin Netanyahu](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Benjamin_Netanyahu "Trial of Benjamin Netanyahu"), [Day to Mark the Departure and Expulsion of Jews from the Arab Countries and Iran](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_to_Mark_the_Departure_and_Expulsion_of_Jews_from_the_Arab_Countries_and_Iran "Day to Mark the Departure and Expulsion of Jews from the Arab Countries and Iran"), [Pre-Modern Aliyah](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah#Pre-modern_aliyah "Aliyah")  
    See also *[Articles needing translation from Hebrew Wikipedia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Articles_needing_translation_from_Hebrew_Wikipedia "Category:Articles needing translation from Hebrew Wikipedia")*.
*   ***[Geographical coordinates](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Geographical_coordinates "Wikipedia:WikiProject Geographical coordinates")* :** Add geographic coordinates to *[Israel articles missing geocoordinate data](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Israel_articles_missing_geocoordinate_data "Category:Israel articles missing geocoordinate data")*.
*   ***[Infobox](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Infoboxes "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Infoboxes")* :** Add infoboxes to *[Israel articles needing infoboxes](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Israel_articles_needing_infoboxes "Category:Israel articles needing infoboxes")*.
*   ***[Maintain](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Maintenance "Wikipedia:Maintenance")* :** See *[Israel articles needing attention](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Israel_articles_needing_attention "Category:Israel articles needing attention")*.
*   ***[Map](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Maps "Wikipedia:WikiProject Maps")* :** See discussion at [Module:Location map/data/Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Module:Location_map/data/Israel "Module:Location map/data/Israel"). Add maps to articles in *[Wikipedia requested maps in Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Wikipedia_requested_maps_in_Israel "Category:Wikipedia requested maps in Israel")*.
*   ***[NPOV](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Neutral_point_of_view "Wikipedia:Neutral point of view")* :** [Jewish exodus from Arab and Muslim countries](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_Arab_and_Muslim_countries "Jewish exodus from Arab and Muslim countries")
*   ***[Photo](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requested_pictures "Wikipedia:Requested pictures")* :** Add pictures to articles in *[Wikipedia requested photographs in Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Wikipedia_requested_photographs_in_Israel "Category:Wikipedia requested photographs in Israel")*.

## Articles for Operation Epic Fury/Operation Roaring Lion/Operation True Promise IV?

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Articles for Operation Epic Fury/Operation Roaring Lion/Operation True Promise IV?")\]

It was [previously suggested](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war/Archive_10#Split "Talk:2026 Iran war/Archive 10") that [2026 Iran war § First week (28 February – 6 March)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war#First_week_\(28_February_–_6_March\) "2026 Iran war") be split into its own article. This proposal wasn't successful, however, that section remains the largest one under hostilities and a split would help with the article size.

Perhaps it would be warranted to make a separate article specifically for the initial military operations, namely [Operation Epic Fury](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Epic_Fury "Operation Epic Fury") and [Operation Roaring Lion](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Roaring_Lion "Operation Roaring Lion") by the US and Israel respectively, and [Operation True Promise IV](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_True_Promise_IV "Operation True Promise IV") by Iran in retaliation, similar to how there's an article for [Operation Midnight Hammer](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Midnight_Hammer "Operation Midnight Hammer") which is distinct from that of the [Twelve-Day War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve-Day_War "Twelve-Day War").

Since the US-Israeli operations were conducted jointly, I'm unsure whether a single article or two separate ones for each operation would be most appropriate. If they would share an article, I'm unsure what the title would be. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [16:06, 9 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260409160600-Articles_for_Operation_Epic_Fury/Operation_Roaring_Lion/Operation_True_Promise_I "27 days ago")\[reply\]

These articles could also encompass some of the prelude, particularly the planning of the operations and the disinformation efforts to obscure preparations, in addition to the actual details of their execution. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [10:43, 10 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260410104300-Scyrme-20260409160600 "26 days ago")\[reply\]

@[Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") How about this "Operation Epic Fury/Operation Roaring Lion" as one with that exact title. With the slash [Avishai11](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Avishai11 "User:Avishai11") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Avishai11 "User talk:Avishai11")) [19:41, 10 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Avishai11-20260410194100-Scyrme-20260410104300 "26 days ago")\[reply\]

That had occurred to me, but it didn't seem appropriate so I didn't suggest it. There a few article which have a slashed title like this, but I'm only aware of this being done for cases where there's a single topic which officially has a joint bilingual name such as [Biel/Bienne](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biel/Bienne "Biel/Bienne") or [Aoraki / Mount Cook](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aoraki_/_Mount_Cook "Aoraki / Mount Cook") (most, if not all, of these are located in either Switzerland or New Zealand). In general, titles using slashes tend to be renamed to ones without slashes. For example, [UV/VIS spectroscopy](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UV/VIS_spectroscopy "UV/VIS spectroscopy") was renamed [Ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraviolet%E2%80%93visible_spectroscopy "Ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy") and [Sticky end/blunt end](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sticky_end/blunt_end "Sticky end/blunt end") was renamed [Sticky and blunt ends](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sticky_and_blunt_ends "Sticky and blunt ends"). I don't know whether this is because there's a consensus or guideline that encourages doing so. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [19:56, 10 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260410195600-Avishai11-20260410194100 "26 days ago")\[reply\]

The word count is ~12,300 words, which is within the 9,000-15,000 range for @media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .inline-quote-talk{color:#00B785}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .inline-quote-talk{color:#00B785}}.mw-parser-output .inline-quote-talk{font-family:Georgia,"DejaVu Serif",serif;color:#008560;quotes:none}.mw-parser-output .inline-quote-talk-italic{font-family:inherit;font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output .inline-quote-talk-marks{quotes:"\\"""\\""}the scope of a topic can sometimes justify the added reading material ([WP:SIZERULE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:SIZERULE "Wikipedia:SIZERULE")), however [Lfstevens](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Lfstevens "User:Lfstevens") noted that it would probably be a good idea to trim the article down enough that using `#invoke` to invoke the citation module instead of using citation templates would no longer be necessary. While it makes no difference to how the references appear to readers, tools like [ProveIt](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:ProveIt "Wikipedia:ProveIt") and the [citation expander](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_expander "Wikipedia:Citation expander") gadgets don't work as intended with references that use `#invoke` rather than a template, which means module-invoking references generally have to be maintained largely manually.

To some extent, all refs require some manual maintenance as the automated tools don't always get it right, and module-invoking references will still be subject to automatic error-checking mechanisms which are built into the templates since it's the module that implements them, which makes identifying references that need maintenance easy, but certain tools like the two common ones I mentioned only work properly when citations use templates rather than invoking the module. In my experience ProveIt interprets module-invoking references the same way as plain text references and citation expander just ignores them completely. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [22:16, 22 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260422221600-HarvardJock-20260422215000 "14 days ago")\[reply\]

## Image at the top

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Image at the top")\]

Why doesn't this article have a typical quadrant with actual photos from the conflict? The image as it is conveys pretty much no useful information and at this point. There are so many markets, it's impossible to even discern where they are meant to represent. It's been over a month, surely we have actual images from the conflict now. [Dunnowy123](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Dunnowy123&action=edit&redlink=1 "User:Dunnowy123 (page does not exist)") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Dunnowy123 "User talk:Dunnowy123")) [12:43, 17 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Dunnowy123-20260417124300-Image_at_the_top "19 days ago")\[reply\]

I think a more beneficial proposal is to create two separate boxes, one which depicts locations struck and another being the aforementioned quadrant which would include pictures relevant to the conflict. The actual layout of the said boxes would depend on what we want to prioritize, I for one, think that placing the quadrant with the images has to be placed on top of the box with the depiction of strikes. [Lothengrun de Spigel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Lothengrun_de_Spigel "User:Lothengrun de Spigel") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Lothengrun_de_Spigel "User talk:Lothengrun de Spigel")) [15:45, 17 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Lothengrun_de_Spigel-20260417154500-Dunnowy123-20260417124300 "19 days ago")\[reply\]

The technical reason is the `|image=` parameter is occupied by {{[2026 Iran war map](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:2026_Iran_war_map "Template:2026 Iran war map")}} and {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} only supports a single image. Not all conflicts have a collage of images in the infobox. [Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war_\(2022%E2%80%93present\) "Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)"), for example, also has a map.

It was decided early on to include a map of strikes, presumably because at the time no photos were available on Wikimedia Commons. Replacing it with a simplified map that's clearer to interpret was proposed later, but that discussion ultimately didn't lead to anything being done. Some editors objected to simplifying the map because the map can be opened in fullscreen by clicking on it, allowing readers to zoom in. Personally, I don't think readers should have pause reading the article to open the map to fullscreen to pan/scroll to see the key details, and I argued as much in that discussion. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [16:35, 17 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260417163500-Dunnowy123-20260417124300 "19 days ago")\[reply\]

Instead of using `|image=` why not use `|map=` for the depiction of strikes and `|image=` for images? Or am I mistaken to think this? [Lothengrun de Spigel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Lothengrun_de_Spigel "User:Lothengrun de Spigel") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Lothengrun_de_Spigel "User talk:Lothengrun de Spigel")) [19:08, 17 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Lothengrun_de_Spigel-20260417190800-Scyrme-20260417163500 "19 days ago")\[reply\]

There is no `|map=` parameter. The infobox can generate a map if coordinates are provided to `|coordinates=`, but this wouldn't be the same and isn't suitable for what's needed.

The documentation for {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} (which is what {{[2026 Iran war infobox](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:2026_Iran_war_infobox "Template:2026 Iran war infobox")}}) uses) mentions `|mapframe-custom=` which can supposedly accept a template that generates a [mapframe](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Mapframe "Wikipedia:Mapframe"), which is essentially what {{[2026 Iran war map](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:2026_Iran_war_map "Template:2026 Iran war map")}} is, but that part of the documentation is a transclusion from the documentation for {{[Infobox mapframe](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_mapframe "Template:Infobox mapframe")}}; it's not specific to what {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} actually supports. In theory, it should support everything described there, but as far as I can tell, {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} does not actually support `|mapframe-custom=`. I could be wrong though, since {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} is almost entirely actually handled by [Module:Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Module:Infobox_military_conflict "Module:Infobox military conflict") rather than by the template itself. I'm not sufficiently skilled in Lua to understand how the module works. If it were just a template I could figure out how it works, but modules are mostly beyond me.

If `|mapframe-custom=` *does* work, I don't understand how to use it properly. Based on the documentation, it seems like the infobox should display what's provided to that parameter if `|mapframe=yes` is set to allow it to work. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [19:52, 17 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260417195200-Lothengrun_de_Spigel-20260417190800 "19 days ago")\[reply\]

@[Dunnowy123](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Dunnowy123&action=edit&redlink=1 "User:Dunnowy123 (page does not exist)") and [Lothengrun de Spigel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Lothengrun_de_Spigel "User:Lothengrun de Spigel"): I pursued this further over at [Template talk:Infobox mapframe § "mapframe-custom" parameter](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template_talk:Infobox_mapframe#"mapframe-custom"_parameter "Template talk:Infobox mapframe") and received a helpful suggestion from [The Equalizer](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:The_Equalizer "User:The Equalizer"), which has now been implemented in the sandbox for {{[2026 Iran war infobox](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:2026_Iran_war_infobox "Template:2026 Iran war infobox")}}. A comparison between the current and sandbox versions of the infobox can be seen in the collapsible box in the section below. The sandbox version has an image collage in `|image=` and uses `|notes=` to provide {{[2026 Iran war map](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:2026_Iran_war_map "Template:2026 Iran war map")}} at the bottom of the infobox. This would allow having both a map and an image collage without having to provide specific coordinates to allow the use of `|mapframe=`.

Note, the infobox has a long list of notes and references which are transcluded with it, which are also contained in the collapsible box. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [16:55, 25 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260425165500-Image_at_the_top "11 days ago")\[reply\]

Another note, the image collage included in the sandbox is just for demonstration. It's one that's used on Wikimedia Commons, but we don't necessarily have to use it here in this article. We could make a new one or use {{[Photo montage](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Photo_montage "Template:Photo montage")}} instead. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [16:58, 25 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260425165800-Scyrme-20260425165500 "11 days ago")\[reply\]

Date

28 February 2026 (2026-02-28) – present  
(2 months, 1 week and 2 days)

Location

*   [West Asia](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia")[\[i\]](#cite_note-19)
*   [Indian Ocean](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean")[\[j\]](#cite_note-21)

Status

Stalemate;[\[12\]](#cite_note-22)[\[13\]](#cite_note-23) Temporary ceasefire between [Iran and the United States since 8 April 2026](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire "2026 Iran war ceasefire") and [Hezbollah and Israel since 16 April 2026](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire "2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire")  

*   Assassination of [top Iranian officials](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Iranian_officials_killed_during_the_2026_Iran_war "List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war") in the U.S.–Israeli stikes, including [Ali Khamenei](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Khamenei "Assassination of Ali Khamenei") and [Ali Larijani](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Ali_Larijani "Assassination of Ali Larijani")
*   Iranian retaliation by [striking Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Israel "2026 Iranian strikes on Israel"), US bases, and [US-allied Arab countries](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iranian_strikes_on_Arab_countries "2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries")
*   [Iranian closure](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis#Iranian_blockade "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis") of the Strait of Hormuz
*   Election of [Mojtaba Khamenei](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei "Mojtaba Khamenei") as the Supreme Leader of Iran
*   [Escalation of the Israel–Hezbollah conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Lebanon_war "2026 Lebanon war")
*   [Global economic disruption](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war") and [fuel crisis](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_fuel_crisis "2026 Iran war fuel crisis")
*   [U.S. naval blockade of Iran](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran "2026 United States naval blockade of Iran")

Casualties and losses

*   **Per US and Israel:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)United States:
        *   15 soldiers killed[\[k\]](#cite_note-25)
        *   538 military personnel wounded
        *   17+ sites damaged[\[15\]](#cite_note-26)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Flag_of_Israel.svg/40px-Flag_of_Israel.svg.png)Israel:
        *   17 soldiers and 1 contractor killed[\[l\]](#cite_note-27)
        *   28 civilians killed[\[m\]](#cite_note-28)
        *   8,524 injured
        *   743 military personnel wounded
        *   $11.52 billion in economic damage[\[16\]](#cite_note-29)

Casualties and losses

*   **Per US and Israel:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)United States:
        *   15 soldiers killed[\[l\]](#cite_note-118)
        *   538 military personnel wounded
        *   17+ sites damaged[\[15\]](#cite_note-119)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Flag_of_Israel.svg/40px-Flag_of_Israel.svg.png)Israel:
        *   18 soldiers and 1 contractor killed[\[m\]](#cite_note-120)
        *   28 civilians killed[\[n\]](#cite_note-121)
        *   8,594 injured (including 760 military personnel)

* * *

*   **Per Iran:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)United States:
        *   12+ [radar systems](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar "Radar") and [satellite terminals](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satcom_\(satellite\) "Satcom (satellite)") destroyed or damaged[\[16\]](#cite_note-122)
        *   Multiple [AN/TPY-2s](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/TPY-2_transportable_radar "AN/TPY-2 transportable radar") destroyed or damaged[\[17\]](#cite_note-123)
        *   1 [THAAD](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_High_Altitude_Area_Defense "Terminal High Altitude Area Defense") radar destroyed or seriously damaged[\[18\]](#cite_note-124)
        *   1 [AN/FPS-132](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_State_Phased_Array_Radar_System "Solid State Phased Array Radar System"), 1 [AN/TPS-59](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/FPS-117 "AN/FPS-117"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-Amoah0305-125) 1 [AN/FPS-117](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/FPS-117 "AN/FPS-117"),[\[20\]](#cite_note-126) 1 [AN/MPQ-64](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/MPQ-64_Sentinel "AN/MPQ-64 Sentinel") destroyed[\[21\]](#cite_note-127)
        *   1 [MIM-104 Patriot](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIM-104_Patriot "MIM-104 Patriot") AN/MPQ-65 radar and 1 [AN/TPS-75](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/TPS-75 "AN/TPS-75") damaged[\[22\]](#cite_note-128)

*   **Per Iran:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Flag_of_Iran.svg/40px-Flag_of_Iran.svg.png)Iran:

*   *   3,468 people killed[\[o\]](#cite_note-129)
    *   26,500 injured[\[p\]](#cite_note-130)
*   **Per internal sources:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg.png)Hezbollah:
    *   1,000+ fighters killed[\[23\]](#cite_note-131)
    *   ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Flag_of_the_Amal_Movement.svg/20px-Flag_of_the_Amal_Movement.svg.png) Amal Movement:
    *   6 paramedics killed[\[24\]](#cite_note-132)[\[25\]](#cite_note-133)
    *   ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Flag_of_al-Qassam_Brigades.svg/40px-Flag_of_al-Qassam_Brigades.svg.png) Hamas:
    *   3 members killed[\[26\]](#cite_note-134)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/PMF_infobox.png/40px-PMF_infobox.png)Popular Mobilization Forces:
    *   80 fighters killed, 270 injured[\[27\]](#cite_note-135)

* * *

*   **Per [HRANA](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HRANA "HRANA"):**  
    3,636 killed (1,221 military personnel, 1,701 civilians, and 714 unclassified)[\[28\]](#cite_note-136)

* * *

*   **Per US and Israel:**
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Flag_of_Iran.svg/40px-Flag_of_Iran.svg.png)Iran:
    *   6,000+ military personnel killed[\[29\]](#cite_note-Bohbot150326-137)
    *   ~15,000 military personnel wounded[\[29\]](#cite_note-Bohbot150326-137)

    *   155 naval vessels destroyed or damaged[\[31\]](#cite_note-139)[\[q\]](#cite_note-141)
    *    ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Hezbollah_%28thumbnail_placeholder%29.svg.png)Hezbollah:

Saudi Arabia: 3 killed and 23 injured[\[x\]](#cite_note-172)

France: 1 soldier killed[\[y\]](#cite_note-France-177) and 7 injured[\[y\]](#cite_note-France-177)[\[61\]](#cite_note-trt13march-178)

These types of images fail the test of *necessary*. We are also told per [MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE "MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE") that *less is better*.     It could be argued that a collage would be necessary to illustrate the various facets of the war, such as the civilian impact in Iran, the closure of the strait and its consequences for the global economy, the war in Lebanon, etc. However, I do agree that the collage presently used in the sandbox as of writing this does *not* do so and so we would need a different collage or {{[photo montage](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Photo_montage "Template:Photo montage")}} to address the concern about it being necessary in this way.
    
    This would still leave open the issue of a detailed caption bloating the infobox. We could address that by trimming information elsewhere. However, I also understand if other editors feel a casualty list is more important than illustrating the many facets of the war. Per [WP:COLLAGE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:COLLAGE "Wikipedia:COLLAGE"): ... is necessary to illustrate a point in an encyclopedic way - not multiple points or *facets*. Per [MOS:LEADIMAGE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:LEADIMAGE "MOS:LEADIMAGE"): It is common for an article's lead or infobox to carry a representative image—such as of a person or place, a book or album cover—to give readers visual confirmation that they've arrived at the right page. The map alone achieves this. It is not the purpose of the lead image to capture multiple facets of the subject. The type of collage you indicate is a photo essay. [MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE "MOS:INFOBOXPURPOSE") tells us not to try to write the article in the infobox (in full or part) and that *less is better*. The type of collage you indicate is a photo essay. Multiple images crammed into the small frame of an infobox lack visual acuity, create visual noise (clutter) and detracts from the article. @[Cinderella157](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Cinderella157 "User:Cinderella157"): Facets are aspects of a point. The point would be the scale or impact of the war. I suppose the strike map can communicate the scale, to an extent, though it doesn't really capture the full scale. The impact of a war seems like a reasonable point to make to me, and it's something that can't be done with 1 image. You could argue this depends on how narrowly you interpret what counts as a "point". but arguing the semantics doesn't seem very productive. It would be more helpful to consider what point we think the lead image should make, then consider if a collage is needed to make it. Do we want to make the impact of the war the point? It seems like we do, given that much of the infobox (such as the casualty list) seems intended to make this point, and a {{[photo montage](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Photo_montage "Template:Photo montage")}} might communicate this point more effectively than a list of numbers.

While you're right that a map is sufficient to provide visual confirmation that a reader has arrived at the right page, the map does not display in previews when hovering on a link or using the search bar, so it doesn't accomplish the aim as well as an actual image would. I'd also note that the language of [MOS:LEADIMAGE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:LEADIMAGE "MOS:LEADIMAGE") is phrased as it is common not it should or it must. This is more of a description of how lead images are often used, rather than an exhaustive or definitive statement of what they're intended for. I don't think a lead image's only purpose is to provide a visual confirmation that a reader is on the right page.

@[HarvardJock](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:HarvardJock "User:HarvardJock"): Keeping the map where it is and having a collage at the bottom of the infobox is technically feasible, by placing a frameless image in the `|notes=` parameter instead of the map. [WP:P&G](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:P%26G "Wikipedia:P&G") is rarely written in emphatic terms. They are nonetheless standards all users should normally follow. The infobox is not the place to tell a story about the the scale or impact of the war or to illustrate the various facets of the war, such as the civilian impact in Iran, the closure of the strait ... through a photo essay. WP is a written encyclopedia not a picture encyclopedia. INFOBOXPURPOSE tells us that *less is better*. Per [MOS:IMAGEREL](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:IMAGEREL "MOS:IMAGEREL"): too many \[images\] can be distracting and usually, less is more. So, *less is better* goes doubly for images in the lead. We should not get hung up on what the correct WL is. It's a fundamental question of whether the infobox should only directly mention the main belligerents, like in the [World War I](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") infobox (and others, such as [Korean War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War")), or should it try to list everyone, like in the [Kivu conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kivu_conflict "Kivu conflict") infobox (and even that infobox isn't exhaustive, and offers a WL to a [full list](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_armed_groups_in_the_Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "List of armed groups in the Democratic Republic of the Congo")). If the answer is yes, only main belligerents should be directly mentioned then the *others* can handled accordingly, whether it is through a single wikilink, or with a footnote that provides multiple wikilinks, or multiple wikilinks, or multiple footnotes, some combination of these, or something else. Asking what the appropriate WL is, or whether other countries should be in a collapsible list, misses that main point.

The main point is that per [WP:INFOBOXPURPOSE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:INFOBOXPURPOSE "Wikipedia:INFOBOXPURPOSE"), "**An infobox is unsuitable for nuance or detail and should generally avoid prose or prose-like statements. If information cannot be simply stated in an infobox without explanation or qualification, it probably doesn't belong in the infobox.**" The nuance of exactly how much each Persian Gulf country has been affected, whether they host US forces or otherwise allowed the US to use their land, sea, or airspace for combat operations, whether they activated their air defenses, etc. etc. is exactly what needs to be excluded from the infobox. This conflict, the **Iran war**, is primarily between Iran and the Axis of Resistance, and Israel and the United States; the infobox should clearly represent that. Listing a whole bunch of countries whose only claim to fame is that they host US bases and got attacked, despite themselves stating that they want to stay out of the conflict, is useless clutter for an infobox. ## remove as undue "Iran has an "ambitious" nuclear power program"

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: remove as undue \"Iran has an \"ambitious\" nuclear power program\"")\]

This is grasping at straws and beating around the bush in a lead way too crowded and important for it. We should use a concrete evaluation e.g. "There is a consensus among scholars that Iran pursues [nuclear latency](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_latency "Nuclear latency")". [Doeze](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Doeze "User:Doeze") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Doeze "User talk:Doeze")) [20:18, 29 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Doeze-20260429201800-remove_as_undue_"Iran_has_an_"ambitious"_nuclear_power_program" "7 days ago")\[reply\]

I don't necessarily object to this in principle, but to make a case for [WP:UNDUE](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:UNDUE "Wikipedia:UNDUE"), you should explain with sources that the overwhelming amount of scholarly sources state that *"Iran pursues [nuclear latency](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_latency "Nuclear latency")"*, and that the current phrasing describing the "ambitious nuclear power program" is a significant minority opinion, or fringe, in other words. If the vast majority of sources agree with your statement, list them out, and then state the current phrase is fringe because only a source or two mention it. Altnernatively, just [be bold](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:BOLD "Wikipedia:BOLD") and add it in with multiple references, and if a user has issue, they can revert you and we'll continue discussing things here. [**HarvardJock🏫**](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:HarvardJock "User:HarvardJock") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:HarvardJock "User talk:HarvardJock")) [21:40, 29 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-HarvardJock-20260429214000-Doeze-20260429201800 "7 days ago")\[reply\]

These can both be (and, as far as I know, are) true; Iran can both have an ambitious nuclear *power* program while also pursuing a policy of nuclear latency with regards to nuclear *weapons*. The two are not mutually exclusive. I don't think it's controversial to say that Iran has a policy of nuclear latency. As far as I know it's not something that Iran even denies. The main objection would be from those who argue that Iran intends to actively develop nuclear weapons, not merely to maintain nuclear latency, which has been the position of the US and Israel. Regardless of policy, the article [Nuclear latency](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_latency "Nuclear latency") provides multiple references for Iran's nuclear latency in practice, where it states: .mw-parser-output .talkquote-minimal{color:var(--color-subtle,#54595d);border-left:.25em solid var(--border-color-muted,#dadde3);padding:0 1em;margin:0.3em 0 0 0}

> Iran is also considered a nuclear threshold state, with its advanced nuclear program capable of producing fissile material for a bomb in a matter of days if weaponized. \[See [Nuclear latency § Nuclear-threshold states](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_latency#Nuclear-threshold_states "Nuclear latency") for refs.\]

Regardless, the lead does not make it clear why an ambitious nuclear *power* program is even relevant, particularly as *weapons* require much more highly enriched uranium than nuclear *power*, so the latter does't really suggest anything with regards to a country's intentions or capacity with regards to *weapons*. On that, Iran's nuclear power program is relevant to the war in two respects: firstly, it contributes to Iran's nuclear latency, and, secondly, Trump has threatened to attack Iran's energy infrastructure. Neither of these is made clear in the part of the lead in question, though the former seems implied by the context in which it's mentioned.

That all said, the proposed wording wouldn't really make sense as a substitution into the lead to replace the current wording, as it specifically concerns the judgement of the International Atomic Energy Agency. I agree with HarvardJock that the wording there is a consensus among scholars requires very strong referencing; these would have to be references to academic publications ("scholars") not the opinions of journalists. These references would also have to actually state that there is such a consensus explicitly; it would not be sufficient to cite several academic publications that demonstrate the views of individual academics (or particular teams of co-authors), as that would be editorial synthesis ([WP:SYNTH](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:SYNTH "Wikipedia:SYNTH")).

It would much simpler to address the unclear relevance by just cutting Iran has an "ambitious" nuclear power program from the sentence. This would also help to address [§ Summary is too long](#Summary_is_too_long). That would leave: 

> The International Atomic Energy Agency said that, while Iran has refused to allow inspections of its damaged sites after the 2025 war, there was no evidence of an ongoing nuclear weapons program.

Alternatively, if we agree that nuclear latency is important context to include, we could rephrase the paragraph to: 

> Though Iran is considered a nuclear threshold state, the International Atomic Energy Agency said that there was no evidence of an ongoing nuclear weapons program, despite Iran's refusal to allow inspections of its damaged sites after the 2025 war.

The initial addition could reuse the references provided at [nuclear latency](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_latency "Nuclear latency"). – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [23:47, 30 April 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260430234700-HarvardJock-20260429214000 "6 days ago")\[reply\]

Great points here! Thanks for the detailed explanation. Thinking about this issue in detail, you're right the two statements *aren't* in fact in necessary contradiction with one another. No objections to cutting *Iran has an "ambitious" nuclear power program* from the sentence based on how you rationalized it. @[Doeze](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Doeze "User:Doeze") - since you posted about this, would you like to add anything? ## Summary is too long

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Summary is too long")\]

That 250-400 figure was added in 2023 after discussion on the Talk page, so it's probably reasonably up to date.

However, "featured article" isn't synonymous with "long article". Some FAs are quite short, like [Constantine (son of Theophilos)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine_\(son_of_Theophilos\) "Constantine (son of Theophilos)"). Since [2026 Iran war](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war "2026 Iran war") is on the high end of article length, it can also be expected to be on the higher end for lead length as a lead section should still provide a complete summary of the article's content. It would probably be fine to aim for ~500 words.

It may help to compare the current lead with the article's main content to confirm that the lead isn't stating too much new information, but is instead summarising the main content.
