## Iran's "destruction of Israel" rhetoric for a third time

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Iran's \"destruction of Israel\" rhetoric for a third time")\]

Hi [DemFail](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:DemFail "User:DemFail"), can you please explain why you expanded and reworded part of the "Iran's relations with United States with Israel" section without any consensus? Please see [your edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351757085) and [Pachu Kannan](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Pachu_Kannan "User:Pachu Kannan")'s five reverts. [\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351955087), [\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351955946), [\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351956863), [\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351957098), [\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Iran_war&diff=prev&oldid=1351957234). [Achmad Rachmani](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Achmad_Rachmani "User:Achmad Rachmani") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Achmad_Rachmani "User talk:Achmad Rachmani")) [04:51, 1 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Achmad_Rachmani-20260501045100-Iran's_"destruction_of_Israel"_rhetoric_for_a_third_time "6 days ago")\[reply\]

Apologies, did not see that I needed a consensus to make edits to that specific section. The edits I made to the section fall under the following rationale:

**1.** Adding (arguably) important details and links to relevant English Wikipedia articles. The goal was to adjust the current verbiage with additional relevant content while simultaneously pointing readers to already existing, more in-depth articles on the subject(s). Additionally, some of the background is overly vague in its content or awkwardly worded.

Some examples of edits based on that rationale:

\-Adding a link to the [Background and causes of the Iranian Revolution](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Background_and_causes_of_the_Iranian_Revolution "Background and causes of the Iranian Revolution") article when the section was discussing reasons for the revolution. I also added a tidbit about corruption, which is discussed in the article as well.

\-Adding general items of how the US supported Iraq, which can found in the [United States support for Iraq during the Iran–Iraq War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_support_for_Iraq_during_the_Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "United States support for Iraq during the Iran–Iraq War") article.

\-Added a link to the [USS Samuel B. Roberts (FFG-58)](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Samuel_B._Roberts_\(FFG-58\) "USS Samuel B. Roberts (FFG-58)") article to point readers to the specific ship that had been struck; its article includes a more detailed description of the event.

\-Re-rolling of the existing content on Iranian proxies/Axis of Resistance into a "new" paragraph, while making minor additions to the content.

**2.** NPOV: A few statements in this section were arguably not neutral in their verbiage. In my opinion, the sentences that leaned off from being neutral were the sentences regarding Iran's nuclear program and the "Western powers" response, the redundant and less formal sentence on Iran Flight 655 (that deletion has been stayed), and to a lesser extent, the reasons the Iranian government initially became hostile to Israel. The verbiage regarding Iran's nuclear program in this particular section was not neutral by omission of crucial facts. Previous/current verbiage implies it was *only* the "West" who imposed sanctions on Iran, but in reality, [non-Western countries (including China and Russia) also voted to impose sanctions on Iran at multiple UNSC meetings](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sanctions_against_Iran#UN_sanctions_against_Iran "International sanctions against Iran"). As such, I edited the verbiage to correctly state the UNSC and the US separately imposed sanctions on Iran.

As for the "destruction of Israel" rhetoric inclusion debate, based on previous archived discussions and the current verbiage in the section, I believe it should be briefly mentioned with a link to [Destruction of Israel in Iranian discourse](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_relations#Destruction_of_Israel_in_Iranian_policy "Iran–Israel relations"). The current verbiage of "Seeing Israel as an occupier of Palestine" is technically true, but considering the views of the leaders of the then-newly-formed Islamic Republic, that statement comes off as omitting key information/broader context. My original replacement of stating "the desire to destroy Israel for ideological and religious reasons" as a motivation for Iran to break up relations with Israel is both neutral, consistent with other articles' nomenclature, factually correct (albeit admittedly vague), and directs readers to view more thorough content in the Iran-Israel relations article regarding the previously-mentioned Iranian leader ideological and religious views.

I believe the edits I published to the "Iran's relations with United States with Israel" section are fair, but I am open to tweaking of both my originally published edits and the current article verbiage, particularly the "destruction of Israel" inclusion. For the "destruction of Israel" verbiage, perhaps something akin to "Motivated by [anti-imperialism](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-imperialism "Anti-imperialism"), [anti-Zionism](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Zionism "Anti-Zionism"), and [Shia Islamism](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islamism "Shia Islamism"), Iran severed diplomatic ties with Israel and the United States following the revolution, [called for the destruction of Israel](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran-Israel_relations#Destruction_of_Israel_in_Iranian_policy "Iran-Israel relations"), and held the [American embassy staff hostage for over a year](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_hostage_crisis "Iran hostage crisis")" might be more agreeable for inclusion. Let me know your thoughts.

## Should the article be named the "2026 Iran War"?

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Should the article be named the \"2026 Iran War\"?")\]

Conflicts typically have the belligerents in the name. I expect this conflict to be named the "2026 US Israel Iran War". Any objections? [Gaskew7](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Gaskew7&action=edit&redlink=1 "User:Gaskew7 (page does not exist)") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Gaskew7 "User talk:Gaskew7")) [12:18, 2 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Gaskew7-20260502121800-Should_the_article_be_named_the_"2026_Iran_War"? "4 days ago")\[reply\]

Capitalisation has been proposed before and rejected in previous requested moves. Adding the belligerents to the title has also been suggested before. The rationale that conflicts typically have the belligerents in the name is obviously false; many counter examples can be listed. eg. [Vietnam War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"), [Iraq War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), etc. Regardless, while some sources do refer to the war descriptively as the "US-Israel war on Iran", most overwhelmingly refer to it as "the Iran war" or "war on Iran" so a move to include the belligerents is unlikely to succeed. I do not recommend pursuing a requested move unless you have very strong evidence that reliable sources have changed how they refer to the war. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [12:47, 2 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260502124700-Gaskew7-20260502121800 "4 days ago")\[reply\]

\> most overwhelmingly refer to it as "the Iran war"

That is likely more convenient so as to avoid an awkward moment saying the name of an ally in a broadcast.

My objective is different, to minimize or marginally indent the number of broadcasts or presentations where the war is presented as bad things falling out of the sky on Iran. [Gaskew7](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Gaskew7&action=edit&redlink=1 "User:Gaskew7 (page does not exist)") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Gaskew7 "User talk:Gaskew7")) [14:18, 2 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Gaskew7-20260502141800-Scyrme-20260502124700 "4 days ago")\[reply\]

Our job is not to influence what sources say, rather the reverse, Wikipedia follows what the sources say. [331dot](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:331dot "User:331dot") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:331dot "User talk:331dot")) [14:25, 2 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-331dot-20260502142500-Gaskew7-20260502141800 "4 days ago")\[reply\]

While biased journalism is a valid concern and policies like [WP:NDESC](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NDESC "Wikipedia:NDESC") encourage the use of neutral titles, reporting has generally not been shy in naming or implicating the US and Israel in this war so their omission in descriptive references to the war like "the Iran war" aren't likely an intentional attempt at obfuscation. More likely, they're just using "the Iran war" because it's shorter than "the US-Israel war on Iran", and it's obvious from context which war is meant by the former. Personally, I'd prefer they abbreviated it to "the war on Iran" rather than "the Iran war", but, as 331dot has rightly said, it's not appropriate for us to try to intentionally influence what the sources say ([WP:SOAPBOX](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:SOAPBOX "Wikipedia:SOAPBOX")). – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [14:38, 2 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260502143800-Gaskew7-20260502141800 "4 days ago")\[reply\]

## Infobox: economic damages in the "Casualties and losses" section

\[[edit](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Talk:2026_Iran_war&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Infobox: economic damages in the \"Casualties and losses\" section")\]

At some point someone added economic damages to the "casualties and losses" section. I didn't notice until today as the infobox is so overfilled with info that it's difficult to take it all in when scanning over it.

I've removed this information for the same reasons I objected to the proposal to add more of such information at [§ Impact in Gulf states](#Impact_in_Gulf_states), namely that this sort of information isn't usually included in {{[Infobox military conflict](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_military_conflict "Template:Infobox military conflict")}} templates, the infobox is already packed with information, and it would be better to present this information elsewhere, such as a table at [Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_2026_Iran_war "Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war").

The "casualties and losses" section is intended for casualties and military losses, not vague and disputed estimates of economic damages. If we decide to make a exception to the usual use of the section on this article because we feel this is very important to include, this should be discussed first to establish a clear consensus. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [21:14, 4 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260504211400-Infobox:_economic_damages_in_the_"Casualties_and_losses"_section "2 days ago")\[reply\]

I've never actually seen anyone put economic damages data in an infobox. Destroyed equipment is okay for infobox inclusion though, if I'm not mistaken, right? [**HarvardJock🏫**](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:HarvardJock "User:HarvardJock") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:HarvardJock "User talk:HarvardJock")) [00:05, 5 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-HarvardJock-20260505000500-Scyrme-20260504211400 "2 days ago")\[reply\]

It's usually used just for the killed/wounded (eg. [Iraq War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), [Vietnam War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War")), but there are examples including major losses of military equipment too (eg. [Gulf War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War"), [Falklands War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War "Falklands War")) so it's not unheard of. This seems like a natural extension of including other information about the militaries involved, such as leadership or the strength of forces. Though, notably, the [2026 Iran war](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war "2026 Iran war") does not include information about the strength of forces involved, unlike, eg. [Gulf War](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War"), so the lost equipment is presented without the context that would allow a reader to judge whether those losses are impactful.

Economic damages is taking it too far though, in my opinion. Any attempt to calculate the economic losses or damages is by necessity a very rough estimate, and can vary massively depending on what you decide is relevant. Do you try to tally the cost of all damages, including to civilian property? What about the cost of lost opportunities as trade is diverted away from the region; does that count? Or do you only narrowly focus on the expense to taxpayers on the public expenditure for the war effort? The answers depend on the point you're trying to make, so there's no single objectively right answer. There are too many caveats for this sort of thing to be adequately addressed in an infobox summary.

This is all before addressing the problem of repurposing a parameter primarily used to communicate the human cost of a conflict and making it about money. I'm aware that the economic costs come with human costs attached, but this is, again, better addressed elsewhere than the infobox. Just having what's essentially a big price tag in the infobox doesn't do anything to convey that point. All it conveys to a reader is that war is expensive, which is neither appropriate for that section of the infobox nor something that warrants such weight that it must be included in the infobox.

I don't object to including this sort of information elsewhere where it can be better contextualised; it just doesn't belong in the infobox. – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [02:25, 5 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260505022500-HarvardJock-20260505000500 "2 days ago")\[reply\]

I see, thanks for explaining. I agree about the economic damages aspect too, it seems odd to include that in an infobox. Besides, including such information in the infobox opens the floodgates for all kinds of infomation to be included, making it way too long, against established policy and against user concerns. Infobox looks fine as it currently stands, in any case. [**HarvardJock🏫**](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:HarvardJock "User:HarvardJock") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:HarvardJock "User talk:HarvardJock")) [02:40, 5 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-HarvardJock-20260505024000-Scyrme-20260505022500 "2 days ago")\[reply\]

 ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/X_mark.svg/20px-X_mark.svg.png) **Not done** The was a strong consensus for calling this a war and moving the article to this title in the [requested move](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war/Archive_3#Requested_move_2_March_2026 "Talk:2026 Iran war/Archive 3") to the present title. The consensus is unlikely to change as reliable sources overwhelming refer to it as a war. (See also the discussion at [§ War has not been declared by an involved party](#War_has_not_been_declared_by_an_involved_party).) – [Scyrme](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Scyrme "User:Scyrme") ([talk](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_talk:Scyrme "User talk:Scyrme")) [19:39, 6 May 2026 (UTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:2026_Iran_war#c-Scyrme-20260506193900-~2026-27603-87-20260506191900 "11 hours ago")\[reply\]

{{Short description|Ongoing armed conflict in West Asia}} {{Pp-extended|small=yes}} {{Use American spelling|date=March 2026}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Stack begin}} {{2026 Iran war infobox}} {{Campaignbox 2026 Iran war}} {{Campaignbox Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)}} {{Campaignbox Persian Gulf Wars}} {{United States involvement in regime change}} {{Stack end}} Since 28 February 2026, the \[\[United States\]\] and \[\[Israel\]\]<!--This order is established based on sources throughout the article. Do not change without first gaining consensus on the talk page.--> have been engaged in a war with \[\[Iran\]\] and its regional allies. The conflict began when the US and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran, targeting military and government sites and assassinating \[\[List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war|several Iranian officials\]\], \[\[Assassination of Ali Khamenei|including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei\]\]. The surprise attacks were launched during \[\[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations|negotiations between Iran and the US\]\] regarding \[\[Nuclear program of Iran|Iran's nuclear program\]\]. Iran responded with missile and drone \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Israel|strikes on Israel\]\], US bases, and US-allied \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries|Arab countries\]\] in \[\[West Asia\]\]; and the \[\[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis|closure of the Strait of Hormuz\]\], disrupting global trade. After the \[\[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis\]\] began in 2023, Iran and Israel exchanged \[\[2024 Iran–Israel conflict|missile strikes in 2024\]\], and again during the \[\[Twelve-Day War\]\] in June 2025, which resulted in a \[\[2025 United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites|US airstrike on Iranian nuclear sites\]\]. In January 2026, Iranian security forces \[\[2026 Iran massacres|massacred thousands of civilians\]\] in their crackdown on the \[\[2025–2026 Iranian protests|largest Iranian protests\]\] since \[\[Iranian Revolution|1979\]\]. US president \[\[Donald Trump\]\] responded by threatening military action and starting the \[\[2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East|largest US military buildup in the region\]\] since the \[\[2003 invasion of Iraq|2003 US-led invasion of Iraq\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |date=26 February 2026 |title=US-Iran talks end with no deal but potential signs of progress |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-nuclear-talks-resume-geneva-against-backdrop-military-threat-2026-02-26/ |access-date=26 February 2026 |work=\[\[Reuters\]\]}}</ref> Israeli–US airstrikes damaged military bases, government buildings, schools, hospitals, and heritage sites and resulted in \[\[#Civilians|civilian casualties\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |last1=Brown |first1=Paul |last2=Sardarizadeh |first2=Shayan |last3=Murphy |first3=Matt |title=Iranian schools, hospital and landmarks among civilian sites hit during US-Israeli strikes |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cpw004xqxnjo |access-date=6 March 2026 |website=\[\[BBC Verify\]\] |date=6 March 2026}}</ref> In retaliation, Iran launched hundreds of \[\[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|drones\]\] and ballistic missiles at Israel, US military bases in the region, and \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries|at neighbouring Arab countries\]\] including \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain|Bahrain\]\], \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan|Jordan\]\], \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait|Kuwait\]\], \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Oman|Oman\]\], \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar|Qatar\]\], \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia\]\], and the \[\[2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates|United Arab In 1988, \[\[USS Samuel B. Roberts (FFG-58)#1988\_deployment\_and\_mine\_strike|a US warship was struck by an Iranian mine\]\]; the US responded by \[\[Operation Praying Mantis|attacking Iran's navy\]\]. A few months later, the US mistakenly shot down a \[\[Iran Air Flight 655|civilian Iranian flight\]\].<ref name="MacFarquhar1926">{{#invoke:cite |news |last1=MacFarquhar |first1=Neil |title=A Timeline of the Tensions Between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the U.S. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/15/world/middleeast/united-states-iran-history.html |access-date=19 March 2026 |work=\[\[The New York Times\]\] |date=15 March 2026}}</ref> Iran started a ballistic missile program to deter Iraqi \[\[War of the Cities|missile attacks on Iranian cities\]\] and to compensate for its lack of a modern air force due to sanctions.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |title=Iran unveils new solid-fueled ballistic missile, state TV reports |url=https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-israel-ballistic-missile-dd4500eaf8553f6375eab10a884dabd2 |access-date=28 March 2026 |work=Associated Press |date=4 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Al-MarashiCon">{{#invoke:cite |web |last=Al-Marashi |first=Ibrahim |date=2 March 2026 |title=Iran and the US have been at war for decades – and there's no end in sight |url=https://theconversation.com/iran-and-the-us-have-been-at-war-for-decades-and-theres-no-end-in-sight-277284 |access-date=4 March 2026 |website=\[\[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation\]\] |language=en}}</ref> Starting in the 1980s, Iran began engaging in \[\[proxy conflicts\]\] throughout the Middle East. Iran backed \[\[Hezbollah\]\] in Lebanon against Israel during and after the \[\[Lebanese Civil War\]\]. During the \[\[Iraq War\]\], Iran supported militias fighting the US in Iraq. Along with the \[\[Houthis\]\] in \[\[Yemen\]\] and other groups in Syria and Palestine, these proxy groups became part of the informal '\[\[Axis of Resistance\]\]' committed to countering American, Israeli, Saudi, and Emirati influence in the region. In 2002, Iran's covert expansion of its nuclear program was first revealed. Beginning in 2006, the \[\[United Nations Security Council\]\] responded with \[\[International sanctions against Iran#UN\_sanctions\_against\_Iran|a series of sanctions against Iran\]\], with the US imposing \[\[United States sanctions against Iran|its own series of sanctions against Iran\]\]. The US and Israel conducted \[\[Operation Olympic Games|a campaign of cyberwarfare\]\] against Iranian nuclear facilities to disrupt their operations, while Israel \[\[Assassinations of Iranian nuclear scientists|assassinated several top Iranian nuclear scientists\]\].<ref name="MacFarquhar1926"/><ref name="Le Monde Assassinations">{{cite web |last1=Imbert |last2=Golshiri |last3=Mas |first1=Louis |first2=Ghazal |first3=Liselotte |title=How Israel tracked down and assassinated scientists involved in Iran's nuclear program |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2025/07/08/how-israel-tracked-down-and-assassinated-scientists-involved-in-iran-s-nuclear-program\_6743166\_4.html |website=lemonde.fr |publisher=Le Monde |access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref> The conflict escalated in January 2020 when President Trump ordered the \[\[assassination of Qasem Soleimani\]\], the commander of the \[\[Quds Force\]\].<ref name="News1828"/><ref name="Al-MarashiCon"/> Tensions escalated following the \[\[October 7 attacks\]\] on Israel and the start of the \[\[Gaza war\]\]. In June 2025, Israel launched the \[\[Twelve-Day War\]\] by attacking Iranian military and nuclear facilities, provoking Iranian counter-strikes. The US also \[\[United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites|struck Iranian nuclear facilities\]\] during the Twelve-Day War, which ended in a \[\[Twelve-Day War ceasefire|ceasefire\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |title=Iran's Conflict With Israel and the United States |url=https://www.cfr.org/global-conflict-tracker/conflict/confrontation-between-united-states-and-iran |website=\[\[Council on Foreign Relations\]\]}}</ref> In early 2026, Israeli Prime Minister \[\[Benjamin Netanyahu\]\] lobbied President Donald Trump for a joint military strike on Iran, specifically targeting its leadership.<ref>{{cite news | last1=Swan | first1=Jonathan | last2=Haberman | first2=Maggie | title=How Trump Took the U.S. to War With Iran | work=The New York Times | date=7 April 2026 | issn=0362-4331 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/07/us/politics/trump-iran-war.html | language=en-US | page=}}</ref> Following high-level meetings in February, Trump authorized "Operation Epic Fury", with reports citing \[\[Israeli intelligence community|Israeli intelligence\]\] provided by Netanyahu as a decisive factor in the decision.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Banco |first1=Erin |last2=Slattery |first2=Gram |last3=Lubell |first3=Maayan |title=Exclusive: Trump approved Iran operation after Netanyahu argued for joint killing of Khamenei, sources say |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-approved-iran-operation-after-netanyahu-argued-joint-killing-khamenei-2026-03-23/ |work=Reuters |date=24 March 2026}}</ref> ===Iran nuclear issue=== {{Further|Iran and weapons of mass destruction#Nuclear weapons}} {{See also|Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons#Iran}} Iran suspended its \[\[AMAD Project\]\] pursuant to \[\[Ali Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons\]\] in 2003. IT caused Iran to believe that strikes were not imminent. Thus, groups of senior Iranian officials continued gathering in person. These gatherings were targeted in initial strikes. One part of the deception was information about a US F-22 deployment leaked to hide that preparations were more advanced at other bases.<ref name="Estrin-2026">{{Cite news |last=Estrin |first=Daniel |date=11 March 2026 |title=Old-school tricks and AI tech are weapons in the Iran war |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/10/nx-s1-5741726/israel-iran-war-cyber-ai |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Avraham-2026">{{Cite web |last1=Avraham |first1=Yaron |last2=Davori |first2=Nir |last3=Segal |first3=Amit |date=28 February 2026 |script-title=he:30 בכירים איראנים הותקפו בחצי דקה, חלקם הותקפו במקום המסתור |title=30 bekirim iranim hutakfu bechtzi dka, halkam hutakfu bemekum hamistor |trans-title=30 Iranian senior officials attacked in half a minute, after Israeli deception: New details from the opening strike |url=https://www.mako.co.il/news-military/2026\_q1/Article-df96fd26975ac91026.htm |access-date=1 March 2026 |website=N12 |language=he}}</ref> Calls between Trump and Netanyahu before the war were not publicised to diminish the possibility of an Iranian first strike.<ref name="Avraham-2026" /> \[\[IDF Spokesperson's Unit|IDF Spokesperson\]\] Brigadier General \[\[Effie Defrin\]\] stated that months of joint US and Israeli "strategic and operational deception" of satellite imagery led up to the war. This encompassed planes and other facilities. The night of the initial strike he and \[\[Chief of the General Staff (Israel)|IDF Chief of Staff\]\] Lieutenant General \[\[Eyal Zamir\]\] took their official cars home from \[\[HaKirya|IDF Headquarters\]\].<ref name="Estrin-2026" /> They came back without them so that satellite imagery would show that their base did not appear full nor warplanes appear armed and ready.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Eichner |first=Itamar |date=28 February 2026 |title=How Israel pulled off a second surprise against Iran |url=https://www.ynetnews.com/article/rko5i2ef11l |access-date=9 April 2026 |work=\[\[Ynet\]\] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Levin |first=Hani |date=28 February 2026 |title=כך הורדמה טהרן: מבצע ההטעיה המתוחכם שסלל את הדרך לתקיפה - בחדרי חרדים |trans-title=This is how Tehran was lulled to sleep: the sophisticated deception operation that paved the way for the attack. |url=https://www.bhol.co.il/news/1720329 |access-date=12 April 2026 |website=Bhol |language=he |trans-quote=The deception operation revealed: What secret moves caused Iranian intelligence to look away at the crucial moment, and how did Israeli-American cooperation create a false image of routine at IDF Headquarters? 2026}}</ref> |} == Direct impacts == === Iran === {{main|Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran}} ==== Leadership ==== {{see also|2026 Iranian supreme leader election}} {{#invoke:multiple image| | image1 = Masoud Pezeshkian 2025 (cropped).jpg | image2 = Gholam Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i 2023 (Cropped).jpg | image3 = Alireza Arafi 13990824 0146818 crop.jpg | perrow = 3 | footer = The three members of the \[\[Interim Leadership Council\]\]{{snd}}President \[\[Masoud Pezeshkian\]\], Chief Justice \[\[Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i\]\] and Ayatollah \[\[Alireza Arafi\]\] | total\_width = 260 }} The death of Ali Khamenei triggered an election for a new supreme leader. Under the terms of Iran's constitution, an \[\[Interim Leadership Council\]\] was established on 1 March to exercise the functions of Iran's \[\[head of state\]\] until a new supreme leader is elected.<ref name="Reuters-2026"/> \[\[Mojtaba Khamenei\]\] was elected on 8 March 2026 to replace his father as supreme leader,<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Tondo |first=Lorenzo |date=8 March 2026 |title=Ali Khamenei's son Mojtaba chosen as Iran's new supreme leader |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/08/ali-khameneis-son-mojtaba-chosen-as-irans-new-supreme-leader |access-date=8 March 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> and the IRGC, as well as Iran's top leaders, including \[\[Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf\]\], \[\[Ali Larijani\]\], and \[\[Masoud Pezeshkian\]\],<ref name="Sabah-2026">{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Sabah |first=Zaid |date=9 March 2026 |title=Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei to replace his father as supreme leader |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/3/9/iran-war-live-mojtaba-khamenei-named-supreme-leader-israel-bombs-tehran |access-date=9 March 2026 |work=\[\[Al Jazeera English\]\] |language=en}}</ref> pledged their allegiance to him.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Kelliher |first=Fiona |date=8 March 2026 |title='Act of defiance': Iran picks Khamenei's son to lead as US-Israel attack |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/3/8/iran-live-israel-bombs-tehran-oil-depots-attacks-on-gulf-states-continue |access-date=8 March 2026 |work=\[\[Al Jazeera English\]\] |language=en}}</ref> In late March, the NYT described Iran's leadership as paralyzed with severely disrupted decision-making process. It also reported that the damage to communications infrastructure caused paranoia and internal power struggles.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |title=Iran's leadership is struggling to function and facing mounting internal disarray - report |url=https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/middle-east/iran-eastern-states/artc-iran-s-leadership-is-struggling-to-function-and-facing-mounting-internal-disarray-report |access-date=2 April 2026 |work=i24NEWS |date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> ==== Civilian life ==== {{see also|2025–2026 Iranian protests#After the strikes}} \[\[File:Tehran - The Fourth Day of War 4 Avash.webp|thumb|Residents in Tehran on the third day of US-Israeli airstrikes, 3 March 2026\]\] According to UN Human Rights Chief \[\[Volker Türk\]\], the "reckless" war is disproportionately impacting civilians in the Middle East and beyond.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |date=19 March 2026 |title=Civilians bear brunt of reckless war in the Middle East, says Türk |url=https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2026/03/civilians-bear-brunt-reckless-war-middle-east-says-turk |website=\[\[OHCHR\]\] |language=en}}</ref> 138,000 civilian sites in Iran were damaged during the conflict, with estimated time of reconstruction being 2 to 5 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramazanian |first=Ali |date=24 April 2026 |title=بازسازی ویرانه‌های جنگ در ایران چگونه پیش می‌رود؟ |script-title= |trans-title=How is the reconstruction of war ruins progressing in Iran? |url=https://www.bbc.com/persian/articles/cz0evpdrzxro |access-date=26 April 2026 |website=BBC News فارسی |language=fa}}</ref> As the US and Israel executed joint strikes targeting Iranian military and institutional targets, Iran's capital reportedly became a \[\[ghost town\]\], as civilians feared going outside or to their daily jobs.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |date=3 March 2026 |title=Bombardment unleashes terror in Tehran with no sign of protests |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/bombardment-unleashes-terror-tehran-with-no-sign-protests-2026-03-03 |work=\[\[Reuters\]\]}}</ref> Reports have emerged that prisoners in \[\[Evin Prison\]\] have been receiving limited bread and water since the onset of the war.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |date=4 March 2026 |title=Families say food distribution disrupted in Evin wards after strikes in Tehran |url=https://www.iranintl.com/en/202603043283 |access-date=5 March 2026 |website=\[\[Iran International\]\] |language=en}}</ref> After the strikes, schools were ordered closed while banks and government offices remained in operation at reduced capacity. Local media reported that subway and bus services would remain operational.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |date=28 February 2026 |title=Streets empty and shops close as US strikes confirm Iranian fears country's \[\[2025–2026 hunger crisis in Afghanistan|severe humanitarian crisis\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last1=Peltier |first1=Elian |title=Caught Between Two Conflicts, Afghans Flee Iran |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/23/world/asia/iran-afghanistan-border-refugees.html |work=\[\[The New York Times\]\] |date=23 March 2026}}</ref> Arafat Jamal, the UNHCR Representative in ==== Cultural heritage sites ==== {{Main|Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran War}} Multiple historic and cultural sites, including \[\[UNESCO World Heritage Sites\]\], were damaged during the war. The most affected was \[\[Chehel Sotoun\]\] and its rich ''\[\[ayeneh-kari\]\]''.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Babaie |first1=Sussan |title=In a month of war, Iran's cultural heritage has suffered huge damage |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/01/in-just-a-few-weeks-irans-cultural-heritage-has-suffered-huge-damage |work=The Art Newspaper - International art news and events |date=1 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref> On 2 March, a strike on \[\[Arg Square\]\] damaged nearby \[\[Golestan Palace\]\], prompting \[\[UNESCO\]\] to issue a statement of concern.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Charles |first=Starr |date=5 March 2026 |title=US-Israeli airstrike damages UNESCO-listed palace in Tehran |url=https://www.dezeen.com/2026/03/05/golestan-palace-damaged-unesco-world-heritage/ |access-date=10 March, the \[\[Azadi Sport Complex\]\] was bombed.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Zirin |first=Dave |author-link=Dave Zirin |date=11 March 2026 |title=The Bombing of Iran's Azadi Stadium Is Straight An 8 March strike on \[\[Falak-ol-Aflak\]\], which was marked with a \[\[Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict|blue shield emblem\]\], damaged several sections of the site.<ref name = "ArtNewspaper310"/> Strikes on \[\[Isfahan\]\] on 9 March damaged \[\[Naqsh-e Jahan Square\]\], Chehel Sotoun, \[\[Ali Qapu\]\], the \[\[Shah Mosque (Isfahan)|Shah Mosque\]\], \[\[Jameh Mosque of Isfahan|Jameh Mosque\]\], and \[\[Natural History Museum of Isfahan|Teymouri Hall\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Fassihi |first=Farnaz |date=11 March 2026 |title=World Heritage Sites Hit in Airstrikes on Iran |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/11/world/middleeast/iran-heritage-sites-damaged.html |access-date=12 March 2026 |work=\[\[The New York damaged by US-Israel strikes |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/03/10/unesco-sites-in-iranian-city-of-isfahan-and-others-across-countrydamaged-by-us-israel-strikes |access-date=10 March 2026 |website=The Art Newspaper |language=en}}</ref> On 11 March, UNESCO urged protection for Iran's \[\[heritage sites\]\] and World Heritage Sites that have been damaged or are under high risk due to the war, alongside other \[\[historic site\]\]s in Israel, Lebanon, and across the Middle East.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |date=11 March 2026 |title=UNESCO raises concern over damage to Iran's heritage sites amid war, urges protection |url=https://www.trtworld.com/article/68e9ee629824 |access-date=12 March 2026 |work=\[\[TRT World\]\] |language=en}}</ref> === Israel === Israel declared a nationwide \[\[state of emergency\]\], saying that the strikes on Iran were the largest that it had ever launched.<ref name="Liebermann-2026"/><ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |date=1 March 2026 |title=Israeli army says air raids on Iran largest ever in air forces history |url=https://www.lbcgroup.tv/news/middleeastnews/908321/lbci-lebanon-articles/en |access-date=28 February 2026 |website=LBCIV7 |language=en}}</ref> Israeli schools and workspaces were closed and public gatherings were canceled.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last1=Boxerman |first1=Aaron |last2=Pager |first2=Tyler |last3=Fassihi |first3=Farnaz |last4=Bergman |first4=Ronen |date=28 February 2026 |title=U.S.-Led Strike on Iran: Live Updates as Trump Calls for Government Overthrow |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/02/28/world/iran-strikes-trump |access-date=28 February 2026 |work=\[\[The New York Times\]\] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/LDjEo |archive-date=1 March 2026}}</ref> In the 40 days from the start of the war through the \[\[2026 Iran war ceasefire|8 April ceasefire\]\], there were a total of 650 missile attacks from Iran to Israel, the majority of which carried cluster munitions. About 16 of the missiles that made it past Israeli missile defenses carried conventional warheads, while 50 had cluster munitions. The attacks killed a total of 24 people, all of them civilians, and resulted in more than 7,000 injuries. Of the 24 civilians killed, 14 were struck by warheads with conventional explosive warheads and 10 were victims of cluster submunitions; two of the deaths were inside a sheltered space, with the other fatalities being people in unprotected areas.<ref>Fabian, Emanuel. \[https://www.timesofisrael.com/650-iranian-missiles-fired-24-killed-and-10800-israeli-strikes-the-war-in-numbers/ "The war in numbers: 650 Iranian missiles fired; 24 killed in Israel, West Bank; 10,800 Israeli strikes"\], ''\[\[The Times of Israel\]\]'', 10 April 2026. Accessed 29 April 2026. "With a ceasefire in Iran taking effect early Wednesday morning, the full scope of the Israeli-American 40-day campaign against the Islamic Republic began to emerge.... Iran, during the fighting, launched some 650 ballistic missiles at Israel. According to the military, more than half of the missiles carried cluster bomb warheads, which spread bomblets indiscriminately over wide areas. The missile attacks killed 20 Israeli civilians and foreign nationals in Israel, along with four Palestinians in the West Bank.... In all, at least 16 missiles carrying conventional warheads — with hundreds of kilograms of explosives — struck populated areas in Israel, causing extensive damage. There were also some 50 incidents of missiles carrying cluster bomb warheads hitting populated areas, with hundreds of separate impact sites.... All 24 fatalities from Iran’s missile attacks were civilians, and all but two were not inside bomb shelters. Cluster munitions killed 10, and conventional missiles killed 14."</ref> === Palestine === {{See also|Gaza war}} The Israeli \[\[Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories\]\] closed multiple aid crossings in the \[\[Gaza Strip\]\], specifically interrupting free circulation on the \[\[Egypt–Gaza border\]\].<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |date=1 March 2026 |title=Israel closes Gaza's Rafah crossing amid attacks on Iran |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/1/israel-closes-gazas-rafah-crossing-amid-attacks-on-iran |work=\[\[Al Jazeera English\]\] |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref> Israeli forces suspended \[\[United Nations\]\] humanitarian movements and postponed planned rotations of international humanitarian staff, including medical evacuations and the return of people into Gaza, which the \[\[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs\]\] condemned.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |date=2 March 2026 |title=Today's top news: Middle East, Occupied Palestinian Territory, Sudan |url=https://www.unocha.org/news/todays-top-news-middle-east-occupied-palestinian-territory-sudan |access-date=3 March 2026 |website=\[\[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs\]\] |language=en}}</ref> \[\[Israeli settler violence\]\] against \[\[Palestinians\]\] in \[\[occupied West Bank\]\] has increased; settlers have taken advantage of curbs on movement imposed during the renewed \[\[Israeli state of emergency\]\]. The renewed blocking of West Bank roads in the context of the \[\[2026 Lebanon war\]\] has delayed medics from assisting injured Palestinians.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |date=11 March 2026 |title=Israeli Settler Violence Rises in West Bank Under Iran War Curbs |url=https://english.aawsat.com/node/5250010 |access-date=11 March 2026 |website=Asharq Al-Awsat |language=en}}</ref> The EU March 2026 |website=\[\[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express\]\] |language=en}}</ref> March threats by \[\[Houthis|Houthi\]\] leader \[\[Abdul-Malik al-Houthi\]\] had not stopped Red Sea traffic as of mid-April, although traffic remained under historic levels after crashing in 2024 as a result of Houthi attacks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 March 2026 |title=Potential Houthi threat to Red Sea shipping could further damage global economy |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwyvd5z1xjno |access-date=16 April 2026 |work=\[\[BBC News\]\] |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 15 March, the ''\[\[Associated Press\]\]'' reported that the weapons stockpile of the Houthis was running low from repeated attacks on Israel, while Iran had not been able to resupply them, because of the war.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |last=Khaled |first=Fatma |date=15 March 2026 |title=As other Iran‑allied groups are engaging in the Mideast war, Yemen's Houthis hold back |url=https://apnews.com/article/yemen-houthis-iran-war-gulf-us-israel-1fc2a646d0cc42131385e7e61c409565 |access-date=19 March 2026 |work=\[\[Associated Press\]\]}}</ref><ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/as-irans-other-proxy-groups-join-war-houthi-rebels-in-yemen-hold-back-for-now/ |access-date=19 March 2026 |work=\[\[The Times of Israel\]\]}}</ref> === Internet infrastructure === {{Further|Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war}} Three \[\[Amazon Web Services\]\] data centers in the United Arab Emirates were struck and damaged as a result of \[\[drone strikes\]\], leading to outages of web infrastructure within the Middle East,<ref>{{#invoke:cite |web |last=Gault |first=Matthew |date=2 March 2026 |title=Amazon Data Centers on Fire After Iranian Missile Strikes on Dubai |url=https://www.404media.co/amazon-data-centers-on-fire-after-iranian-missile-strikes-on-dubai/ |access-date=3 March 2026 |website=\[\[404 Media\]\] |language=en}}</ref> causing "sparks and fire" as well as "major structural damage" for 2 of the centers, with internal water levels reaching up to {{Val|4|u=cm}}, worsened by the failure of cooling and air systems. Fundamental web infrastructure including \[\[Amazon S3|S3 storage\]\], \[\[Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud|EC2 compute\]\] and \[\[Amazon DynamoDB|DynamoDB databases\]\] suffered complete outages in early March.<ref>{{#invoke:cite |news |first1=Eugene |last1=Kim |first2=Lee Chong |last2=Ming |date=3 March 2026 |title=Amazon says 3 data centers were damaged by drone strikes in the Middle East |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/amazon-data-centers-middle-east-drone-strukes-us-iran-conflict-2026-3 |access-date=3 March 2026 |work=\[\[Business Insider\]\] |language=en-US}}</ref> Iran shut down Internet access for its people throughout the war.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Down |first=Aisha |date=6 April 2026 |title=Iran's internet blackout is longest national shutdown since Arab spring |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/apr/06/iran-internet-blackout-is-longest-national-shutdown-since-arab-spring |access-date=16 April 2026 |work=\[\[The Guardian\]\] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Users who took the potentially fatal risk of smuggling \[\[Starlink\]\] terminals into the country \[\[2026 Internet blackout in Iran|retained some access\]\]. === Military millions of dollars a day': US counts cost of war on Iran |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/world/middle-east/2026/04/07/hundreds-of-millions-of-dollars-a-day-us-counts-equipment-cost-of-iran-war/ |access-date=16 April 2026 |newspaper=\[\[The Irish Times\]\] |language=en}}</ref> Israeli costs were estimated at $11{{nbsp}}billion.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 April 2026 |title=Iran war has cost Israel $11.5{{nbsp}}billion in budgetary expenses, ministry says |url=https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/04/12/iran-war-has-cost-israel-115-billion-in-budgetary-expenses-ministry-says |access-date=16 April 2026 |work=\[\[Al Arabiya English\]\] |language=en}}</ref> Costs to the Iranian economy were estimated at $40-50{{nbsp}}billion, around 10% of \[\[Gross domestic product|GDP\]\].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shearing |first=Neal |date=17 March 2026 |title=How will the Iran war affect the global economy? |url=https://www.chathamhouse.org/2026/03/how-will-iran-war-affect-global-economy |access-date=16 April 2026 |website=\[\[Chatham House\]\] |language=en}}</ref> The monetary costs of Iranian attacks name="ndtv10march" /> == Reactions == {{Further|Reactions to the 2026 Iran war|Protests against the 2026 Iran war}} === Iran === {{Excerpt|Reactions to the 2026 Iran war|Government|paragraphs=1-3}} ==== Media coverage ==== =====Background===== Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and \[\[2025–2026 Iranian protests|domestic unrest in Iran\]\]. Iranian state media, such as the \[\[IRNA\]\], portrayed these developments as provocations.<ref name="Brookings Institute-03032026">{{cite web |date=3 March 2026 |title=After the strike: The danger of war in Iran |url=https://www.brookings.edu/articles/after-the-strike-the-danger-of-war-in-iran |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=Brookings Institution}}</ref> ===== Disinformation and propaganda ===== \[\[File:Explosive Media L O S E R.webm|thumb|right|150px|\[\[Lego\]\]-style \[\[propaganda\]\] animation produced by Iranian media company \[\[Explosive Media\]\] using \[\[text-to-video model\]\]ing. \]\] Iranian state-controlled outlets have been described as employing propaganda techniques, including the use of \[\[AI-generated video\]\]s (such as those produced by \[\[Explosive Media\]\]) and inflated casualty figures.<ref>{{cite news |date=6 March 2026 |title=AI-generated Iran war videos surge as creators use new tech to cash in |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckg8wvz427vo |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=BBC}}</ref> Trump has accused Iran of using artificial intelligence as a "disinformation weapon."<ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Trump accuses Iran of using AI to spread disinformation |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/trump-accuses-iran-using-ai-spread-disinformation-2026-03-16/ |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref> Iranian media broadcast manipulated images of alleged victories, prompting fact-checking from organizations like \[\[NewsGuard\]\].<ref name="CNN-05032026">{{cite web |date=5 March 2026 |title=White House posts video of operations in Iran mixed with 'Call of Duty' footage |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/05/world/video/iran-war-propaganda-call-of-duty-stelter-nc-digvid |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=CNN}}</ref> The Iranian government responded to the \[\[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration\]\]'s use of video game clips, cartoon characters, and blockbuster movie scenes for Iran messaging with an AI-generated \[\[propaganda video\]\] mimicking \[\[Brickfilm|Lego animation\]\], produced by the Revayat-e-Fath Institute and redistributed on various government-run outlets, including redistribution by the \[\[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs\]\]. The video declares itself in remembrance of the \[\[Minab school attack\]\] and showcases Iran attacking various of its neighbours and American-Israeli outposts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 March 2026|title=Truth or Fake - Iran trolls Trump with AI-generated LEGO propaganda video|url=https://www.france24.com/en/iran-trolls-trump-with-ai-generated-lego-propaganda-video|access-date=16 March 2026|website=France 24|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Coen|first=Susie|date=10 March 2026|title=Iran creates propaganda video using Lego-like models|url=https://www.thetimes.com/world/middle-east/article/iran-propaganda-video-lego-like-models-vn8p3jq3b|access-date=16 March 2026|website=www.thetimes.com|language=en|archive-date=11 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311170902/https://www.thetimes.com/world/middle-east/article/iran-propaganda-video-lego-like-models-vn8p3jq3b|url-status=live}}</ref> Rumors that Israeli Prime Minister \[\[Benjamin Netanyahu\]\] had been killed in Iranian attacks were circulating widely on social media and were amplified by Iranian state-controlled outlets.<ref name="i24NEWS-16032026">{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Is Benjamin Netanyahu Dead? Fake News Becomes The Loudest Voice On Social Media |url=https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/israel/diplomacy-defense/artc-is-benjamin-netanyahu-dead-fake-news-becomes-the-loudest-voice-on-social-media |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260315221436/https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/israel/diplomacy-defense/artc-is-benjamin-netanyahu-dead-fake-news-becomes-the-loudest-voice-on-social-media |archive-date=15 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=i24NEWS}}</ref><ref name="CTV News-15032026">{{cite news |date=15 March 2026 |title=Netanyahu posts video in response to Iran rumors that he is dead |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/netanyahu-posts-video-in-response-to-iran-rumors-that-he-is-dead/ |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=CTV News}}</ref> Users claimed that footage of Netanyahu speaking at a press conference on 13 March 2026 was AI-generated, citing alleged anomalies such as a “sixth finger.”<ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Benjamin Netanyahu Death Rumours: Israeli PM Netanyahu's Coffee Video Under Scrutiny, Grok Calls It 'Deepfake' |url=https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/benjamin-netanyahu-death-rumours-israeli-pm-netanyahus-new-video-under-scrutiny-grok-calls-it-deepfake-11221132 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316070254/https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/benjamin-netanyahu-death-rumours-israeli-pm-netanyahus-new-video-under-scrutiny-grok-calls-it-deepfake-11221132 |archive-date=16 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=NDTV}}</ref> ===== Impact ===== Coverage of the war strained journalistic resources, with reports of targeted attacks on media infrastructure.<ref>{{cite web |date=5 March 2026 |title="Why Are We Going to War?": Former U.S. Middle East Officials Say Trump Has "No Clear Plan" on Iran |url=https://www.democracynow.org/2026/3/5/iran\_state\_defense |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=Democracy Now!}}</ref> === Israel === {{Excerpt|Reactions to the 2026 Iran war#Israel}} ==== Media coverage ==== =====Background===== Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and reports of Iranian domestic unrest. Outlets such as \[\[CNN\]\] and ''\[\[The New York Times\]\]'' detailed US military buildups in the region, speculating about possible attacks.<ref name="CNN-02032026">{{cite web |date=2 March 2026 |title=What we know about the widening US war with Iran |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/02/middleeast/us-israel-iran-conflict-what-we-know-intl |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=CNN}}</ref> Israeli broadcasters focused on the threats posed by Iranian proxies such as \[\[Hezbollah\]\].<ref name="Brookings Institute-03032026" /> ===== Disinformation and propaganda ===== Rumors that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had been killed in Iranian attacks were circulating widely on social media and were amplified by Iranian state-controlled outlets.<ref name="i24NEWS-16032026" /><ref name="CTV News-15032026" /> Netanyahu responded by posting several videos, including one filmed in a Jerusalem cafe in which he sarcastically declared that he was "dying for coffee" while holding up a cappuccino and holding up his hands to show that he had five fingers.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Watch: Netanyahu shares another video as 'death' rumours refuse to die down |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/watch-netanyahu-shares-another-video-as-death-rumours-refuse-to-die-down/articleshow/129610220.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316132007/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/watch-netanyahu-shares-another-video-as-death-rumours-refuse-to-die-down/articleshow/129610220.cms |archive-date=16 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=The Times of India}}</ref> The cafe video itself quickly became the subject of fresh rumors, with some social media users and commentators claiming that it too was AI-generated or a \[\[deepfake\]\]. The cafe later released images as evidence that Netanyahu had visited.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Cafe shares proof after Grok calls Netanyahu's coffee shop video 'deepfake' |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/netanyahu-dead-rumours-after-grok-labels-video-as-deepfake-cafe-releases-photos-of-alive-netanyahu-getting-coffee-101773639441412.html |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=Benjamin Netanyahu 'coffee' video amid dead rumours is 'AI generated'? Netizens troll Israel PM, Tel Aviv cafe shares proof |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/world/report-benjamin-netanyahu-coffee-video-amid-dead-rumours-is-ai-generated-netizens-trolls-israel-pm-tel-aviv-cafe-shares-proof-3203365 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=DNA India}}</ref> === United States === {{Excerpt|Reactions to the 2026 Iran war#United States}} ==== Media coverage ==== =====Background===== Before hostilities erupted, media attention on US-Iran tensions increased in early 2026, following failed nuclear talks and reports of Iranian domestic unrest. Outlets such as \[\[CNN\]\] and ''\[\[The New York Times\]\]'' detailed US military buildups in the region, speculating about possible attacks.<ref name="CNN-02032026" /> As the airstrikes began, initial reporting relied heavily on satellite imagery and official briefings. The Pentagon's announcements of the destruction of Iranian assets were widely echoed, but independent verification proved difficult due to Tehran's communications restrictions.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 March 2026 |title=Seven days on, seven questions about the US-Israeli war on Iran |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/07/seven-questions-about-iran-war |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> ===== Disinformation and propaganda ===== The White House faced backlash over a video that mixed real war footage with video game clips.<ref name="CNN-05032026" /> Critics said such efforts distorted public understanding.<ref name="Mondoweiss-04032026">{{cite web |date=4 March 2026 |title=Lies, distortions, and propaganda: how the U.S. mainstream media coverage on Iran hides the truth |url=https://mondoweiss.net/2026/03/lies-distortions-and-propaganda-how-the-u-s-mainstream-media-coverage-on-iran-hides-the-truth |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260306195307/https://mondoweiss.net/2026/03/lies-distortions-and-propaganda-how-the-u-s-mainstream-media-coverage-on-iran-hides-the-truth/ |archive-date=6 March 2026 |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=Mondoweiss}}</ref> \[\[Use of copyrighted works by the second Trump administration|The Trump administration's use\]\] of \[\[copyrighted\]\] video game clips, cartoon characters, and blockbuster movie scenes for Iran messaging risked turning war into entertainment and a spectacle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Leila |date=19 March 2026 |title=White House's use of internet memes to promote Iran war sparks criticism |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/white-houses-use-of-internet-memes-to-promote-iran-war-sparks-criticism |access-date=28 March 2026 |website=PBS News |language=en-us}}</ref> The White House circulates videos fusing real airstrike footages with visuals from video games and action movies, "transforming acts of destruction into a spectacle of national triumph", keeping the audience detached from the human suffering it produces.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Giroux |first1=Henry A. |author1-link=Henry Giroux |date=21 March 2026 |title=War Becomes Spectacle in Trump's Horrific Propaganda Promoting War in Iran |url=https://truthout.org/articles/war-becomes-spectacle-in-trumps-horrific-propaganda-promoting-war-in-iran/ |work=\[\[Truthout\]\]}}</ref> A video from the White House drew widespread criticism and bewilderment. Another clip used \[\[Kesha\]\]'s song "\[\[Blow (Kesha song)|Blow\]\]" under the footage of an airstrike, which prompted the singer to protest against the "perverts".<ref>{{cite news |date=6 March 2026 |title=White House glorifies Iran strikes with Hollywood & anime: 'Justice the American way' sparks outrage |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/white-house-glorifies-iran-strikes-with-hollywood-anime-justice-the-american-way-sparks-outrage/articleshow/129162686.cms |work=The Times of India}}</ref> \[\[Blase Cupich\]\], an American \[\[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|Catholic Cardinal\]\] who is close with \[\[Pope Leo XIV\]\], referred to a video released by the White House of attacks on Iran mixed with Hollywood film clips as "horrifying" and "sickening".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kelliher |first1=Fiona |last2=Regencia |first2=Ted |last3=Pietromarchi |first3=Virginia |last4=Milisic |first4=Alma |last5=Magee |first5=Caolán |date=8 March 2026 |title=Iran war updates: New supreme leader named; 2 killed in Saudi Arabia strike |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/3/8/iran-live-israel-bombs-tehran-oil-depots-attacks-on-gulf-states-continue |access-date=9 March 2026 |website=Al Jazeera English |language=en}}</ref> ===== United States media and government ===== On 14 March 2026, \[\[Federal Communications Commission\]\] Chairman \[\[Brendan Carr\]\], a Trump appointee, warned broadcasters that those who "perpetrate fake news and distort the news" must "take the right course" or risk losing their licenses at renewal.<ref>{{cite news |date=14 March 2026 |title=FCC chair threatens to throttle news broadcasts over 'hoaxes' about Iran war |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/14/fcc-broadcast-permits-iran-war-news |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=16 March 2026 |title=FCC chair threatens broadcasters' licenses over negative coverage of the war in Iran |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/16/nx-s1-5748570/fcc-chair-threatens-broadcasters-licenses-over-negative-coverage-of-the-war-in-iran |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316085309/https://www.npr.org/2026/03/16/nx-s1-5748570/fcc-chair-threatens-broadcasters-licenses-over-negative-coverage-of-the-war-in-iran |archive-date=16 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=NPR}}</ref> Carr said broadcasters "must act in the public interest, and if they don't, they will lose their licenses," citing the public's low trust in legacy media and past election coverage problems. Trump expressed that he was "enthusiastic" about Carr's stance.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 March 2026 |title=Trump says he's 'thrilled' to see Brendan Carr looking at FCC licenses |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5785553-trump-thrilled-fcc-broadcast-licenses/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316160708/https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5785553-trump-thrilled-fcc-broadcast-licenses/ |archive-date=16 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=The Hill}}</ref> Defense Secretary \[\[Pete Hegseth\]\] also criticized the coverage during a news conference, taking issue with CNN's reporting and suggesting emphasizing Iranian frustration rather than adding to the headlines.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 March 2026 |title=Trump officials target media over Iran war reporting |url=https://www.axios.com/2026/03/15/iran-war-trump-media-threats-fcc-hegseth-carr |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=Axios}}</ref> \[\[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic\]\] lawmakers condemned the FCC's remarks as unconstitutional censorship, with many calling it "oppressive" and a violation of the First Amendment.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 March 2026 |title=Democrats blast FCC Chair Carr's broadcast license threats as anti-First Amendment, 'totalitarian' |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/15/trump-iran-war-fcc-carr-broadcast-license.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260315230525/https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/15/trump-iran-war-fcc-carr-broadcast-license.html |archive-date=15 March 2026 |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=CNBC}}</ref> ===== Impact ===== Coverage of the war influenced public opinion, with the US public showing mixed support amid economic concerns.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 March 2026 |title=One week into the Iran war, the fallout is global |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/07/nx-s1-5739242/iran-war-oil-trump-israel-spain-economy-one-week |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=NPR}}</ref>{{outdated inline|date=April 2026}} ===== Criticism ===== Analysts accused Western media of failing to challenge the official narrative, with \[\[Mondoweiss\]\] highlighting the flattering language that downplayed civilian casualties.<ref name="Mondoweiss-04032026" /> \[\[Al Jazeera\]\] noted the overrepresentation of voices from the pro-war \[\[Iranian diaspora\]\].<ref name="Al Jazeera English-07032026">{{cite web |date=7 March 2026 |title=Trump-Netanyahu's 'war in search of a strategy' |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/video/the-listening-post/2026/3/7/trump-netanyahus-war-in-search-of-a-strategy |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=Al Jazeera English}}</ref> Pre-war coverage was also marred by inadequate public warnings.<ref>{{cite web |date=19 February 2026 |title=The US news media is failing the public in its coverage of a possible war against Iran |url=https://presswatchers.org/2026/02/the-news-media-is-failing-the-public-in-its-coverage-of-a-possible-war-against-iran |access-date=7 March 2026 |website=Press Watch}}</ref> === International ===
